  • Display or otherwise use the Khan Academy Trademarks in a manner likely to lead others to believe that you are in any way associated with, endorsed by, or affiliated with Khan Academy.
  • Stretch, distort, alter, rearrange, recolor, combine, or otherwise manipulate Khan Academy design logos or the KHAN ACADEMY® wordmark.
  • In any way state or imply that Khan Academy produces, endorses, or supports you or any of your products or services.
  • Display any Khan Academy Trademarks in connection with your own trademarks.
  • Use Khan Academy trademarks in the naming or promotion of an app or other services, nor may organizations combine their brands with Khan Academy to create a new brand (e.g., “Khan EduCo Academy”). Instead, use the following language: “Viewer for Khan Academy”. This makes it clear that the offering is not from nor supported by Khan Academy.

Permitted Use of Materials

  • An organization may provide a link to the www.khanacademy.org site or a page starting with www.khanacademy.org.
  • An organization may also embed a video into a site, provided they comply with our content usage policies.
  • Usage of materials must adhere to our Creative Commons (CC-by-NC-SA) Licensing and Terms of Service, in particular, the attribution and non-commercial clauses. Attribution: Per our license, you must attribute the material to Khan Academy, but not in any way that suggests that Khan Academy directly endorses you or your use of the materials. Please include a link to www.khanacademy.org and the following verbiage:

“Note: All Khan Academy content is available for free at www.khanacademy.org”.

In addition, where Khan Academy materials are incorporated into a service that requires login for the service, the notification must be provided prior to login that all Khan Academy materials are available for free at www.khanacademy.org.

Non-commercial: Khan Academy defines “non-commercial” as any use that is not directly intended to generate sales or profits or any other commercial advantage for the user. Here are a few examples:

  • Advertisements on a website are considered commercial. It is also considered commercial for a third party to use Khan Academy in advertising or marketing for their services or products.
  • The use of our content by a for-profit corporation for internal professional development and/or training of its employees is “non-commercial” as long as that corporation does not charge its employees for such use.
  • The use of our content by an organization that is incorporating it into a paid offering is NOT “non-commercial.”
  • For mobile apps or other similar use cases, the title and/or description should clearly indicate it is unofficial; if there is a “contact us” section, the developer(s) should be listed for technical issues.

Prohibited Use of Materials

You agree not to link or embed Khan Academy’s site or materials in any manner such that the site or materials are “framed,” surrounded, or obfuscated by any third-party content, materials, or branding (e.g., banner ads or putting Khan Academy materials behind a paid login wall is commercial). We may require that any link to or embedding of Khan Academy materials be discontinued and may revoke your right to link to the sites from any other website at any time.

What’s allowed and not allowed under Khan Academy’s Terms of Service?

We want Khan Academy to be a safe, respectful, and productive learning environment for everyone. This policy outlines behavior that is or isn’t allowed on our site, in accordance with our Website Terms of Service.

This article outlines Khan Academy’s Prohibited Conduct and comprises guidelines for use of our Service under our Website Terms of Service. It applies to all users. Any capitalized terms used and not defined in this Guideline have the meanings given to them in the Website Terms of Service.

1. Use Khan Academy for learning—not for commercial purposes

Khan Academy is a nonprofit organization offering free learning tools and resources. You may only use our Services for personal, non-commercial use, as outlined in our Terms of Service.

Do:

  • Use Khan Academy to learn, practice, and explore new subjects

  • Share your learning with others

  • Use our free resources to teach or tutor

  • Tell others about Khan Academy Don’t:

  • Use our content as part of a business or paid service without permission

  • Reproduce, sell, or copy our materials commercially

  • Display ads, send spam, or use our platform for promotions

  • Replicate Khan Academy’s features or use its data to build similar services

  • Break any laws (especially those related to intellectual property or data privacy)

2. Help keep the community respectful and safe

We’re a global community of learners. That means everyone (regardless of age, background, or identity) should feel supported here.

Do:

  • Follow our Community Guidelines when posting or interacting with the platform

  • Be respectful in discussions and forums, and stay on topic

  • Use learning tools (including AI features) with academic honesty

  • Protect your own privacy and respect others’

  • Report any issues you encounter through the Help Center Don’t:

  • Use Khan Academy to cheat or encourage academic dishonesty

  • Impersonate others or mislead users

  • Access someone else’s account without permission

  • Collect or misuse personal data

  • Use language or behavior that could be seen as offensive, harmful, or inappropriate, especially in the context of a community with many young learners We will take action to protect our site and learners from any conduct that misleads, harms, or disrespects others.

3. Share content responsibly

When posting or creating content (including AI-generated content) remember this is a learning space for a general audience. Content that’s misleading, inappropriate, or harmful to others isn’t allowed.

Do:

  • Share content that’s appropriate for an all-ages learning environment

  • Take responsibility for how your content might affect others

  • Make it clear when content was created using AI tools Don’t share:

  • Discriminatory, hateful, or violent content

  • Content that harasses, bullies, or threatens anyone

  • Pornographic or sexually explicit content

  • Defamatory or privacy-invading messages

  • Political or religious materials

  • Misinformation, or anything that’s false, misleading, or harmful Content should support learning—not distract or harm.

4. Respect copyright and ownership

Khan Academy’s lessons, tools, and exercises are developed by educators and designers to support learners around the world. Please use them responsibly.

Do:

  • Use our resources for learning and teaching

  • Keep any credit or attribution notices intact when sharing Khan Academy content Don’t:

  • Sell, sublicense, or commercially distribute our materials (unless permitted in our Terms of Service)

  • Modify our content or create derivative works unless explicitly allowed

  • Use scraping tools, bots, or other tech to copy or extract data from our site

  • Use Khan Academy content or data to train, test, or develop AI models or machine learning tools Using our content fairly helps keep Khan Academy free and available to all.

5. Help protect our platform

We work hard to keep Khan Academy secure, reliable, and accessible to learners every day.

Do:

  • Use Khan Academy through our website, apps, or supported educational platforms

  • Report bugs and technical issues via the Help Center Don’t:

  • Attempt to bypass or disable security features or content protections

  • Reverse engineer or attempt to access Khan Academy’s source code

  • Upload malware, spyware, or other harmful software

  • Create fake or automated accounts (e.g., bots)

  • Disrupt our platform through denial-of-service attacks, AI jailbreaking, or prompt injection

  • Attempt to access non-public areas of the site or system Actions that interfere with how Khan Academy works negatively affects learning for everyone.

If something goes wrong

If we believe a user is violating this policy or our Terms of Service, we may:

  • Remove content
  • Restrict access or features
  • Take other actions to protect our community and platform Our goal is always to keep Khan Academy safe, respectful, and focused on learning.

Why does Khan Academy process my personal data?

Overview

This article analyzes the legal bases on which Khan Academy generally relies when processing personal data of individual customers.

Data privacy laws in many jurisdictions require organizations acting as data controllers to identify a valid legal basis before carrying out any processing of personal data. For example, under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), data controllers may rely on six lawful bases for processing personal data:

  • contractual necessity (processing required to provide our services under our Terms of Service, a school services contract or other contract)
  • legal obligation (processing required by law)
  • vital interests (life-or-death situations)
  • public tasks (public interest or official authority)
  • legitimate interests (controller’s interests balanced against data subject rights)
  • consent (affirmative agreement for specific purposes) Many countries, including the UK, use the GDPR framework or a substantially similar framework under their local privacy laws.

GDPR Framework

The table below sets out the legal basis generally relied on by Khan Academy for each processing purpose, in accordance with the GDPR framework. In many cases, more than one basis is available, depending on the specific context of the processing, the relationship with the individual customer, and applicable regulatory requirements in jurisdictions whose data protection frameworks differ from, or only partially align with, the GDPR. In cases where legitimate interests serve as the basis of our processing, we conduct an assessment to weigh Khan Academy’s legitimate interests against our customer’s individual privacy rights and interests.

The categories of data described in the table are further detailed in the “Collection of Information” section of our privacy policy.

Purpose

Category of Data

GDPR Legal Basis

To provide our Service. Khan Academy uses your information to operate, maintain, and provide all of the features of our Services.

  • Account ownership and contact information, such as user name and email address

  • Information from Single Sign On (SSO) authentication services;

  • Information obtained from a school, or from other users, that is required to establish an account or enroll in a program, including class roster data

  • Learning activity associated with your account

  • Usage and device information

  • Necessary to provide our services or otherwise perform a contract. To personalize your experience. We use your information to personalize your experience while using the Service, including on various devices you may use to access the Service. For instance, Khan Academy remembers your recent activity so we can recommend the most appropriate content for you and provide personalized learning experiences.

  • Information about your use of our platform, including learning activity and associated insights

  • General location information

  • Usage and device information

  • Necessary to provide our services or otherwise perform a contract. Personalization is inherent in the learning experience we deliver.

  • Our legitimate interests to personalize your experience. To communicate with you about your account. We use your information to communicate with you about your account and respond to your inquiries. We may also communicate with you to let you know about account features and help you get the most of your account.

  • Email address

  • Information about your use of our Service, such as videos watched or skills attained

  • Your communications with us, including support requests

  • Necessary to provide our services or otherwise perform a contract. Certain communications are a core part of our Service.

  • Our legitimate interests to inform you about our Services, respond to and, where necessary, investigate your inquiries about the Services. To communicate with you about our services and our mission. We may use your information to communicate with you about our mission and fundraising for our mission.

  • Email address

  • Information about your use of our Service, such as using videos watched or skills attained to suggest additional learning activities you may be interested in

  • Donation information

  • Our legitimate interest in communicating with you regarding our mission and philanthropic fundraising, including your prior support.

  • Your consent. To enable the customer’s participation in Khan Academy partnership arrangements. We use your information to enable you to participate in programs or features we may offer in partnership with third parties, to the extent you decide to participate in such programs.

  • Email address

  • User type (student vs parent or teacher, grade level)

  • Information we collect to enable your participation in special programs or features

  • Information provided by partners and other sources

  • Necessary to provide our services or otherwise perform a contract.

  • Your consent. To understand, improve, and develop our Service. Khan Academy uses information to understand and analyze the usage trends, learning behaviors, and preferences of our users, to improve the way the Service works and looks, and to create new features and functionality. In most cases, we use de-identified, anonymized or aggregate information for these purposes.

  • Information about your use of our Service, such as videos watched, features used or other learning activities you engage in

  • Usage and device information

  • Your communications with us

  • Feedback you may provide to us

  • Our legitimate interests in improving our Service.

  • Your consent. To develop new educational offerings. We may use information to maintain, develop, support and improve our Service and other educational products and services, and for educational research. In most cases, we use de-identified, anonymized or aggregate data for this purpose.

  • Information about your use of our Service, such as videos watched, features used or other learning activities you engage in;

  • Usage and device information

  • Your communications with us

  • Feedback you may provide to us

  • Our legitimate interests in developing our Service.

  • Your consent. For legal, compliance or safety reasons. We may use or share information to comply with applicable laws, rules, or regulations, and our Terms of Service, including protecting the safety and rights of Khan Academy, users, and the general public.

  • Your contact and account owner information and account and account usage data, to the extent necessary for such purposes

  • Necessary for a legal obligation, including maintenance of financial and compliance records

  • Our legitimate interests to maintain the safety and security of our platform and defend against legal claims. Global application

While the legal basis framework established under the GDPR has influenced privacy legislation worldwide, there is no uniform global standard. Some countries use different terminology to describe what is essentially the same legal basis; others do not require a legal basis at all or impose more restrictive requirements, including a greater reliance on consent and the exclusion of certain bases, such as legitimate interest.

If you reside in a country outside the US and EU, we will process personal data according to the legal basis requirements of the country in which you habitually reside. In most cases the basis of processing will follow similar principles as set forth in the GDPR table above. When the specific legal bases vary from the GDPR (e.g., Brazil’s LGPD, India’s DPDP Act), the following general principles apply:

  • In countries where one of the bases available under the GDPR is not recognized, we rely on alternate available bases under the relevant applicable law.
  • We are generally able to provide our core educational services under Khan Academy’s Terms of Service in reliance on bases relating to contractual necessity or equivalent concepts.
  • When we offer supplemental programs or activities beyond our core educational services, we may rely on other available bases of processing, obtain your explicit consent, or we may refrain from providing that program or activity if no lawful basis exists.
  • We limit our use of data for ancillary uses (such as analytics and product development) to uses for which a lawful basis exists, or limit our use to aggregate, anonymized or de-identified data.
  • We limit marketing activities to those permitted under applicable law, including by obtaining explicit consent if required, or we may refrain from marketing activities. You can opt out of communications and marketing activities that are not part of the core service. School Services

Khan Academy offers structured educational programs to schools and educational institutions in select countries outside the United States, principally through our subsidiary in Brazil and other partner entities such as our “KhanX” partners (independent nonprofit organizations authorized to provide school programs in select countries). In cases where we support institutional use in formal school programs, we process student data at the direction of the school customer, as the data controller, as provided under our services contract with the school or partner entity. We will process data as necessary to provide our services under the school contract and to support programs and activities requested or approved by the school. The school or other educational institution is responsible for obtaining any parent or guardian consent required to process the data of minor students, and for informing parents about processing of student data and as required under applicable law and our Terms of Service.

Automated Decision-Making

Khan Academy’s AI-enabled features are used solely for informative and educational purposes, with use by students and children under the supervision of a teacher, parent or other responsible adult. These tools are not intended to be used to make decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects on data subjects. While our AI-Enabled learning solutions include features that provide AI-powered feedback to learners and educators, consequential decisions regarding educational progress are made by the teacher or other supervising adult in the broader context of overall student performance.

AI-enabled features are not offered in all jurisdictions or to all types of users. AI-enabled features for students are available outside the United States only though school partnerships in select jurisdictions.

You should see this screen:

Issues with Exercises

How do I enter math symbols in an exercise?

Hello, brilliant learners! We’ve got some tips to make your math journey smoother when completing math exercises. Let’s dive into using our math keypad and LaTeX commands.

The Math Keypad

When using the math keypad, note that it changes based on the exercise, showing only the symbols you need.

On desktop computers:

Spot a button near the exercise input? Click it to reveal or hide the math keypad.

On Mobile:

For math inputs, a special keypad pops up automatically.

Keep in mind: Using the math palatte is a slightly different experience when in a test or quiz vs when using it with Khanmigo.

LaTeX: Your Math Typing Tool

Some exercises have a special keypad for math symbols. But sometimes, you’ll need to type them. That’s where LaTeX comes in handy. Here are some common LaTeX commands:

Multiplication: Use an asterisk (). E.g., “34”

Division: Use a slash (/). E.g., “3/4”. For operations in the numerator or denominator, use parentheses. E.g., “12/(5n)” or “(n+3)/6”

Square root: Type “sqrt(x)”. E.g., “sqrt(3)”

Pi: Type “pi”

Theta (θ): Type “theta”

Powers or exponents: Use a caret (^). E.g., “4^5”

Fractional exponents: Use a caret (^) and type the fraction in parentheses. E.g., “x^(1/3)”

Greater than or equal to: Type “>=”

Less than or equal to: Type “<=”

Logarithms: For base 10, enter “log(x)”. For natural logarithms, enter “ln(x)”

Logarithms with other bases: Enter as “log_b(n)”, where b is the base and n is the number

There are many more LaTeX commands to explore. Keep learning, keep growing!

How do I report a mistake or issue with an exercise?

If a question within a set of practice exercises, a quiz, a unit test, or a course challenge isn’t working correctly, it’s best to notify our Khan Academy Content team using the Report a problem link in its lower right-hand corner.

This allows the Content team to see exactly which question you were working on and what steps you took when trying to solve it.

If the issue isn’t specific to that one particular question, please submit a support request through the Help Center describing the steps you took and provide screenshots if possible.

Why am I getting the problem wrong when entering the correct answer?

There are two main reasons a correct answer may not be accepted in an exercise (even if it appears to be the same answer given in the hints):

  • The answer entered isn’t really the same as the answer in the hints.
  • The answer in the hints is incorrect. The first issue is related to formatting your answer, so double-check this article to make sure the answer entered matches the formatting. This article deals with the second issue, though.

Problems like this should be reported using the Report a problem link on the lower right of the exercise page after checking that your answer is correct.

Why did I get the problem wrong when entering the correct math expression?

When working on math exercises that involve entering an expression, students occasionally report that they cannot enter a correct expression, even though the answer they’ve entered is the one shown in the hints. (We assume they’ll look through the hints when an answer is unknown or marked as incorrect.)

There are three reasons this situation might arise:

  • The answer entered isn’t really the same as the answer in the hints.
  • It isn’t obvious how to enter the answer in the hints. The appearance of square brackets ([ ]) is the most common cause of this instance of the problem.
  • The answer in the hints is incorrect.

First case

In the first case, for example, a hint might show that the correct answer is:

When the user enters “1/2p”, the answer is marked as incorrect. What’s up?

The answer is in the order of operations. Remember PEMDAS? The expression as entered is equivalent to “1/2×p”. So it will evaluate “1/2”, then multiply the result by “p”. “1/2” times “p” is the same as “p/2”. That is not the same as the correct answer specified in the hints.

To fix this, use parentheses! If you enter “1/(2p)”, the evaluator has no choice but to use “2p” as the denominator, as shown in the hint. Use parentheses to show the evaluator which part of the problem to evaluate first.

Second case

The second case involves the use of brackets. For example, a hint may display the correct answer with brackets (shown below).

However, if you try to enter the answer with brackets, the problem says there are more parts to the problem. Replace the brackets with parentheses and your answer will be accepted.

Third case

The third case is when there is an error with the hints or the question itself. Please follow the instructions in this article: Why am I getting the problem wrong when entering the correct answer?

Issues with Videos

How do I report mistakes in videos?

We sometimes receive reports of errors in videos that have already been corrected with a small text box in the lower right-hand corner.

Here’s what a video with correction looks like:

Image caption: A screenshot of a video titled Olfaction: structure and function. The video screenshot shows a drawing of the sinus cavity and its structures. In the lower right corner of the video screenshot, there is a pink arrow pointing to the correction text box, which identifies and corrects a spelling error in a label on the sinus cavity drawing.

Corrections are not visible in full-screen mode. Please watch the videos in small-screen mode first, so you can see if corrections have already been made.

If there is a correction, take notes in small-screen mode first so that you can consult your notes if you watch in full-screen mode later. In a class setting, you can then stop the video at the appropriate moment and explain it.

If you would like to report a new clarification for an error in a video, please follow these steps:

  • Begin typing in the Ask a question text box under the video or article.
  • Look for the Report a mistake link to the right and click it.
  • Clicking this will bring up a new text box below Mistakes.
  • When you begin typing in this box, directions about how to provide the best feedback will appear above the box.
  • You can visit this article for more information about the steps listed above and helpful screenshots. The feedback you provide will go directly to the content team and they’ll review it for accuracy. Thank you for helping to improve Khan Academy!

Note: The option to report an error is only available on the website, not in the Khan Academy app.

Why are Khan Academy videos not playing for me?

If Khan Academy videos aren’t playing for you, there are a few common causes and options for troubleshooting:

  • Check your bandwidth. Check that your internet connection is working and can handle streaming videos. Most Khan Academy videos require less bandwidth than live-action content, but we still suggest 1.5 Mbps bandwidth per device playing a standard-definition video.
  • Make sure your browser is up-to-date. Check that you are using a web browser supported by Khan Academy and that it is updated to its latest version.
  • International Problems: YouTube is currently blocked in China and Iran. However, you may be able to watch our videos in China on the Khan Academy website instead of YouTube, as Khan Academy uses a different video player to play our instructional videos. If you’re in Iran, you may be able to access Kolibri (previously known as KA Lite) rather than our full site. If none of the above steps resolve your video playback issues, please report the problem with a description of the steps you took (and screenshots, if possible!).

Javacript and the Web

Can I write ProcessingJS programs inside the webpage environment?

Yes, you can write ProcessingJS programs inside our webpage environment. This is something you may want to do if you’re adding buttons, input fields, or other interactive elements using HTML tags.

Here’s a template that shows how to do that, plus an article that describes the differences between the code that will work inside the ProcessingJS environment versus the webpage environment.

Generally, it is best to use the dedicated ProcessingJS environment to develop ProcessingJS programs, since we provide special error checking and other code helpers just for ProcessingJS.

One approach is to develop your programs in the ProcessingJS environment first and then move them over to the webpage environment.

How can I report a problem in Computer Programming - Javascript and the Web?

Please first look through the Computer Programming FAQ and the Khan Academy Help Center to see if we have a suggestion for your problem there.

If you’re having a problem with a challenge not accepting your code, showing a confusing message, or if you’re not sure how to proceed to complete the challenge or project, you can access the Study Group Community and post your questions. It’s a great opportunity to reach out to a global circle of learners and teachers who are always happy to help! (This can only be done by users who are 13+ years old).

Besides posting your questions on the Study Group, you can click on Report a problem on the right-hand side of the Hint. That will go into a dedicated system for challenge grader reports that will capture your code as well.

If you identify that your problem is an actual bug or glitch, please use the Report a problem button in the Help Center and send a Help request describing the steps you took and provide screenshots if possible.

How do I program webpages and ProcessingJS programs offline or outside of KA?

For webpages:

  • You can paste your HTML into a file, save it as “some_name.html” and open it in your web browser.

  • For more details, read the article on Developing Webpages outside Khan Academy. For ProcessingJS programs:

  • You can make a webpage, including the ProcessingJS library in it, and put your program code in it, and open it in a browser. Try using the template here to get started.

  • Note there are differences between our version of ProcessingJS and the linked version.

  • For more details, read the article on Using ProcessingJS outside Khan Academy.

What resources (images, scripts, etc.) can I bring into webpages that I make on Khan Academy?

We restrict the resources that user-created webpages can bring in for security and moderation reasons. Specifically:

  • Webpages can bring in images from Khan Academy static servers, and Wikipedia. The webpages should attribute images properly, like using CC licenses for Wikipedia images.
  • Webpages can bring in CSS and font files from Google Web Fonts and Twitter Bootstrap.
  • Webpages can bring in sounds/videos from Khan Academy static servers.
  • Webpages can bring in JavaScript files from rawgit.com, Google hosted libraries, and cdnJS. The resources must all come in over SSL, so the URLs should start with https://. Remember to check your developer console for errors if you’re having trouble bringing in any of those resources.

What’s the difference between “==” and “===” operator?

When programming in JavaScript, you’ll need to compare variables sometimes. To do so, you can use the operators “==” and “===,” they will tell you if the outcome of the comparison is true or false. Even though these operators look very similar, they differ when comparing the variables’ elements:

  • ==: compares the value of the variables
  • ===: compares the type and value of the variables For example, 5 === “5” will return a false result. Even though the value of both variables is the same, their type is not; one of them is a String (“5”), and the other one is an Integer (5).

On the other hand, 5 == “5” will return a true result. Both variables have the same value; therefore, the result will be true.

When do I use a for loop and when do I use a while loop in the JavaScript challenges?

All for loops can be written as while loops, and vice-versa. Just use whichever loop seems more appropriate to the task at hand.

In general, you should use a for loop when you know how many times the loop should run. If you want the loop to break based on a condition other than the number of times it runs, you should use a while loop.

Which parts of ProcessingJS does Khan Academy support?

In our Drawing & Animation curriculum, we use the open source ProcessingJS library to do the drawing and animation.

Here are the differences between the ProcessingJS reference and what we support:

  • We do not support the Java-like syntax changes to JS, like void, class, extends, and super.
  • We use degrees by default for all angle parameters, instead of radians. Use angleMode to change to radians.
  • We use mouseIsPressed instead of mousePressed for the boolean because it is less confusing to have both a function and a boolean with the same name. Similarly, we use keyIsPressed instead of keyPressed.
  • We only support loading officially supported images and sounds via getImage() and getSound(), for moderation reasons.
  • We do not support all PImage manipulation functionality, for performance reasons.
  • We do not support all commands that are not specifically mentioned in the Documentation. As long as a ProcessingJS Reference command is not among the forbidden ones for moderation reasons or performance reasons and it works, you can use it on Khan Academy. However, if a ProcessingJS Reference command does not work or works erratically, we do not consider it a bug unless it is specifically mentioned in the Documentation.

Click here to see the documentation of the supported ProcessingJS items. You can also find this documentation available in one of the tabs below the programs you work on.

Why do I need variables in a JavaScript program? Isn’t it easier to just type the number?

Variables introduce an element of change into your program. By using variables, you can store data, make animations, create games, etc. Variables are also useful for maintaining your code. By creating a variable, you can easily change a value which is used in many places throughout your code.

Why does Oh Noes keep popping up when I’m writing my program?

If Oh Noes appears, it means you made a mistake. Check your code for spelling and syntax errors. Look for missing semicolons. Remember: JavaScript is case-sensitive. If you think you’ve fixed all the bugs in your code and Oh Noes is still appearing, try restarting the program.

Is the Khan Academy app for Windows supported?

The Windows app is no longer supported by Khan Academy. If this is keeping you from using Khan Academy effectively, please try the following:

  • Access Khan Academy through a browser on your desktop, laptop, or mobile device. Keep in mind that Khan Academy works best on Google Chrome.
  • Download the Khan Academy app for your iOS device.
  • Download the Khan Academy app for your Android device.

What Android and iOS versions does the Khan Academy app support?

We aim to provide a quality learning experience for as many people as we can. Our small team does its best to support older operating systems (OS), especially if there are large numbers of learners on those older versions, or if we anticipate that learners’ devices aren’t compatible with newer OS updates.

However, every additional OS version means that weird bugs can appear, and it increases the number and variety of bugs that we have to watch out for. By removing support for older operating systems that are infrequently used by our user community, we free up our small team to improve the overall quality and build new features.

To provide our users with the best experience at Khan Academy, the Khan Academy app supports:

  • Android 9.0 (Pie) and newer
  • iOS 15 and newer Nonetheless, if your device’s OS cannot be updated to a newer version, you can try to continue enjoying the full Khan Academy experience! To do so, access the Khan Academy website through your device’s browser. To know which browsers we support, check out this article.

Note: Older operating systems could make our website behave oddly, as they may not support all the features available on it.

Khan Academy Programming Challenge Council

How do I apply to the KACP Challenge Council?

Application Process

  • Send in your application via the KACP Challenge Council Application
  • Due to the volume of applications, we unfortunately won’t be able to personally respond to each applicant.
  • The current cohort for 2020 has been selected, and our next evaluation is planned for the end of the year.

Requirements for Challenge Council Members

  • Creativity and passion for promoting learning computer programming!
    • Brainstorming contest ideas for KACP learners of all levels is going to take a lot of thinking outside the box. You’ll be regularly coming up with engaging, challenging, and rewarding projects for community members to work on.
  • Consistent contributions to the KACP section in the form of answering questions, contributing to discussions, and completing project evaluations.
    • Council members need to be highly familiar with the KACP platform and community and have experience supporting the community.
  • Availability to meet with other Council members to create and carry out contest launches every other month.
    • Creating contests will take a bit of time, and it’s important that Council members be available to connect with each other in order to create fun, well thought-out contests that will benefit the whole KACP community.
  • A record free of any bans or repeated bad behavior, such as plagiarism, vote soliciting, or spamming for at least six months.
    • Council members should be aware of what constitutes good behavior according to KA guidelines so they can set a good example for others and demonstrate good judgement when helping the community.

What is the KACP Challenge Council?

The Challenge Council consists of a small team of active members of the Khan Academy Computer Programming (KACP) community that works together to develop contests for KACP over the course of a year. Members have gone through the application process and been accepted by KA staff.

The Council creates one contest every 2 months for the KACP community, handles the judging of the projects submitted, and announces 9 winners (3 per category) each contest. As a group, the Challenge Council is responsible for the following:

  • create 6 contests a year that will engage and challenge the KACP community;
  • create a set of fair and equitable standards for judging contest entries;
  • ensure that the contests are geared towards learners of different skill and experience levels throughout the year; and
  • maintain respectful communication and interactions with KA community, including fellow Council members, to create a supportive community environment and set a good example for other KACP learners.

Requirements for Challenge Council Members

  • Creativity and passion for promoting learning computer programming!
    • Brainstorming contest ideas for KACP learners of all levels is going to take a lot of thinking outside the box. You’ll be regularly coming up with engaging, challenging, and rewarding projects for community members to work on.
  • Consistent contributions to the KACP section in the form of answering questions, contributing to discussions, and completing project evaluations.
    • Council members need to be highly familiar with the KACP platform and community and have experience supporting the community.
  • Availability to meet with other Council members to create and carry out contest launches every two months.
    • Creating contests will take a bit of time, and it’s important that Council members be available to connect with each other in order to create fun, well thought-out contests that will benefit the whole KACP community.
  • A record free of any bans or repeated bad behavior, such as plagiarism, vote soliciting, or spamming for at least six months.
    • Council members should be aware of what constitutes good behavior according to KA guidelines so they can set a good example for others and demonstrate good judgement when helping the community.

Khan Academy Reimagined for Students

How can I go back to the classic Khan Academy experience as an independent learner?

Khan Academy has been reimagined for teachers and their students! We are thrilled to offer these updates to ensure a more streamlined and engaging learning experience. Below we have some resources if you’d prefer to experience the platform as an independent learner, outside of the classroom experience.

This article will cover:

  • Why you are seeing the updated reimagined Khan Academy experience
  • How to tell if you are enrolled in classes
  • How to stay in your classes, but access the features as an independent learner
  • How to transition your account from being enrolled in classes, to being an independent learner instead

Why am I seeing the reimagined Khan Academy experience?

The following account types will see the reimagined Khan Academy experience:

  • Accounts with the teacher role enabled (this includes combo Parent + Teacher accounts)
  • Accounts which have gone through the teacher onboarding.
  • -If you are seeing the teacher onboarding page, but don’t know why check out this article!
  • Students who are enrolled in a Khan Academy class .
  • Any account rostered with Khan Academy Districts .

How can I tell if I am enrolled in classes?

  • You will see the reimagined Khan Academy experience upon login. Here’s what it looks like!
  • You also can visit khanacademy.org and if it says “My classes” on the lefthand side, you are enrolled in the class listed there.

If you need to stay in your Khan Academy classes for your school or teacher, but want to still see the independent learner experience:

  • Visit: khanacademy.org
  • This page will take you to the classic Khan Academy experience, where you can continue learning independently and access features such as:
    • Badges
    • Energy points
    • Avatars
    • The classic learner profile
  • Note: Clicking on a class title will take you back to the reimagined experience. Keep the khanacademy.org URL handy!

If you would like to transition your account to be an independent learner (aka leave your classes):

  • Visit khanacademy.org
  • Click “Remove” next to the teachers of the classes you are enrolled in
  • Click “Remove” on the confirmation popup.
  • NOTE: as this popup says, clicking “Remove” will delete all your assignment data and grades. So if you are still in school, check with your teacher(s) before you click this! If you are having trouble with this process, or have additional questions about your account, please contact the Khan Academy Support Team. We are here and happy to help!

What’s changing for students on the reimagined Khan Academy?

Khan Academy is being reimagined for classrooms to create a more guided, engaging learning experience for students. As mentioned in this blog post, these updates were piloted in schools and designed with feedback from teachers and students to help learners stay focused, motivated, and on track toward Mastery.

This article highlights the key changes for students in the Khan Academy reimagined experience and what teachers should know as they prepare their classrooms for the transition. Once your teacher account transitions to the new experience, you can also use the student preview functionality to play around with the student side as well.

These changes apply for students who are in a classroom on Khan Academy. Independent learners who are not in a classroom, will continue with the current experience.

  • If you’d like more info about what’s changing for teachers, check out this article.
  • If you are an administrator, check out this article for how to prepare your school(s) for the switch.

What is staying the same?

Before diving into what’s changing, we want to reassure teachers and students that many of the core learning experiences on Khan Academy are not going away.

Students will continue to be able to:

  • Sign in using their existing Khan Academy accounts. Any existing mastery progress will also remain on student accounts.
  • Access and complete assignments from their teachers (other than Course Mastery Goals)
  • Build Mastery through practice
  • Track their learning progress
  • Have access to the library of high quality, standards-aligned content

What students may notice first

One of the biggest changes in Khan Academy Reimagined is a more guided learning experience for students.

Students will notice:

  • An updated homepage
  • Simplified navigation
  • A learning queue that easily shows students what to work on next
  • Unit Missions that organize learning by unit
  • More visible progress indicators throughout the platform The goal is to help students spend less time navigating and more time learning.

Learning is now organized around Missions

Missions are goal-oriented learning journeys that help students know what to work on first.

  • If you assign individual content assignments, they will be included in the Daily and Weekly Missions.

  • Mastery Goals are now Unit Missions, but the content included in a Unit Mission will be included in the Daily and Weekly Missions too. Below is some more information about how each Mission type works:

  • Unit Missions:

    • Unit Missions are assigned by their teacher and replace Unit and Course Mastery Goals from the previous experience.
    • The goal of Unit Missions is for students to get the Proficient or Mastered Mastery levels on all skills in that unit.
    • Students will complete all the exercises, quizzes and unit test in the unit. Once they reach the Proficient or Mastered level on all skills in that unit, the Unit Mission will be marked as complete.

  • Daily Missions:

    • Daily Missions are a focused view of the students’ assignments that are due today, tomorrow, or overdue.
    • These are not assignable by the teacher but are comprised of assignments teachers make for students (from Unit Missions and individually assigned pieces of content)
    • Daily Missions essentially bump up the most important Unit Mission and standalone content assignments to the front of the line so students know what to work on right now.

  • Weekly Missions:

    • Weekly Missions is the list of assignments that shows to students after they complete the daily Mission.
    • Weekly Missions give students a broader look at what’s coming up so they can work on what is due next
    • These are not assignable by the teacher but are comprised of assignments teachers make for students (from Unit Missions and individually assigned pieces of content) Students can easily access their Missions on their student dashboard. To do so:

  • Make sure students have selected the correct class from the top dropdown

  • Unit Mission: click “Start” or Continue in the Unit Missions section of the Learner Dashboard

  • Daily mission: Click the big blue “Start” or “Continue” button at the top of their student dashboard.

  • Weekly missions: will automatically show to the student once they complete all the tasks in their Daily Mission

  • Reminder! All work completed in the Daily + Weekly missions count towards the applicable Unit Missions, and content assignments as well

Viewing their assignments
  • There are 2 views students can use to see their assignments
    • The “Path” view: we recommend this path for younger students or those who might want a more visual and direct view of their assignments
    • The “List” view: great for students who can navigate filters and want more customization
  • Both the views are available on Unit Missions, Daily and Weekly Missions.
  • The student can decide which view by selecting either of these icons

New ways students can stay motivated

Khan Academy Reimagined introduces several new ways for students to celebrate progress and stay engaged with their learning:

  • Gems (these replaced Energy Points)
  • Gem Challenges + Gem rewards set by their teachers (replacing Learnstorm)
  • Customizable Khanmigo with earned accessories (replacing Avatars)

Some familiar features have been replaced

As part of the transition to Khan Academy Reimagined, the following features are no longer available:

  • Discussions
  • Levels
  • Avatars (replaced by Khanmigo customization)
  • Badges
  • Energy Points (replaced by Gems)
  • Learnstorm (replaced by Gem rewards)

Additional experiences available through Khan Academy Districts partnerships

The following experiences are available to accounts that are part of a Khan Academy District partnerships:

  • Khanmigo-powered tutoring
  • Live Team Game
  • Assignable Khanmigo activities
  • Optional Add-ons:
    • Khan Academy Interim Assessments
    • Learning Paths informed by MAP Growth

Frequently asked questions

Can I see what my students see?
  • Yes, via the student preview feature on your Teacher Dashboard.
Will students lose their progress?
  • No. Existing student progress and Mastery levels will remain on student accounts.
Do students need to create new accounts?
  • No. Students can continue using their existing Khan Academy accounts.
Will teacher assignments still work?
  • Yes. Teachers can continue assigning content (except Course Mastery Goals) to students and monitoring progress.
Can students still use Writing Coach?
  • Yes. Students in the USA can continue completing Writing Coach assignments from their teachers. We’re excited to bring these updates into classrooms and hope students enjoy the more guided and engaging learning experience!

If you have questions or need help, please contact the Khan Academy Support team through the support request form.

Where can I find detailed information about the reimagined classroom experience for students?

For the most up-to-date collection of support articles about the experience, visit this section of our help center!

Khan Academy Reimagined for Teachers

How can I preview my students’ experience in Khan Academy Reimagined?

If you’re part of Khan Academy Reimagined and want to see what your students will experience, there are two types of previews available:

Previewing the student learning queue and site navigation

To preview how your students will see and interact with their learning queue experience:

  • Select a class from your teacher dashboard.
  • Go to the Assignments tab.
  • Click Student preview. This will show you what your students see in their learning queue, including how assignments are organized, how they navigate through them, and what assignments are showing as completed on their end.

Previewing the Khan Academy content you’re assigning to students

There are different ways to preview the content depending on whether your are just browsing Khan Academy content, are creating a new assignment, or are wanting to preview an assignment you’ve already made.

1. Browsing the Khan Academy Content:
  • Click the “Explore library” option in your lefthand menu to browse through Khan Academy content.
  • Click on any link to be taken to that Khan Academy course. Then you will see everything there is to offer in that course.
  • You can also search for a topic and Khanmigo will offer different relevant content items for you.
2. Previewing new assignments before assigning:

  • You’ll see a preview option when you are making any time of assignment except for Writing Coach.

  • Here’s where to find this preview option on the different eligible assignment types:

  • Mastery Mission:

  • Khan Academy content items (videos, articles, exercises, quizzes, unit tests, course challenges): Expand the course’s units to reveal individual items. Click any item title to open and preview it

  • When available, you can click the “Show all questions” button in the top right-hand corner of the screen if you would like to see all the questions in the assignment. The “Show all questions” button is available only on exercises.

  • Khanmigo assignments:

    • Choose an activity, fill out the prompts, and then click Preview to see the full experience your students will interact with.
3. For existing assignments:
  • Go to the Assignments tab
  • Click the title of the assignment to open and preview the exact content your students will see.
  • Then you can interact with the assignment itself, just as your students would. You can also do this through clicking the “Student preview” button
  • When available, you can click the “Show all questions” button if you would like to see all the questions in the assignment. The “Show all questions” button is available only on exercises. We hope these preview tools help you confidently assign content and better support your students’ learning experience in Khan Academy Reimagined. If you have questions, please reach out to your Districts Success Manager or submit a ticket to the Khan Academy Support Team.

How do I replace Course Mastery Goals in the Khan Academy reimagined experience?

In the reimagined Khan Academy, Mastery-based practice is organized through Unit Missions rather than Course Mastery Goals. Unit Missions show student progress to teachers in smaller chunks, making it easier to spot specific gaps and see exactly where students need support.

This article will cover how to adjust your classroom routines accordingly now that Course Mastery Goals are no longer available, and answer some FAQs about this change.

What happens to existing Course Mastery Goals?

  • Course Mastery Goals are the only assignment type that do not transfer to the new reimagined Khan Academy experience.
What should I do if I was using Course Mastery Goals?
  • Assign all unit missions in the course instead
    • To do this:
      • Select “Create an assignment” from your Teacher Dashboard or Class Overview
      • Select which course you’d like to assign from
      • Click “Select all” on the Unit Missions tab
      • Optional: Drag and drop the units into the desired cadence you’d like your students to follow
      • Set due dates for each unit (don’t worry, you can adjust these later if needed!)
      • Optional: add a Course Challenge + additional classes you’d like to receive these assignments
      • Click “Assign Unit Missions”

Will students lose their progress?

  • Nope! Existing student progress remains on their accounts.
  • When you assign all the corresponding Unit Missions, any previous work students completed on that content will be reflected on your teacher reports
Speaking of reports, what reports should I use to view Mastery progress?
  • While the Course Mastery report (the purple bar graph report) has been deprecated, you will be able to see progress at the unit level rather.
  • Once you assign the Unit Missions, use the “Assignments” report to see student Mastery progress percentages at the unit level
    • To do this:
      • Click “Reports” on the lefthand side window
      • Click “Assignments”
      • Click on the title of the Unit Mission assignment
      • This will open up a chart which lists your students’ Mastery percentage for that unit
  • You can also view Mastery progress data at the unit level on the “Assignments” tab.
    • To do this:
      • Click “Assignments” from the lefthand menu
      • Click on a Unit Mission assignment
      • Click “Student summary”
      • This will show when students completed the Unit Mission, how many content items in the Unit Mission they have completed, and the number of Skills to proficient (or Mastered) each student has. We hope this article was helpful in understanding how to transition your classroom routines to Unit Missions rather than Course Mastery Goals!

If you have questions or feedback, please feel free to contact the Khan Academy Support Team. We are here and happy to help!

What do administrators need to know about the Khan Academy reimagined experience?

The reimagined Khan Academy experience offers a more streamlined and engaging learning experience for students and teachers. As mentioned in this blog post, these updates were piloted in schools, and designed with direct input from teachers to better support instruction, reporting, and student motivation. We are excited to get your school(s) started on the reimagined Khan Academy!

This admin-focused article is comprised of 4 sections:

  • Section 1: When you can expect to see these platform changes

    • Important! Ensure you have added the updated Khan Academy URL to your allowlists, firewalls and adblockers!
    • We recommend adding *.khanacademy.org (make sure to add the star and the period at the beginning!) and khanacademy.org
  • Section 4: Additional information for administrators in Khan Academy partner districts

  • July 2026: North America, Europe, East Asia, the Middle East, the Caribbean, Ecuador and Vietnam

Khan Academy Writing Coach FAQs for teachers

Can I edit a Writing Coach assignment?

Yes! You can make certain changes to a Writing Coach assignment, depending on whether students have started working on it.

To edit an assignment from the assignment page, click on the ellipsis next to the assignment.

Before any student starts the assignment

If no student has started the assignment, you can edit:

  • Assigned students
  • Assignment details:
    • Title
    • Assignment Type
    • Grade level
    • Essay type
    • Instructions
    • Due date and time

After a student starts the assignment

Once a student begins the assignment, you can still edit:

  • Assigned students
  • Due date and time

How can I use the Writing Coach essay assignments library?

The Writing Coach essay assignments library gives teachers quick access to over 80 high-quality, ready-to-assign essay prompts. These prompts are designed to save you time while supporting meaningful writing practice for your students. Each one can be customized to fit your classroom needs.

You’ll find prompts for both English Language Arts (ELA) and Social Studies. You can search by keyword, sort by grade level, and filter by essay type or subject.

Where to find the library

To get started, open Writing Coach then select Explore and assign from the left-hand menu. This will take you directly to the prompt library.

How to search and filter

Once you’re in the library, you can:

  • Search by keyword (for example, “Shakespeare” or “AI”)
  • Filter by grade level
  • For ELA prompts, filter by essay type (persuasive, explanatory, literary analysis)
  • For Social Studies prompts, filter by subject (U.S. History, World History, A.P. World History,OER Project)
  • View favorited templates
    • Clicking the ❤️ icon will add the template to the favorites tab

How to assign a prompt

Click on any prompt to view the full instructions. When you’re ready to assign, select Edit & assign. This will open an editable template with the prompt pre-filled.

You’ll need to:

  • Choose the assignment type
  • Select the grade level
  • Enter a word count (optional)
  • Select your class and students
  • Choose start and due dates and times Once everything is set, click Create assignment.

What students will see

After you create the assignment, students will see it when they log into Writing Coach. You’ll also receive a link that you can share directly with them.

Examples of available prompts

The prompt library includes a wide range of topics across genres and subjects. Some examples:

  • The School Dress Code Debate (Persuasive, ELA)
  • Romeo and Juliet: The Blame Game (Literary Analysis, ELA)
  • Critical Analysis of AI Simulations of Literary Figures (Explanatory, ELA)
  • Choose a Work of Literature for Our High School Curriculum (ELA)
  • OER Project prompts on global history themes (Social Studies) Each prompt includes clear instructions that guide students through their response.

Can I customize the prompts?

Yes. All prompts are fully editable. You can adjust the wording, change the assignment details, or tailor the instructions to your students. Whether you use a prompt as-is or modify it to fit your classroom goals, the library is designed to make setup easier and faster.

For more help with Writing Coach, visit the Writing Coach FAQs for teachers

How does the originality flag work?

When viewing student progress on a Khan Academy Writing Coach assignment, you might see that an essay was flagged for originality.

What does it mean if a student essay has an originality flag?

An originality flag refers to the potential instance of plagiarism detected by the system.

How does it work?

Writing Coach identifies instances where the student has pasted text from an unknown source, defined as any source outside of Writing Coach. This means from another tab/window or app like Microsoft Word.

What triggers a flag?

An originality flag is raised in the following instances when a student:

ACTION

FLAG SEVERITY

Pastes more than 10 words into “Thesis/claim”

Questionable flag

Pastes more than 10 words into “Reasoning/explanation”

Questionable flag

Pastes between 15-50 words into the essay

Questionable flag

Pastes more than 50 words into the essay

Critical flag

Two or more originality flags will raise a critical flag, even if none of the individual flags are critical.

Once a flag has been raised, it will be displayed in your report.

  • Even if a student erases their flagged content, the flag will remain. Notes:

This flag does not impact the student experience in any way. The student is not informed a flag was raised.

Originality flags are only available in full Writing Coach assignments. They are not included in Essay feedback assignments.

What should I include in my essay instructions?

You should be as specific and detailed as possible when writing your essay instructions. The more specific you are, the better Khanmigo can assist your students. Below are 2 examples of essay instructions.

Weak Specificity:

Who is responsible for the tragedy of Romeo and Juliet? Friar Laurence? The two lovers themselves? Their parents? Do a number of people share the blame? To what extent can these people be held responsible for the deaths of Romeo and Juliet? Analyze the actions of the character(s) you think are responsible for the lovers’ deaths.

Strong Specificity:

Who is responsible for the tragedy of Romeo and Juliet? Friar Laurence? The two lovers themselves? Their parents? Do a number of people share the blame? To what extent can these people be held responsible for the deaths of Romeo and Juliet? Analyze the actions of the character(s) you think are responsible for the lovers’ deaths.

REQUIREMENTS:

  • Your introduction should “set the stage” for your reader by introducing the play and the specific topic above, building to a clear thesis statement that makes a claim answering the question(s) posed above.
  • In the body of your essay, use at least three specific incidents from the play (one per body paragraph) as support. Make sure to:
    • Introduce each incident with enough context for your reader.
    • Explain how the incident supports your claim.
    • Incorporate at least one properly cited quotation from the text. Your quotations should clearly support your argument / explanation of the incident. Note that you may need more than one quotation from the scene you’re discussing to fully support your argument!
      • Remember, skillful essay writers incorporate quotations into their essays in a variety of ways. Try to take advantage of this variety by integrating shorter quotations seamlessly into your prose, rather than introducing every quotation with a colon!
  • Your conclusion should restate your thesis, summarize your argument, and leave your reader with some more “food for thought.”
  • Write in third person, and use literary present tense. Bottom line:

Be as detailed as possible about the requirements for the essay, so that the system “knows” to encourage the student to meet these requirements.

What will my students see when completing a Writing Coach assignment?

Writing Coach guides students through a structured writing process that helps them plan, write, and revise an essay with support from Khanmigo.

Whether students access Writing Coach through Khan Academy Classroom (KAC) or the standalone Writing Coach site, the writing experience is nearly identical. This article explains what students will experience during each stage of a Writing Coach assignment and highlights the few differences where they exist.

The student writing process

Students complete Writing Coach assignments in five stages:

  • Understand the assignment
  • Create an outline
  • Write a first draft
  • Complete the completeness check
  • Revise the essay

1. Understand the assignment

Students begin by reviewing the essay prompt and any instructions you’ve provided.

During this stage, students can:

  • Read the assignment prompt and instructions.
  • Ask Khanmigo questions about the assignment.
  • Get help understanding what the prompt is asking.
  • Receive suggestions for how to get started. Khanmigo can help students understand the assignment, but it won’t generate essay content for them.

When students are ready, they continue to the outlining stage.

2. Create an outline

Before writing, students organize their ideas using a graphic organizer.

Depending on the assignment, students can add:

  • A thesis statement
  • Body paragraphs
  • Supporting evidence
  • Reasoning and explanations
  • External sources Students can also add additional body paragraphs, rearrange sections, or remove sections they no longer need.

Throughout this stage, students can ask Khanmigo questions or request feedback on their outline. Khanmigo helps students develop their ideas, but it won’t generate outline content for them.

Note: If a student pastes more than 10 words into the Thesis/Claim, Main point/Topic, or Reasoning/Explanation fields, you’ll see a Questionable originality flag in the student’s report. Students aren’t notified when these flags are generated.

3. Write a first draft

.

Students use their completed outline to write the first draft of their essay.

While drafting, students can:

  • View their outline alongside the essay editor.
  • Copy sections from their outline into their draft.
  • Ask Khanmigo questions or request feedback.
  • Review the assignment instructions at any time. Khanmigo can provide guidance throughout the drafting process, but it won’t write the essay for the student.

Note: If a student pastes more than 15 words into their draft that didn’t originate from their outline, you’ll see an originality flag in the student’s report with additional details for review.

Important: Students can only submit their first draft for feedback once. After moving to the revision stage, they can’t return to rewrite their original draft from scratch.

4. Complete the completeness check

Before feedback begins, Writing Coach reviews the student’s draft to determine whether it’s ready for revision.

If the draft needs additional work—for example, it’s too short or missing major sections—the student will be prompted to continue writing before moving on.

This helps ensure students receive meaningful feedback on a complete draft.

5. Revise the essay

Rather than presenting all feedback at once, Writing Coach guides students through revisions one category at a time.

Students work through four feedback categories in this order:

  • Thesis & Focus – Is the main argument clear and well-defined?

  • Evidence & Reasoning – Are ideas supported with strong evidence and explanation?

  • Structure & Organization – Is the essay logically organized?

  • Language – Is the writing clear, precise, and appropriate? For each category, students:

  • Review the feedback.

  • Revise their essay.

  • Ask Khanmigo follow-up questions if they need additional guidance.

  • Continue to the next category after completing their revisions. Khanmigo won’t tell students exactly what to write. Instead, it provides guidance and actionable suggestions that help students strengthen their own writing.

This guided approach encourages students to focus on one aspect of their writing at a time instead of trying to revise everything at once.

After students finish

The final step depends on how students accessed Writing Coach.

Students using Khan Academy Classroom (KAC)

After completing all four revision categories, students see an End-of-Task card confirming they’ve completed the assignment.

They also earn 10 gems before returning to their learning queue.

Students can then export their work as:

  • Microsoft Word (.docx)
  • Google Drive (requires a Google account) Their completed essay remains available if they return later.

Preview the student experience

If you’d like to experience Writing Coach from a student’s perspective before assigning it:

In Khan Academy Classroom (KAC)

Open your Assignments page and select Preview from the assignment’s options menu.

In standalone Writing Coach

Open one of the sample essays available from the My essays page (or the essay library).

How do I disable or turn off Khanmigo for my students?

While Khanmigo is a valuable learning tool, there may be times when you want your students to work without it. Focus mode lets you temporarily disable Khanmigo for some or all students for a specific amount of time.

How do I turn on Focus mode?

  • Select your class to activate Focus mode
  • Make sure you’re signed in and have a class rostered.
  • From the left-hand menu, select My Classes, then choose your class.
  • At the top of your class view, select Settings, then the Khanmigo tab.
  • In the Focus mode section, click Set focus mode.
  • In the pop-up window, you can:
    • Select students (all students or specific ones)
    • Choose a duration (up to 4 hours)
    • See the exact end time based on your selections
    • Click Start focus mode to confirm

Can I turn Focus mode off early? Can I adjust it?

Yes! If Focus mode is already active, you’ll see:

  • A list of students with Focus mode on
  • How long it will remain active
  • The option to turn it off early for individuals or for the whole class
  • Adjust the duration if needed by selecting “Set focus mode”. The total time limit remains 4 hours.

What will my students see?

When Focus mode is turned on, students will see a message letting them know Khanmigo has been temporarily disabled by their teacher. This appears in several places:

  • In any assignment or lesson
  • In the Tutor me tab after they try to ask a question
  • In Writing Coach when trying to start or submit an essay Once the timer runs out, Khanmigo will become available to students again automatically.

We hope this article helped understand Focus Mode! If you have further questions or concerns, please reach out to our Support Team through this link. We are happy to help!

How do I use Gem Jam with my students in Khan Academy Reimagined?

Gem Jam is a classroom activity that turns practice into a team-based competition. Students are divided into teams and race to earn Gems by reaching Proficient in skills from their learning queue, while you monitor progress in real time.

Requirements and availability

  • Available to Khan Academy Reimagined users only
  • Requires mastery-enabled content such as exercises and quizzes
    • Note: Khanmigo assignments and Writing Coach will not register on the Gem Jam

How to start a Gem Jam

  • Go to your Class Overview page
  • In the top-right corner, select Start team game!

How to set up the game

This setup determines how teams are created and how long the activity will run.

After selecting Start team game!, choose your settings:

  • Set the timer

  • Select which students to include

  • Select the # of teams to create

    • This is based on how many students you select to play the game

  • Add class instructions to guide student work

  • Click “Launch team game” Important to remember:

  • Teams are assigned automatically

  • Teams are not balanced by skill level

  • Team names + Racermigo mascots are assigned automatically and cannot be edited

  • Game settings reset after each game

What students do during the game

Once the game starts:

  • Each student is placed on a team and sees their team’s Racermigo (replaces their usual Khanmigo)

  • Students work from their learning queue

  • Gems are earned only when students reach Proficient in a skill

  • Every gem earned moves their team’s Racermigo up

  • The team with the most Gems at the end of the game wins Important:

  • Students can join at any time during the game and still contribute, as long as they see their Racermigo

  • If the student does not see their Racermigo, it might not be reflected on their screen yet. They can refresh their page to make it appear

  • Refreshing the page does not interrupt participation

How to monitor the game

Once the game starts, you will be shown the live leaderboard.It shows:

  • Remaining time

  • Team Gem totals

  • Student activity feed

  • Class Gem total From this view, you can:

  • Select Edit to update instructions

  • Select End live activity to finish the game early

  • Turn game sounds on/off Recommended: Project the live leaderboard so your class can follow along!

Important:

  • The leaderboard is only visible when projected (students do not see it individually)
  • Games cannot be paused once started

How the game ends

When the timer ends (or you end the game early):

  • The final results screen shows the winning team, the class gem total, and other stats
  • If teams have the same score, the result is displayed as a tie
  • You can celebrate results or start another round

How Gem Jam impacts student progress

Work completed during a Gem Jam counts toward their learning achievement:

  • Skills completed contribute to mastery progress
  • Students earn Gems as usual
  • Gems earned count toward customizations
  • Content that has been assigned already will count as completed if the student finished it during the Gem Jam

Tips for using Gem Jam

  • Assign a specific Unit Mission for targeted review
  • Have students sit with their teams to support each other
  • Use during review time or structured practice blocks If you have questions or need help, feel free to reach out to the support team!

Any interactions that were flagged by the moderation system will have a red disclaimer under them.

From here, you can click on any of the conversations and read through them in a new pop-up:
