Khanmigo FAQs for Learners

Does Khanmigo have a read-aloud or Text-to-speech feature?

Khanmigo offers users a Text-to-Speech feature for those who would prefer to hear Khanmigo talk to them instead of reading Khanmigo’s responses on their screen.

This article will cover the below aspects of the read-aloud feature, also known as Text-to-Speech.

Click on one of the topics to skip to that section, or scroll through the article to read all the sections:

  • What can Khanmigo read out loud to me?
  • What devices and browsers does the Text-to-Speech feature work on?
  • What languages can Khanmigo talk in?
  • How do I select a voice for Khanmigo to talk to me in?
  • How do I use Text-to-speech? Where do I click so I can hear Khanmigo talk?

What can Khanmigo read out loud to me?

Khanmigo can speak its own responses on the Activities Page and chat windows out loud to you.

  • Please note: on writing activities like the Give feedback on my academic essay, Check for problems in my admissions essay, and Create a lesson plan, Khanmigo cannot read out the passages you are writing. It can only speak the responses it offers in the sidebar. Khanmigo cannot read Khan Academy content (like articles, practice exercises, or tests) or other aspects of the Khan Academy outloud to you.

What devices and browsers does the Text-to-Speech feature work on?

Text-to-Speech is optimized to work best on all of Khan Academy’s supported browsers (Google Chrome, Firefox, Microsoft Edge and Safari)

Text-to-speech is also available on the Khan Academy iOS mobile app version v8.0.0, mobile web, and desktop web. At this time, Text-to-speech is not available on the Khan Academy Android Mobile App.

What languages can Khanmigo talk in?

At this time, the Khanmigo Text-to-Speech feature is optimized to work in English, Spanish, Hindi, and Brazilian Portuguese. You can set up the language by going to Preferences > Language and selecting the one you prefer.

How do I select a voice for Khanmigo to talk to me in?

  • The first time you set up Khanmigo’s voice, the below messages will pop up on your screen. Here, you can listen to the different voices and select your preference. After this initial setup, you can change Khanmigo’s voice at any time in the Khanmigo Preferences section, which can be accessed in 3 places:

  • On the Khanmigo Activities page click the 3 dots to the right of the battery icon, followed by the “Preferences” link from the dropdown

  • On any Khanmigo chat window by opening the Khanmigo chat window through clicking the Khanmigo icon in the bottom right-hand corner of your screen, then click on the 3 dots to the right of the battery icon, followed by the “Preferences” link from the dropdown.

  • On your Learner Home in the “Khanmigo Settings” section. You can get to your Learner Home by clicking your name in the top right-hand corner, followed by “Learner home” from the dropdown list.

How do I use Text-to-speech? Where do I click so I can hear Khanmigo talk?

In order to hear Khanmigo speak to you please follow the below steps:

  • Click the headphones icon which is available in both the Khanmigo Activities page and chat windows. You will then notice a confirmation in the chat saying Khanmigo voice enabled.
    • If you haven’t selected a voice yet for Khanmigo before clicking the headphones icon, you will be prompted to choose one
  • Have a conversation with Khanmigo as normal through typing your thoughts, or clicking the microphone icon to say your response to Khanmigo.
  • Khanmigo will send its response as text first, and then read its response out loud to you. You will notice 2 things as it is responding out loud to you:
    • The section Khanmigo is saying out loud will be highlighted
    • A blue audio wavelength icon will appear below the headphones icon, indicating Khanmigo is talking
    • Please note: If you are seeing the text being highlighted and the blue audio wavelength icon, but not hearing Khanmigo speak, check the audio settings on your device to ensure the volume is turned up.
  • Click the ►icon to the right of Khanmigo’s message to replay it
  • If you want to disable Khanmigo from talking, click the headphones icon again. You will then notice the confirmation message stating Khanmigo voice disabled. We hope this article was helpful in understanding Khanmigo’s Text-to-Speech feature! If you have further questions or concerns, please reach out to our Support Team through this link. We are happy to help!

How can I change the default language that Khanmigo responds in?

You can access your Khanmigo Settings at any time through 2 ways:

  1. First, adjust the option on your Khanmigo Settings page on your Learner Home
  1. A direct link is: khanacademy.org
  1. Also, by clicking the three dots in the purple bar at the top of the chat box or Activities page, followed by the “Preferences” link

Here you can adjust your Khanmigo reading style and language, and access your chat history and interests.

Note that the language setting feature is still continuously being improved, so there are a few things to keep in mind:

  • Teacher-focused and essay-writing activities may remain in English.
  • Khanmigo should by default respond in the language in your language preferences, but in some edge cases where languages are mixed a best effort is made for what language to respond in. Some Khanmigo activities are available in multiple languages!

Thank you for your patience while we continue to develop this and all Khanmigo features! If you have any questions or feedback, please reach out.

How can I customize my Khanmigo avatar?

Did you know that Khanmigo has a vast closet of accessories you can choose from?

To access Khanmigo’s closet, please follow the below steps:

  • Log into your Khanmigo-enabled Khan Academy account and click on the Khanmigo Tab, then “Learner Activities.”

  • Click the 3 dots located in the top right-hand corner of the Khanmigo Activities page, or at the top of the Khanmigo chat window

  • Click the “Khanmigo’s closet” option from the dropdown menu Once in Khanmigo’s closet, you can use the energy points you’ve earned while working on Khan Academy to unlock the different accessories! Follow the below steps to do so:

  • Click anywhere on the item to select it

  • Click the blue “Claim” button to spend your energy points on a new item

  • Click “Wear this item” to display the accessory on Khanmigo as you navigate through Khan Academy Below is a gif showing the process of claiming a new accessory from Khanmigo’s closet!

Here are some reminders to keep in mind when shopping for new accessories in Khanmigo’s closet:

  • Khanmigo can only wear one item at a time (unless it is a combined item like the scarf + beanie set, which count as one item)
  • If you don’t have enough energy points for the item you’d like Khanmigo to wear, it will be grayed out and showing a lock on it
  • Claiming an accessory from Khanmigo’s closet cannot be undone, so be careful when clicking the “Claim” button! We hope you enjoy customizing your Khanmigo avatar with these fun accessories! If you have additional questions or feedback, please reach out to our support team through this link!

How do I enter math expressions with Khanmigo?

Entering math expressions when chatting with Khanmigo is easy, thanks to our “math keys” tool! Additionally, Khanmigo also understands LaTeX, a text-based way to write math. Find out more below.

Chatting Math with Khanmigo

Entering math equations is slightly different when working with Khanmigo vs when you are completing math exercises on a lesson.

If you are working with Khanmigo and want to enter specific math language, the entire equation must be written using the math palette.

To do so:

  • Click the “Math keys” button
    • The keypad will appear. Toggle it on or off as needed.
  • Use the keypad or type in LaTeX to write your equation. Add regular text for context.
  • Hit “Send message” and let Khanmigo assist you!

LaTeX: Your Math Typing Tool

Some exercises have a special keypad for math symbols. But sometimes, you’ll need to type them. That’s where LaTeX comes in handy. Here are some common LaTeX commands:

Multiplication: Use an asterisk (). E.g., “3*4”

Division: Use a slash (/). E.g., “3/4”. For operations in the numerator or denominator, use parentheses. E.g., “12/(5n)” or “(n+3)/6”

Square root: Type “sqrt(x)”. E.g., “sqrt(3)”

Pi: Type “pi”

Theta (θ): Type “theta”

Powers or exponents: Use a caret (^). E.g., “4^5”

Fractional exponents: Use a caret (^) and type the fraction in parentheses. E.g., “x^(1/3)”

Greater than or equal to: Type “>=”

Less than or equal to: Type “<=”

Logarithms: For base 10, enter “log(x)”. For natural logarithms, enter “ln(x)”

Logarithms with other bases: Enter as “log_b(n)”, where b is the base and n is the number

There are many more LaTeX commands to explore. Keep learning, keep growing!

How do I leave feedback about Khanmigo?

Khanmigo is a new tool that is still being improved to best assist you at Khan Academy. Giving us feedback about your conversations and experiences with it is crucial to its future development. Therefore, you will find two ways to leave feedback about your Khanmigo conversations.

1. Clicking the Thumbs Up or Thumbs Down icons

  • Please click the Thumbs Up button if Khanmigo’s message was:
    • Useful to you
    • Accurate or correct
    • Compassionate or kind
    • Prompting you to do the work yourself
  • Please click the Thumbs Down button if Khanmigo’s message was:
    • Not helpful or relevant to your conversation
    • Inaccurate or incorrect
    • Unsafe or inappropriate
    • Giving you the direct answer instead of helping you solve it yourself

2. Clicking the “Leave Feedback” link

This opens a short form for you to leave more in-depth feedback about your conversation and experiences with Khanmigo. Filling this out will send your feedback directly to the right team so they can take a look at it.

Thank you for helping improve Khanmigo by leaving feedback!

How do I view my Khanmigo chat history?

All conversations with Khanmigo are transcribed and viewable on your account. There are 3 ways to access your past Khanmigo conversations:

  1. When on the Khanmigo Activities page: click the 3 dots to the right of the battery icon, followed by the “Chat history” link from the dropdown

  2. When using Khanmigo outside of the Activities page: open the chat box and click on the 3 dots to the right of the battery icon, followed by the “Chat history” link from the dropdown

  3. When in your Learner’s home: in the “Chat History” section. You can get to your Learner Home by clicking your name in the top right-hand corner, followed by “Learner home” from the dropdown list.

Are you a teacher or parent using Khanmigo looking to find your child or student’s Chat History? The below resources are for you!

Teacher: How do I view my students’ Khanmigo chat history?

How to Use Speech-to-Text with Khanmigo

You can use speech-to-text to speak directly to Khanmigo instead of typing your messages. Here’s how to use this feature:

1. Turn on voice input

  • Click the blue microphone icon in the Khanmigo chat window.
  • If this is your first time using voice input, your device will ask for permission to access the microphone.
    • Choose either the “Allow while visiting the site” or “Allow” to continue using voice input.

2. Speak your message

Once the microphone is active:

  • Start speaking clearly into your device’s microphone.
  • A blue dot will appear under the microphone icon, showing that Khanmigo is listening.
    • As you speak, a blue audio wavelength icon will appear below the microphone icon, indicating Khanmigo is picking up your voice.
  • After a short pause, Khanmigo will display a text version of what it heard and continue the conversation based on your message. Tip: If you’re not seeing the blue dot or the voice input isn’t working, check your browser’s microphone permissions and make sure your device microphone is working properly.

What is the difference between the Khanmigo chatbot and the Khanmigo activities page?

The Khanmigo chatbot is designed to offer immediate assistance while working on Khan Academy content, offering tailored support during your learning journey.

Specific prompts will populate on the chatbot depending on what page you are on and these are intended to help you get started with your conversation with Khanmigo.

The Khanmigo activities page, on the other hand, is designed to offer educational experiences that can stand alone outside of Khan Academy content.

There are a variety of prompts to choose from on this page, and we encourage you to explore which sparks your interest!

What kind of images can I upload to Khanmigo?

If you’re working through a challenging math or science problem, you can attach an image in your Khanmigo conversation in the Tutor Me activity. Whether it’s a diagram, graph, handwritten work, or another relevant visual, adding an image helps Khanmigo better understand your question and provide more specific and personalized support.

This article explains how to use the image upload feature effectively, which types of images work best, and what to avoid—so you can get the clearest and most helpful guidance possible.

Which types of images work best for Khanmigo?

To get the most out of this feature on Khanmigo, make sure your image clearly supports your question or learning goal in math or science. Here are a few good examples:

  • A photo of your handwritten math problem to check your steps
  • A geometry diagram you’re trying to solve
  • A science diagram (like a circuit or a cell structure) that needs an explanation
  • A graph or data set that you want help interpreting

How can you attach an image?

  • Navigate to the Tutor Me activity on Khanmigo.
  • Click the paperclip icon in the chat.
  • Choose how you’d like to upload your image: file, URL, or camera.
  • Note: If using the camera option, you’ll need to grant your browser permission to access your camera.

  1. Add your question or prompt in the text box—this helps Khanmigo know how to help you. It is required to include a message or question with your image. The system doesn’t allow image-only submissions.

  2. Click the Send icon.

Supported image types and attachments

You can add the following types of images:

  • PNG
  • JPEG Screenshots, mobile phone photos, and scanned documents all work great. Once submitted, thumbnails are clickable to reveal a full-screen rendering of the image.

⚠️ Note: The Khan Academy app does not currently support image input. If you need this feature on mobile, we recommend using the mobile web version instead.

What not to attach

Please avoid attaching the following types of images, as they may be flagged or ignored by our moderation system:

  • Images that contain personal or sensitive information
  • Images that are not related to schoolwork or learning
  • Inappropriate, offensive, or disruptive content
  • Blurry, blank, or unreadable images Sticking to clear, relevant, and educational images helps us keep Khanmigo safe and focused on learning.

Important: If a child’s chat is flagged by our moderation system, their connected adult will automatically get an email notification. This email notification includes an AI-generated description of the flagged image. Parents can also review past flagged Khanmigo conversations through their child’s chat history page.

For more details, check out these support articles:

  • How do I view my child’s Khanmigo chat history?
  • What happens if my child or student’s Khanmigo conversation gets flagged?

What happens to the images?

Images you attach are only visible during your live chat session. Once you close the chat, the image is removed to protect your privacy and ensure security. Images you upload to Khanmigo are never stored on Khan Academy servers.

In your chat history, you’ll see a placeholder along with a brief, AI-generated description of the image, so you can still reference what was shared.

Who has access to this feature?

The following users have the ability to add images to their Khanmigo conversations:

  • Those who have purchased Khanmigo for themselves
  • Those who gained access to Khanmigo through their parent
  • Those who are part of a Khan Academy Districts partnership that has enabled the feature on their district’s Settings page
    • District administrators can manage this setting for their entire district

Where did the name Khanmigo come from?

The name Khanmigo is derived from the Spanish word conmigo which means “with me”, and the word Khan for Khan Academy! It coincidentally also sounds like a combination of “Khan” with the Spanish word amigo, which means “friend.”

We were drawn to this name as it evokes a welcoming presence to offer guidance as you navigate through your learning journey at Khan Academy!

Which languages can you use for Khanmigo activities?

Depending on your subscription, role, and selected language, most Khanmigo activities are available in English, Spanish, Hindi, and Portuguese.

Khanmigo is available in several more languages listed below! However, these are experimental. You may experience occasional errors or other quality-related issues.

Khanmigo is also available in the following languages:

Arabic, Azerbaijani, Bangla, Bulgarian, Burmese, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, French, Georgian, German, Greek, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Kazakh, Khmer, Korean, Kyrgyz, Latvian, Lithuanian, Mongolian, Norwegian Bokmål, Odia, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Portuguese (Portugal), Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Urdu, Uzbek, Vietnamese

How do I change the language?

There are two ways:

  • You can change the language settings on your Khan Academy account.
    • Note that this works for the listed languages except for Urdu and Arabic
    • This impacts the language your Khan Academy experience is in
  • You can change the language Khanmigo responds in which works for all the above listed languages including Urdu and Arabic.
    • In any Khanmigo activity, select the three dots located near the top right
    • Select “Preferences”
    • Select your language
    • Note that this only impacts the language Khanmigo responds in Keep in mind that the language settings feature is a work in progress. We’re continuously improving it to provide a better experience.

What about speech-to-text/text-to-speech?

Text-to-speech only works if you have set your language to English, Spanish, Hindi, or Portuguese.

Speech-to-text only works for English, no matter what language you select.

Thank you for your patience as we develop this and other exciting Khanmigo features! If you have any questions or feedback, don’t hesitate to reach out.

Khanmigo FAQs for Parents

How do I enable or disable Khanmigo on my child’s account?

Parents who have Khanmigo enabled on their own account can choose to grant access to their connected child accounts as well.

To enable or disable Khammigo on your child’s account, please follow the below steps:

  • Log into your parent account at www.khanacademy.org

  • Click your name in the top right corner

  • Select Settings

  • Click the Khanmigo tab

  • You’ll see a list of your connected child accounts

    • To enable Khanmigo for a child, check the box next to their name.
    • To disable it, uncheck the box.

  • Click Save Changes Please note:

  • This process applies to children under 18 who are connected to a parent account. If your child is 18 or older, they’ll need to sign up for Khanmigo independently at khanmigo.ai.

  • Note: If your child’s account is part of a Khan Academy District, you won’t be able to enable Khanmigo through your parent account.

  • If you’d still like your child to use Khanmigo, you can create a new personal account for them using a non-school email address.

  • If your child received access to Khanmigo through their district and you have concerns about it, please contact your district administrator to remove your child’s Khanmigo access. For more information about how to connect a child account to your parent account, and the difference between child accounts and adult accounts, please see these articles:

  • How do I create child accounts?

  • How are child / restricted accounts different from regular accounts?

How do I view my child’s Khanmigo chat history?

Once your child has Khanmigo enabled on their account, you can view their past Khanmigo conversations through your parent account.

To access your child’s chat transcripts:

  • Log into your parent account at www.khanacademy.org
  • Click your name in the top right corner
  • Select Parent Dashboard
  • Click on the name of the child whose transcripts you’d like to view. This will take you to their Learner Home
  1. On the left-hand side, under the Khanmigo section, click Chat History. You’ll see a list of all past conversations your child has had with Khanmigo.

What will you see in the chat history?

Each conversation includes a full transcript of your child’s interaction with Khanmigo. showing both their questions and Khanmigo’s responses.

  • If any messages or images were flagged by our moderation system, you’ll see a red disclaimer beneath the corresponding conversation.
  • For more information about our conversation safety features, see: What safety features does Khanmigo have?

How can I view images attached to a conversation?

Some conversations may involve images—for example, your child might have uploaded a photo of a math problem or ask Khanmigo to describe a picture.

To protect student privacy, we don’t store the actual images. Instead, the chat history will display:

  • A generic image icon in place of the uploaded image
  • A short, AI-generated description summarizing what the image showed If the image was flagged by the moderation system, a red triangle will appear next to the icon.

For more information: What kind of images can I upload to Khanmigo?

Khanmigo FAQs for Teachers

Can I give my students access to Khanmigo?

At this time, the only students who are able to receive access to Khanmigo are the following:

  • Those who attend a school that is part of an official Khan Academy Districts partnership. Khanmigo pilot schools then choose select teachers and students to use the tool in their classrooms.
  • Those who are being homeschooled by their parents. Parents can grant their children access to Khanmigo through the steps outlined in this article.
  • Those who are above 18 and would like to purchase Khanmigo for themselves. Teachers who are not homeschool parents, or part of the pilot school districts, do not have the ability at this time to enable Khanmigo for their students.

Have questions or concerns about this? Feel free to reach out to the Khan Academy Support team.

Can I print or export the documents I make with the Khanmigo Teacher Tools?

Khanmigo has a suite of incredible teacher tools for you to use in your classroom. Some of these tools generate documents and materials you may want to print or export to use outside of Khan Academy.

To print or export a document made with Khanmigo, please follow the 3 steps below:

  1. Navigate to the “Documents” section of Teacher Tools.

  2. Once in the “Documents” section, click on the document title

  3. From here, you can do a few things:

  • Edit the document’s title by clicking the pencil in the top left corner. This will be the title of the document file if you export it

  • Print the document

  • Edit the text in the document

  • All Khanmigo documents can be exported to Microsoft Word, Microsoft OneDrive, Google Drive, or as a PDF

  • Only Lesson plans and Exit tickets can also be downloaded as a PowerPoint or Google Slides

  • Only Multiple Choice Quizzes, Exit Tickets, or Questions Generator can be exported to Google Forms

  • If you would like to keep the original version of the document, but also generate a completely new version of it, start from scratch on the “Teacher Tools” page for that specific activity. The activities below currently automatically save their materials on the “Documents” section:

  • Rubric Generator

  • Class Newsletter

  • Letter of Recommendation

  • Informational Text

  • Text Rewriter

  • SMART Goal Writer

  • IEP Assistant

  • Report Card Comments

  • Lesson Plan

  • Leveler

  • Chunk Text

  • Clear Directions

  • Exit Ticket

  • Learning Objective(s)

  • Real World context Generator

  • Multiple Choice quiz

  • Questions Generator

  • Discussion Prompts

  • Lesson Hook

  • Make it Relevant We hope this article was helpful in understanding the “Documents” section! If you need further assistance, please reach out to our support team here. We are happy to help!

How can I change the name on my Khanmigo for Educators certificate?

Congratulations of getting certified through the Khanmigo for Educators course! The name displayed on the Khanmigo for Educators certificate is based on the nickname you have set on your Khan Academy account, so you absolutely can adjust it to whichever name you prefer.

Follow the below steps to change your Khan Academy nickname and re-download your Khanmigo for Educators Certificate:

  • Click on your name located near the top right hand corner.
  • Click on “Settings”
  • Edit your nickname to what you would like displayed on your Khanmigo for Educators Certificate.
  • Click “Save Changes”
  • Now that you changed your nickname, go back to the Khanmigo for Educators course.
  • Click on “Get Certificate” to re-download the document We hope this article was helpful in helping you adjust the name on your Khanmigo for Educators certificate. If you’re having any difficulty changing your nickname or getting your certificate, feel free to reach out to our Support team! We are here and happy to help.

I signed up for Khanmigo as a teacher, but am not seeing the teacher tools. What should I do?

If you are a teacher or administrator who signed up for Khanmigo but aren’t seeing the teacher tools, please follow the below steps:

  • Log into your Khanmigo-enabled Khan Academy account
  • Click your name in the top right-hand corner of the screen
  • Select “Settings” from the dropdown menu
  • Ensure you have a birthday set on your account
  • Scroll down to the “Roles” section, select the “Teacher” role and click “Save changes”
  • Scroll down to the “Are you a teacher using Khan Academy on behalf of a school?” section, click the “Yes” option
  • Add your zip code and choose your school from the dropdown list. If you are a homeschool parent or your school isn’t listed, you can select “Other”
  • Click “Save Changes”
  • If you are not seeing these options in your settings page, please click the “Add your school” link located on your Teacher Dashboard. The same steps above will populate for you to follow If you are still having trouble viewing the Khanmigo teacher tools after following these steps, please let us know by submitting a support request. I’m a teacher - where can I learn more about how to use Khanmigo and Artificial Intelligence in my classroom?

Which languages can I use for Khanmigo and free teacher tools?

Khanmigo can understand and respond in multiple languages, and Khan Academy’s free teacher tools are also available in many of those same languages.

This article explains how to change the language Khanmigo uses and lists the languages that are supported for both Khanmigo and the teacher tools experience.

How to set Khanmigo’s response language

You can change the language Khanmigo uses in two ways:

Option 1: Use your Khanmigo settings
  • Go to teacher tools and open any tool
  • Select the three vertical dots near the top right of the tool
  • Select preferences
  • Scroll to the Language section
  • Choose your preferred language from the dropdown
  • Your selection will be saved for future chats
Option 2: Ask Khanmigo directly in a chat

You can also switch languages at any time by typing a message, such as:

“Please respond in Spanish.”

“Can you speak to me in French?”

“Use Urdu from now on.”

Khanmigo will continue in that language until you ask it to switch again.

Supported languages

Khanmigo and Khan Academy’s free teacher tools are available in the following languages:

Arabic, Azerbaijani, Bangla, Bulgarian, Burmese, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, French, Georgian, German, Greek, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Kazakh, Khmer, Korean, Kyrgyz, Latvian, Lithuanian, Mongolian, Norwegian Bokmål, Odia, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Portuguese (Portugal), Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Urdu, Uzbek, Vietnamese

Only English, Hindi, Spanish, and Portuguese have been fully quality-tested for use with Khanmigo.

Khanmigo for School and District Administrators

How are administrators alerted to moderated Khanmigo chats?

We recognize that school leaders must prioritize student safety. To support this,we have developed the option for Khan Academy Districts partners to designate specific administrators to receive email notifications when Khanmigo flags high-severity content.

How moderation alerts work

Khanmigo’s moderation system continuously monitors all student conversations and uses a two-tier alert system to notify designated school personnel based on the severity of the flagged content. Here’s a quick overview:

Standard alerts

  • Who gets notified: The teacher linked to a student’s Khan Academy account.
  • What gets flagged: Any content detected as potentially inappropriate, offensive, or outside community guidelines (e.g., profanity, light bullying, or off-topic behavior).
  • Purpose: Helps teachers monitor day-to-day usage and support positive classroom behavior.
  • Frequency: These alerts are more common and intended for lower-risk concerns.

Admin alerts

  • Who gets notified: Teachers and any designated administrators added to your district’s moderation alert list.
  • What gets flagged: Content that receives a high-confidence score from OpenAI’s moderation tool (e.g., violent threats, indications of harm to self or others, highly explicit content).
  • Purpose: These alerts are escalated because they may indicate real-world safety concerns and often require immediate attention or follow-up.
  • Frequency: These alerts are rarer and reserved for critical cases that go beyond classroom disruption. Important: Administrators will only receive high-severity alerts if they’ve been manually added to the district’s alert list in the settings.

This article will:

  • Provide setup instructions for adding or removing yourself or other administrators to receive high-severity email alerts
    • Please note: there is no default person who is added to this list. Unless an administrator is added, only teachers will continue to receive moderation email alerts.
  • Show a sample email that designated administrators will receive

Section 1: Adding or removing administrators for high-severity alerts

Follow these steps to manage which administrators receive notifications for the most serious moderation flags.

Steps to add administrators:

  • Log into your Khan Academy District Administrator account
  • Access the Administrator Dashboard
    • Click your name in the top right corner
    • Select “Administrator dashboard” from the dropdown menu
  • Select “Settings” from the left-hand menu
  • Select administrators to notify
    • Use the “Select Admins” box to find and select the administrators you’d like to add.
    • Note: If the list is missing someone, it means they are not rostered as an administrator with Khan Academy Districts, or you do not have the necessary permissions to view them. For example, school administrators will not see district administrators on the list unless they too have district-level permissions.
  1. Save your selections
  • Click the blue “Add Users” button To remove administrators:

Click the blue X next to any name in the list to remove them from notifications

Section 2: Sample email individuals will receive once on this list

Once an individual has been added to the notification list, they’ll receive email alerts whenever a student’s conversation with Khanmigo is flagged as high-severity.

Please see the below image showing a sample email of what you will receive when you are added to the above list:

Accessing the full chat history

Important: Only the following people can view the complete conversation by clicking the “Khanmigo chat from [date]” link in the email:

  • The student’s assigned teacher
  • The student’s parent/guardian (if relevant)
  • Administrators on your high-severity notification list

Troubleshooting access issues:

If you click the chat history link and see a message saying you don’t have access to view this content, it means you either:

  • Don’t have the correct permissions to view the chat
  • Are not logged into Khan Academy with an account that has appropriate permissions

Khanmigo usage guidelines for educators

Welcome to Khanmigo: a guide for educators and administrators

Navigating the world of AI in education can be both exciting and a little daunting. That’s why we’ve created this guide to help educators and administrators like you get the most out of Khanmigo and Khanmigo Teacher Tools. Whether you’re just getting started or looking to deepen your use of AI in your teaching, this guide is here to support you every step of the way.

Getting started with responsible AI use

Embracing AI technologies in education begins with learning how to use these tools thoughtfully and responsibly.

Khan Academy provides a range of resources to support educators in integrating AI effectively, including our AI for Education Course and AI Resource Hub. We encourage you to explore these resources to deepen your understanding of how to apply AI effectively in the classroom.

Understanding AI’s capabilities and limitations

Khanmigo and Khanmigo Teacher Tools use AI technology, which is still in the early stages of development. While these tools offer innovative support, they have limitations and may occasionally produce errors or “hallucinations.” We recommend reviewing and verifying the AI-generated content (“Output”) to ensure that any educational materials you create are accurate and appropriate for your intended use.

Privacy matters

Khan Academy is committed to protecting user privacy across all our services, including those powered by AI. Khanmigo uses AI developed by our external partners. While we’ve implemented safeguards to protect submitted information,Khanmigo is not intended to be used to process personally identifiable information (PII). We advise you to avoid including any personally identifiable information in Khanmigo chat queries or activities.

We encourage you to familiarize yourself with our Privacy Policy for more detail.

Keep Humans in the Loop

Khanmigo Teacher Tools are designed to support your work and help lighten your workload. However, they are not a replacement for the professional expertise and judgment you bring as an educator. These tools should be used thoughtfully and should not be relied upon as the sole basis for performance assessments or decisions about students.

Check with school policies

Using Khanmigo within your school environment requires adherence to your school’s policies and regulations. Your commitment to aligning the use of Khanmigo with these policies ensures responsible use of AI tools in a manner that is appropriate for your educational setting.

Guidelines for use and conduct

Our AI-enabled tools are designed for individual use and educational purposes only. To help keep our platform safe and constructive, and to support the responsible use of AI in education, all users must comply with both our Terms of Service and OpenAI’s Usage Policy.

We ask all users to follow these guidelines and avoid using Khanmigo to:

  • Share unlawful or harmful content
  • Create or spread hateful, discriminatory, or offensive material
  • Causing harm to other individuals Creating and sharing AI content

When using Khanmigo to generate content, you must follow our Terms of Service and OpenAI’s Sharing and Publication Policy. This includes:

  • Ensuring you have the rights to any content you submit as input
  • Verifying the accuracy of any content Khanmigo generates as output
  • Clearly disclosing the use of AI if you share the materials externally Khanmigo in the classroom

If your school uses Khanmigo with students, you play a vital role in:

  • Teaching responsible AI use
  • Explaining the limitations of AI-generated responses
  • Helping students protect their personal information Encourage students to ask thoughtful questions and to think critically about the answers they receive.

Onward!

Our goal is to foster responsible, informed, and empowering use of AI-enabled tools in educational settings. By following these guidelines, you can make the most of Khanmigo while upholding your professional integrity and safeguarding your students’ privacy.

Let’s embark on this journey together, embracing the potential of AI to transform education.

Explore our AI for Education Course and AI Resource Hub or try the Khanmigo Teacher Tools to get started today.

Khanmigo Safety and Security Information

How do the Large Language Models powering Khanmigo work?

Large Language Models (LLMs) are a type of artificial intelligence trained to understand and generate human language. They work by analyzing massive amounts of text from books, websites, articles, and more, to learn the patterns and structures of language.

The more data an LLM is trained on, the better it becomes at recognizing patterns in language. Once trained, it can generate new text by predicting the most likely next words or phrases based on the patterns it has learned.

Educational applications and limitations

LLMs have many practical applications in education. They can act like a personal tutor, helping you understand subjects by generating clear explanations, definitions, and relevant examples. If you’re learning a new language, you can practice grammar and vocabulary through conversation. They can also guide you through problem-solving steps rather than simply giving you answers.

However, language models aren’t perfect and can sometimes make mistakes. This is partly because they are trained on large datasets that may include biases or inaccuracies. Additionally, language itself is complex and ever-evolving, which can make it challenging for models to fully understand nuance or context. If the context of a question or conversation is unclear, the model may misinterpret it or respond inaccurately. Sometimes, language models may even produce off-topic or inappropriate responses. That’s why it’s important to use them thoughtfully, and with an understanding of their limitations.

Privacy and safety

When using Khanmigo or any LLM, it’s important not to include personally identifiable information (PII) in your questions or conversations. This includes full names, addresses, phone numbers, school names, student IDs, or personal details about yourself or others. While these models are designed with safety in mind and are generally considered safe to use, keeping sensitive information out of your prompts helps protect your privacy and ensures a safer online experience. LLMs can provide helpful responses and educational support without needing any personal information from you.

Getting the best results from Khanmigo

Here are some ways you can get the highest-quality responses from Khanmigo or any LLM:

  • Be clear and specific: When asking a question or inputting a problem into a language model, be as clear and specific as possible. Provide all the necessary information and context to help the model understand what you’re asking for. This will help ensure that you receive an accurate and helpful response.
  • Check multiple sources: While LLMs can be a great resource for learning and understanding, it’s always a good idea to check multiple sources to verify the information. Don’t rely solely on the response from a language model, but also consult textbooks, articles, or other trusted sources.
  • Understand the limitations: Remember that LLMs can make errors and may have knowledge gaps. It’s important to understand their limitations and be aware of the potential biases or errors in the data they are trained on. Use them as learning tools to supplement your learning, not as the sole source of information.
  • Practice critical thinking: Don’t just accept responses at face value. Practice critical thinking and try to understand the reasoning behind the response. This will help you better understand the concept and improve your problem-solving skills. By following these guidelines, you can effectively use LLMs to enhance your learning while staying aware of their limitations. Understanding how these tools work helps you use them responsibly and get the most educational value from your interactions.

What are the Community Guidelines for Khanmigo?

Khanmigo’s Community Guidelines explain how to use Khanmigo in a safe and responsible way.

Khanmigo is Khan Academy’s AI tool designed to support your learning. You can use it in different ways, including tutoring, classroom activities, and assessments (through Khanductor, our AI assessment facilitator).

Following these guidelines will you get the most out of Khanmigo while keeping your learning experience safe and effective.

Note: If you’re a student connected to a teacher or parent, please keep in mind that they can view all your Khanmigo interactions.

How can you use Khanmigo effectively?

Be clear and specific with your questions

  • When asking Khanmigo a question, be as clear and specific about the topic as possible.

  • Provide the necessary information and context to help Khanmigo understand what you’re asking for. This will help ensure that you receive an accurate and helpful response. Check multiple sources

  • Khanmigo is a helpful learning companion, but it shouldn’t be your only source of information.

  • When possible, check textbooks, class materials, or other trusted resources alongside Khanmigo’s responses. Practice critical thinking

  • When using Khanmigo to learn or solve a problem, don’t just accept answers at face value. Take time to understand the reasoning and make sure it makes sense to you. This helps you build deeper understanding and stronger problem-solving skills.

What is considered misuse of Khanmigo?

Using any kind of inappropriate or offensive language or images.

  • Khan Academy is a learning community for people of all ages, so conversations with Khanmigo should always be respectful and appropriate for a learning environment.

  • Keep language and images appropriate. Do not use violent, hateful, illegal, sexual, or otherwise inappropriate content, or ask Khanmigo to generate or describe it.

  • Even though your chats are private to you and your teacher and/or parent, Khan Academy is never the place for inappropriate conversations. Using Khanmigo for non-educational purposes

  • Khanmigo is designed to support your learning, not do your work for you.

  • Keep conversations focused on learning and educational topics.

  • Using Khanmigo to cheat, complete assignments on your behalf, or avoid doing your own work is not an appropriate use of the tool. Khanmigo should be used to help you learn, practice, and build understanding. Sharing sensitive or private information

  • Do not share private photos or personal details (like your address, phone number, or passwords) with Khanmigo.

  • Keep conversations focused on learning to help protect your privacy. Trying to bypass Khanmigo’s safety features

  • Do not try to trick or manipulate Khanmigo into generating inappropriate content or ignoring its safety rules.

What happens if my conversation gets flagged?

  • Content deemed inappropriate by our moderation system may be rejected or flagged.
  • If you’re a minor, your teacher or parent will be notified about any flagged messages over email.
  • ​​We do not store images to protect your privacy. However, if an inappropriate image is uploaded, your teacher or parent will receive an automated alert that includes a detailed description of the image’s content.
  • Violating the guidelines can lead to temporary or permanent loss of access to Khanmigo.
  • If you believe your access was restricted by mistake, you can submit an appeal form. Note: These guidelines may change as we learn more about how students, teachers, and parents use Khanmigo. In the meantime, we prioritize safety and educational value when reviewing content.

What happens if my child or student’s Khanmigo conversation gets flagged?

Khan Academy uses moderation technology to detect inappropriate, harmful, or unsafe content in Khanmigo conversations. This system monitors both text messages and images to maintain a safe learning environment for all users.

When content is flagged, the system automatically sends both an email notification and an in-platform notification to the adult associated with the child’s account. Notification recipients vary by account based on how a child or student accesses Khanmigo.

Who receives notification alerts?

If the child has received Khanmigo access through their parent:

  • The parent will receive the notification and email alert concerning the flag

  • Parents can also view all flagged conversations and images in their child’s chat history page If the student has received Khanmigo through their school district:

  • If they’re working on a Khanmigo assignment:

    • The teacher who assigned the work will receive the the moderation notification and email.

  • If they’re not working on a Khanmigo assignment:

    • The primary teachers of all district-synced classes will receive the the moderation notification and email.
    • Co-teachers do not receive alerts

  • If a flag meets a certain severity threshold and the district has opted for administrator notifications:

    • Designated admins will also receive an email.
    • These admins can view flagged chats through links included in emails forwarded to them by teachers or parents.
    • While emails to administrators are clearly labeled when a serious issue is detected, all moderation alerts sent to teachers—regardless of severity—have the same format. If the student has received Khanmigo through their school district, but also has a parent connected to their account:

  • Only the teacher (or administrator, if applicable) will receive the notification

  • However, the parent can still see flagged content through the child’s chat history Notifications examples:

This is what a parent or teacher can expect to see in their email and account notifications when a conversation is flagged

Important reminders:

  • About our moderation system: We continuously work to improve content detection accuracy, but no automated system is perfect.
  • About flagged images: To protect student privacy, we don’t store uploaded images on our servers. When an image is flagged, you’ll receive a detailed AI-generated description of the content rather than the actual image. This description provides more context than what appears in the student’s chat history. Learn more:

What is Khan Academy’s approach to responsible AI development?

As a nonprofit educational organization, Khan Academy is committed to explore how AI can shape the future of learning. We believe AI has the potential to transform education in meaningful ways, but we also recognize the serious risks it can pose.

That’s why we’ve developed a set of guidelines and safeguards to ensure our AI development prioritizes the needs of students and teachers. Our goal is to use AI responsibly in educational settings and to ensure its benefits are shared equitably across society. As we continue learning about AI and the technology evolves, so will our guidelines.

  • We educate people about the risks and we are transparent about known issues. We provide clear communication about the risks and limitations of AI both before and after users gain access to our tools. We also offer easy ways for users to report any issues they encounter.

Participants must read and accept the known and potential unknown risks and limitations of AI, including the fact that:

  • AI can be incorrect or misleading

  • It may generate inappropriate or harmful content

  • It can make factual and mathematical errors To help the public better understand AI, we’ve also launched a free course called AI for Education, which covers:

  • How large language models (LLMs) work

  • How LLMs apply to education

  • What AI is (and isn’t) good at

  • Key questions educators and learners should be asking about AI

  • We use proven practices from respected organizations to help guide our risk evaluation and mitigation efforts. We’ve studied and adapted frameworks from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the Institute for Ethical AI in Education to evaluate and mitigate AI risks specific to Khan Academy.

We acknowledge that AI is not always accurate and not entirely safe, and that it’s not possible to eliminate all risks at this time.

That’s why we work diligently to identify risks and put mitigation measures in place. We mitigate risk by using technical approaches such as:

  • Fine-tuning the AI to improve accuracy
  • Prompt engineering to guide and narrow the focus of the AI. This allows us to train and tailor the AI for a learning setting.
  • Monitoring and moderating of participant interactions to detect and respond to inappropriate content and apply appropriate community controls (such as removing access)
  • Limiting daily usage, since longer sessions are more likely to result in poor AI behavior
  • Red teaming to intentionally testing the AI to uncover vulnerabilities or flaws
  • Collecting and consistently reviewing in-product feedback from users to better understand what’s working and where improvements are needed We also make it clear that AI-generated content may include errors (even in subjects like math) and that inappropriate content is possible.

These efforts are designed to help build stronger, safer, and more trustworthy AI tools over time.

  • At this time, we only grant access to our AI applications through khanmigo.ai or through a Khan Academy Districts partnership.
  • To access our AI-powered tools:
  • Individual users must be at least 18 years old and register through khanmigo.ai.
  • Adults who register can grant Khanmigo access to any child accounts linked to their Khan Academy parent account.
  • Users under 18 can only use Khanmigo if:
    • They are part of a Khan Academy Districts partnership, or
    • They have been granted access by a parent or guardian through a linked child account.
    • Their teacher has assigned them a writing coach essay assignment. Note: Outside of these scenarios, users under 18 are not eligible to use Khanmigo.

Every child who has access to our AI-powered tools receives clear communication that their chat history and activity are visible to their parent or guardian, and, if applicable, their teacher and school administrator. We also use moderation technology to detect interactions that may be inappropriate, harmful, or unsafe. When the moderation system is triggered, it sends an automatic email alert to an adult connected to the student’s account.

  • We embrace and encourage a culture where ethics and responsible development are embedded in our workflows and mindsets. Individuals and teams are asked to identify ethical considerations and evaluate risks at the outset of every project. Our decision-making is guided by risk evaluation. We prioritize risk mitigation, embrace transparency, and continuously reflect on the impact of our work.

We have a detailed monitoring and evaluation plan in place during this testing period. We will learn, iterate, and improve.

Looking ahead:

AI is a rapidly developing field with tremendous potential. We are enthusiastic about AI’s ability to benefit education, and we recognize that we have a lot to learn. Our ultimate goal is to harness the power of AI to accelerate learning. We will evaluate how AI works and share our learnings with the world. We expect to adapt our plans along the way.

What safety features does Khanmigo have?

As a nonprofit educational organization, Khan Academy is committed to responsibly exploring AI’s potential in education.

We’re excited about AI’s ability to transform learning in a positive way, but we also recognize the risks that may come with this technology. For this reason, we have incorporated the following practices and features into Khanmigo.

Safety infrastructure

  • We are committed to an ethical and responsible AI development process that puts the needs of students and teachers first, following educational privacy standards and best practices.
  • We use moderation technology to detect interactions that may be inappropriate, harmful or unsafe.
  • We do not store images that users share with Khanmigo in accordance with our Privacy Policies.
  • Communication and feedback
  • Every child who has access to Khanmigo receives clear communication that their chat history and activities are visible to parents or guardians and, if applicable, their teacher and school administrator. Chat logs are stored securely and can be reviewed at any time through the parent/guardian dashboard.
  • When the moderation system is triggered, it automatically notifies and sends an email to an adult connected to the child’s account, providing details about the flagged interaction so they can follow up appropriately.
  • Our in-product messaging clearly states the limitations of the artificial intelligence technology Khanmigo uses, including that it may occasionally provide incorrect information and should not replace teacher instruction or parental guidance.
  • We have built-in feedback features and appeal processes, so users like you can easily bring any questions, concerns, or requests for review directly to the Khan Academy team. For more detailed information about our privacy practices and data handling, please see our full Privacy Policy.

Where can I learn more about artificial intelligence’s potential role in education?

Khan Academy offers a free course called AI for education that explores how generative AI is transforming teaching and learning. This course is an evolving resource, and we’re committed to keeping it up to date as AI technologies and educational practices continue to grow and change.

  • If applicable to your work, we also recommend checking out this help center article: Khan Academy’s AI Resource Hub for Administrators and Education Leaders We hope you’ll let Khan Academy be your trusted partner on this exciting journey!

You can find the course by clicking this link or by selecting it from the Explore menu under the Life Skills section.

The course is organized into three units:

  • Unit 1: Getting Started with Generative AI, which includes introductory videos on what AI is, how it works, and key ethical considerations.
  • Unit 2: Getting Ready to Teach with AI
  • This unit offers strategies, best practices, and video series to help educators build confidence and creativity as you integrate AI into your teaching.
  • Unit 3: Lesson Plans for AI Literacy
  • This unit was developed with Common Sense Education, and includes ready-to-use lesson plans for grades 6–12. Topics cover AI bias, chatbots, algorithms, facial recognition, and more. We invite you to explore the course and grow alongside us as AI continues to shape the future of education.

Why did Khanmigo flag my conversation?

Khan Academy uses a moderation system that combines large language models and other technologies to review conversations and flag content that may be unsafe or inappropriate for a learning environment. These tools are supplemented by human review to help maintain a safe experience for all users.

If one of your conversations was flagged, that means our system detected something that might go against our Khanmigo Community Guidelines.

What’s considered inappropriate?

A good rule of thumb is:

If it wouldn’t be appropriate to say out loud in a classroom, especially with elementary students present, it probably isn’t appropriate on Khan Academy either.

Khanmigo’s moderation system may flag conversations that include:

  • Profanity or inappropriate language
  • Violence, threats, or references to harm — even if meant as a joke
  • Sexual or other mature content
  • Phrases that may trigger safety filters, including references to self-harm or self-harm ideation
  • Bullying, harassment, or hate speech Can the system make mistakes?

Yes — and we know it sometimes does.

Like many AI systems, Khanmigo’s moderation tools are continually improving. We use a combination of automated systems and human review to help strengthen accuracy over time. Because the system is designed to prioritize safety, it may occasionally flag content that is actually appropriate.

We understand this can be frustrating, especially when you’re asking a thoughtful question or seeking help with your schoolwork. That’s why we regularly review flagged cases, learn from them, and refine our processes to improve accuracy and reduce unnecessary flags.

Want to learn more?

You can read the full Khanmigo Community Guidelines here.

What happens if my child or student’s Khanmigo conversation gets flagged?

If you think your message was flagged by mistake and you have questions, you can also contact our support team.

Learning Paths Teachers

How do I use my Learning Paths Placements and how can I view the Placement report?

The Learning Paths Placement tab shows teachers the Khan Academy-recommended MAP RIT ranges for students to work on based on their most recent MAP Growth scores. In this tab, students whose names appear in blue have activated their accounts, and students whose names are in gray have not.

Raw scores appear in parentheses next to each student’s name, and the page groups students based on their MAP RIT ranges. Clicking on an activated student’s name will take you to their individual student report.

From the placements tab, select the test you want to assign to your students.

Once you have selected the test, from the Placement tab, teachers can choose to adjust goals based on their personal knowledge of students’ levels or can opt to accept all recommendations set by Khan Academy by clicking on the “Assign placements” button at the top of the page. As new students activate, the button will reappear to prompt you to set their placements as well. Please note that the system will always take the students’ most recent RIT scores, and they will update again once new scores are in.

If your district is using the Khan Academy + Learning Paths informed by MAP Growth product, in order to be able to see the Placements report:

  • Click on the Reports tab on the left hand side of your Teacher dashboard. Be sure you have the class you are wanting to view reports for selected.
  • Once you click into the Reports tab, you will see the option for Placements
  • From there, you will be able to see the student’s name, their Instructional area, Placement score, Learning Minutes, Skills leveled up, Skills w/o progress, Progress this period, and Progress to date.
    • Please note that you will be able to view All Instructional Areas, as well as toggle specific views if you prefer. Also, you will be able to choose your dates from the dropdown We hope this article was helpful for you to learn how to use your Placements tab and Report for Learning Paths. For additional guidance or to share feedback, please reach out to our support team here! We are happy to help.

My student’s test score isn’t available. How do I set placements by MAP growth manually?

Once your students have activated their accounts, you can start setting their placements based on the MAP Growth scores that have been imported. However, what happens when scores do not import?

No worries!

If you are not seeing your student’s MAP Growth scores on your Placements report, but they are indeed activated, then you will be able to manually set the placements for them based on your knowledge of where the class should be as a whole.

Placements are always customizable, and even when scores are imported properly, teachers have full autonomy over changing the Placements based on the needs of the student and the class.

When scores have not been imported, students on your Placement tab will look like this:

Once you click on the affected student, you will see the following message:

Students can be placed manually in two ways if scores have not been imported: using the Assign placements or by accessing the individual student’s Placement View:

Assign placements

Individual Placement View

Why do the Progress and Individual Student Activity Log reports show different minutes measurements?

Teachers may notice different time measurements for an individual student on their Activity Overview Report versus their Individual Student Report. This is because the Activity Overview is specific to a class, and only includes learning time that students have accumulated since joining that class.

The Individual Student Report, on the other hand, includes learning minutes that the student acquired before joining. It is likely, then, that the Individual Student Report will show more minutes. Please note is that when filtering by content type, the learning and exercise minutes will not appear.

Students only have access to their Individual Student Report, and so this is the number that they will see as well, which may not align with the Activity Overview count.

It is important to note that the Activity Overview includes minutes spent on any topic–not only those spent on material in that class. In the Individual Student Report, you are able to filter by content and type of activity, as seen in the image above.

Making and managing assignments

How can I assign Khan Academy content in my students’ language?

Currently, coaches can assign content (videos, articles, practice, quizzes, and unit tests) to students in any language that that content is available in.

You can assign content as normal through your teacher dashboard, and if the assigned content is not available in a student’s selected language, Khan Academy will automatically display the English version of that content. This allows students to continue accessing and completing their assigned work, even when a translated version isn’t available.

For example, if a coach assigns English-only ELA content to a student who is using the Spanish version of Khan Academy, the student will see that content in English. Please see screenshot below

NOTE: Not all Unit titles are translated in all languages and if the title does not have an equivalent translated name then it will revert to English.

If you would like to take a quick look at what content is available, by language, before you assign that content to your students, you can do so by accessing the following URL and pick the language locale that you prefer: classroom.khanacademy.org<locale>

Examples: classroom.khanacademy.org or classroom.khanacademy.org

To help ensure your students have the most consistent experience, using the same language version of Khan Academy that your students use to complete their assignments whenever possible is highly recommended. You can also review our list of fully translated non-English languages here.

To learn more about how to leverage mulitlingual support for your students, please check out this video!

We also encourage you to take our Khan for Educators Course, which has step-by-step guidance, how-to videos, and tips on how to implement Khan Academy with students.

How do I assign content from more than one subject to my class?

You can assign from any subject to your class, not just the subject you selected for the class originally.

There are three main options for assigning content from other subjects:

  • By going to a course page and browsing its content. You can assign elements of the course like videos, articles, and exercises.
  • By searching for a topic or resource using the Search bar at the top of any Khan Academy page.
  • If you’re teaching math, you can browse by Common Core standard. For more information on assigning content using each of these three options, check out our article on finding content to assign.

How do I delete an assignment?

An assignment can only be deleted from the Teacher Dashboard by the teacher who created the assignment. To delete an assignment, please follow these steps:

  • Go to your Teacher Dashboard.
  • Choose one of your classes under My Classes.
  • Click Assignments.
  • Select the assignment you’d like to delete by clicking the three dots in front of it.
  • Click on Delete.
  • A pop-up window will show up asking if you want to delete the assignment. Click Yes, delete. Note: Deleting an assignment will remove it from both your assignment page and your students’ assignments pages.

How do I edit multiple assignments at once?

At this time, bulk editing assignments is not available in Khan Academy Reimagined.

If you need to update an assignment, you’ll need to edit each assignment individually.

After you create an assignment, you’ll be able to Edit, Copy, or Delete it as needed. Here’s how to do that:

Click on Assignments in the left sidebar.

  • Khanmigo Learner Activities

How do I make assignments for my students on Khan Academy?

Please note: this article reflects the platform before the reimagined Khan Academy was launched. If you are not seeing the reports as shown in this article, check out this version instead: How do I make assignments for my students in Khan Academy Reimagined?

Assignments from Khan Academy can be strategically used as a supplementary tool to provide additional support or acceleration. Articles, videos, exercises, quizzes, unit tests, course challenges, and Khanmigo Activities can be assigned to individual students based on their unique learning needs.

This article will cover the 3 options on how to make assignments for students:

  1. Making them from the “Assign tab” on your Teacher Dashboard

  2. Assigning them while viewing the content item itself

  3. Assigning Khanmigo Activities (for Khan Academy District teachers + students only)

Below are the 5 steps to create an assignment from your Teacher Dashboard:

We recommend this option, as it gives you more insight into the content in a particular course, and helps you customize the assignment to your classroom’s needs.

Step 1: Log into your Khan Academy account. Click your name in the top right-hand corner, then select the “Teacher Dashboard” link from the dropdown list.

Step 2: Select which class you would like to make an assignment for.

Step 3: On the left-hand menu bar, click the “Assign” option below the “Assignments” section.

Step 4: Click the checkbox on the right-hand side of the screen to select which content in the course you would like to assign to your students.

  • Please note, that this page is organized by the units in the course. If you click the > symbol next to the unit title, it will expand to show the lessons.

    • Click the > symbol next to the lesson to show the videos, articles, practice exercises, quizzes, and/or unit tests in that unit.
    • We recommend choosing 1-2 pieces of individual content to assign, rather than assigning the entire unit or lesson.
    • The Course Challenge is located at the end of this list, so scroll down to the bottom to locate it.

  • The “Search for Content” box also allows you to easily search for content in that course, or search by content type.

  • Please note: if you have multiple courses added to your class, you can select which course from the dropdown which is located to the left of the search bar. Step 5: Click the blue “Assign” button in the top right-hand corner of the screen. This will open a pop-up window with additional information to add about your assignment(s):

  • The blue “Assign” button and the pop-up window show how many items you’re assigning.

    • Note: Watch out that you didn’t assign a unit’s worth of content – 60 assignments can be overwhelming for students!

  • You can decide between different or the same set of questions for your students.

    • The Start Over link is unavailable for assignments set to “Same question set for all students,” setting applied to them.
    • The “Bonus Question” feature is also not available if you select the “Same question set for all students” option.

  • Select which class(es) and student(s) to receive the assignment(s)

    • Note: if all students are selected, then any new students who join your class before the assignment is due will also automatically receive this assignment.
    • Note: if you don’t have any students when you make the assignment, all future students will receive it when they join your class.

  • Choose your assignment Start Date, Due Date and times.

    • Choosing the start date to be today will give your students the assignment immediately
    • Selecting a future start date will give your students the assignment on that date
    • Students will see the assignments listed in order by the due date, with assignments due soonest will show up at the top of their list. If you would like to sequence the assignments in a specific order, assign them with slightly different due dates.
Creating assignments directly from the content page:

To create an assignment from a specific content page please follow the below steps:

Step 1: browse our library until you find material that you want your students to work on. This could be a quiz, unit test, course challenge, video, article, or an exercise.)

Step 2: While viewing a Khan Academy lesson, click the Assign button located near the top center section of the content.

Step 3: Adjust the assignment settings on the pop-up modal.

How do I schedule an assignment for a future date?

You’ve previously learned how to create assignments.

By scheduling assignments, you’ll be able to set assignments to go live for your classes on a specific date in the future.

Scheduling assignments from a class’s Assignments tab

Here’s how you can schedule a future assignment from the Assignments tab for any of your existing classes:

  • Access the desired class on your Teacher Dashboard

  • Go to the Assignments tab.

  • Click “Add Assignments”, then “Assign Content” A new screen will pop up that looks like the screenshot below. On this screen, you will:

  • Select a course from your class’s course list

  • Choose if you want to assign full units or individual content items

  • Select a due date for the future

  • Review and assign.

    • You can select the students who should get the assignments. You can also add another class, or all classes, to receive the assignments.

Scheduling assignments directly from the course page

You can also schedule an assignment from its specific content page. To do so, please follow these instructions:

  • Browse our library until you find a course that you’d like your students to work on;
  • You can either assign all units or individual units
  • Select the class you’d like to assign to and follow the same flow as when creating assignments from the Assignments tab
  • If the start date is in the future, the mission will be scheduled to go live on that chosen date.
  • Note: You need to space out the date for your Unit Mission goals, so they are shown in the correct order to students.

Scheduling assignments directly from the content page

1. Browse our library until you find content that you’d like your students to work on;

  1. At the top-right corner of the page, click Assign

  2. Select the class you’d like to receive the assignments and follow the same flow as when creating assignments from the Assignments tab

If the start date is in the future, the assignment will be scheduled to go live on that chosen date.

Locating scheduled assignments

Every assignment you schedule will be saved in your class’s Assignments > Click the box with three dots > Edit.

A new pop-up window will appear, and you’ll see that the due date is set for the future.

Student notifications

Once the date arrives, your students will see the assignment on their homepage, and they will be notified about the new assignments available for them to complete. Students can find these notifications:

  • in their email inbox,
  • on their Khan Academy account,
  • and, if they’ve downloaded the Khan Academy app, on their phone or tablet.

New students

When new students join your class, they will automatically receive all active assignments. Assignments scheduled for a future date will be sent to new students on the date they are scheduled.

Understanding your students’ Khan Academy experience

We hope this article was helpful for you to learn how to make assignments on Khan Academy. For additional guidance or to share feedback, please reach out to our support team here! We are happy to help.

What types of content can I assign to my students?

Khan Academy offers a wide range of educational content for your students. The content is organized into courses, which are based on specific subjects and include a variety of material.

Courses are organized in the following structure:

  • Courses consist of units and the Course Challenge

  • Units are comprised of lessons and quizzes

  • Lessons are comprised of a mix of articles, videos, and practice exercises Teachers have 4 categories of tasks that their students can work on:

  • Unit Missions:

  • Unit Missions show student progress to teachers in smaller chunks, making it easier to spot specific gaps and see exactly where students need support.

  • Content Assignments:

    • These are one-off tasks designed for students to complete a specific piece of Khan Academy content in a course.
    • Teachers can choose to assign any of the following types of content from a Khan Academy course: article, video, exercise, quiz, unit test, or course challenge.
      • Course challenges are 30 questions long and cover all the skills across the entire course, so they can be helpful to gauge students’ level of understanding at a broader level.
      • Unit tests are a minimum of 9 questions long and cover all the skills in a unit, so can be helpful if students are working towards a Unit mastery goal.
      • Quizzes are a minimum of 5 questions long and cover the skills in a particular lesson.
      • Practice exercises are 4-7 questions long and cover a select group of skills in a lesson.
      • Related resource: How do I create assignments?

  • Writing coach assignment
