Content Update: Big improvements to AP®/College Statistics course

Hello! I’m Jeff on the math content team here at Khan Academy, and I’m happy to share that we’ve updated our AP®/College Statistics course to make it better than ever. Most of the changes are structural, and we think you’ll appreciate the tweaks!

Here are the highlights of what we did:

  • We’ve restructured the course to better align with the official course and exam description from College Board. Previously, this course was aligned in scope with College Board’s official course and exam description for AP® Statistics, but our course units were in a slightly different sequence. This is no longer the case! Our course is now aligned both in scope and sequence with the official course and exam description.
  • Our unit names and sequence make it easier than ever to find content that aligns with what you or your students are learning. The names of our units and lessons largely correspond to the names of units and lessons in the course and exam description, so no matter where you are in the course, you’ll be able to find instructional or practice content for any given topic.
  • We’ve streamlined the course by moving some prerequisite content to our Get ready for AP® Statistics course. We wanted to keep our AP®/College Statistics course focused on just the topics that are in the course and exam description, while also giving teachers and students a curation of the most important prerequisite content. Get ready for AP® Statistics is the new home for topics that aren’t necessarily in the course and exam description for AP® Statistics, but are foundational to learner success in AP® Statistics. You can learn anything!

Jeff Dodds

US mathematics content creator

Content Update: Big improvements to our high school statistics course

Hello! I’m Jeff on the math content team here at Khan Academy, and I’m happy to share that we’ve updated our High school statistics course to make it better than ever. As a former high school math teacher, I’ll admit that teaching statistics was always my favorite, so it was a real treat to spend my time improving this course for you.

Here’s what I’m most excited about when it comes to the new look of our High school statistics course:

  • We completely revamped the course with our freshest and best content. There are a lot of new videos, exercises, and articles in the course that weren’t there before. The course now covers a broader range of topics at a greater depth than before. For example, we now have practice content on calculating expected value and more practice content on interpreting what expected value does (and doesn’t) say.
  • The course is now better aligned to Common Core high school statistics and probability standards. We have new instructional and practice content for standards in topics like study design, probability distributions, and expected value. We also removed some content that’s more appropriate for other grade levels, so learners can focus on what’s most important in a high school course.
  • Video and exercises go beyond rote procedures and contextless data. Learners apply both concepts and procedures in real-world contexts. They’ll wrestle with scenarios like, “Should I buy that protection plan the company offers me when I get a new phone?” You can learn anything!

Content update: New Grammar courses for grades 5–10

This summer, Khan Academy is introducing three new grammar courses designed to help students strengthen essential language skills, become stronger and more confident writers, and prepare for coursework and assessments.

Whether students are looking to build a stronger foundation in grammar, target specific skills, or prepare for standardized tests, these courses provide dedicated instruction and practice across a wide range of grammar and language topics.

This update is part of Khan Academy’s 2026 back-to-school content rollout. You can view the full 2026 Back To School course overview here.

Introducing the new grammar courses

We’re launching three new grade-banded grammar courses:

  • 5th & 6th grade grammar
  • 7th & 8th grade grammar
  • 9th & 10th grade grammar Each course is designed to provide grade-level instruction and practice, with the complexity of skills, examples, and exercises increasing across grade bands.

Together, these courses provide comprehensive coverage of grammar and language skills, from parts of speech and sentence structure to style and tone.

What can students expect?

Each grammar course includes:

  • more than 60 targeted practice exercises
  • additional mixed-practice opportunities
  • instructional articles with student-friendly language and examples
  • engaging grammar videos, with more videos coming soon
  • explanations of common mistakes and misconceptions Students can use these courses in a variety of ways. Some may choose to work through an entire course from beginning to end, while others may focus on specific grammar skills that need extra attention.

These courses can also be used to:

  • prepare for state assessments
  • prepare for the SAT® or ACT®
  • strengthen writing and language skills
  • review concepts taught in class

What can teachers expect?

The new grammar courses are designed to be flexible resources that can support classroom instruction, intervention, enrichment, and independent practice.

Teachers will find:

  • standards-aligned grammar instruction and practice
  • comprehensive coverage of grammar and language skills
  • targeted exercises that make it easier to address specific skill gaps
  • mixed practice opportunities that reinforce multiple concepts
  • instructional resources that can be used alongside existing curriculum and coursework The grade-banded structure also allows students to receive instruction and practice that is appropriate for their grade band while building toward more advanced language skills. Because skills progress within and across grade bands, teachers can easily provide differentiated instruction, assigning practice in a previous grade band to fill gaps or in a more advanced grade band to provide enrichment.

How do these courses fit with existing grammar resources?

If you’re already using Khan Academy’s existing Grammar course, don’t worry—it’s not going anywhere.

The original all-ages Grammar course will remain available to all Khan Academy users.

These new courses provide an additional option for learners and educators who are looking for rigorous, on-level instruction and practice.

Why are these courses being added?

Grammar and language skills play an important role in reading, writing, communication, and academic success across subjects.

These new courses are designed to give students more opportunities to develop and practice essential language skills through accessible instructional resources, targeted practice, and grade-appropriate content.

Whether students are preparing for a test, filling learning gaps, or simply working to become stronger writers, these courses provide flexible pathways to support their goals.

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out.

Content Update: Precalculus

Hi folks,

This year, we poured our love into updating our Precalculus course. We hope this course opens up opportunities for learners to experience success in college mathematics. Here’s some of what you can expect to see.

  • Go deeper with trigonometry. Did you know that trigonometry is useful for far more than finding side lengths and angles in right triangles? Not only can we use it with angles of all sorts (even reflex and negative angles), but we can also model cyclical data like weather patterns with trigonometry.
  • Discover matrices, a flexible math tool we can use for everything from describing geometric transformations to solving systems of equations. Level up further by using matrices to represent and manipulate data like the relationships in a social network.
  • Make decisions with probability. Which ways of making a “random” choice actually give everyone an equal chance and which ways introduce bias? Just how large does the prize need to be (relative to the ticket price and the chances of each outcome) for you to be likely to win more money than you lose by playing a game? Are you a teacher? This part’s for you.

We’ve added depth to the ways learners engage with Common Core advanced standards, drawing together multiple ways of thinking about each concept to reach more learners. For example, learners discover how multiplying complex numbers graphically reveals different properties than multiplying them symbolically.

Our updated unit structure spirals through key topics like trigonometry and inverse functions, helping learners see how they connect other precalculus topics. For example, as learners consider multiple force vectors acting on an object, they strategize about whether to convert vectors to component form or to apply the law of cosines.

Based on teacher requests, we’ve provided optional units on series and limits. We’ve made sure the other course content does not depend on those units, so teachers are free to include them or not while maintaining a coherent course.

You can learn anything!

Charlotte Auen

US mathematics content creator

Introducing Streaks and Levels!

Hey y’all! Khan Academy is thrilled to announce two new mechanics designed to make learning a bit more fun and motivating: Streaks and Levels!

Streaks are designed to promote and celebrate consistency, motivating learners to get at least one skill to Proficient or higher each week.

Levels, on the other hand, are designed to break apart the daunting task of completing an entire course into smaller, more manageable milestones. At the end of each level, users can celebrate with a “level up” that recognizes their progress towards their goals!

The theory behind both of these mechanics is simple yet powerful: regular, consistent practice fosters learning and retention, and “chunking” divides larger, potentially overwhelming goals into smaller, more achievable tasks. Together, we believe that learning at Khan Academy can be more encouraging and rewarding than ever.

Why Streaks?

Motivation isn’t a fixed trait that students either possess or lack; it can grow or shrink depending on one’s environment and strategies. We wanted our new streaks to embody this philosophy to help users create healthy learning habits that align with learning science in a fun and engaging way.

That being said, we didn’t just want any old streak, we wanted each added week to display meaningful learning. We could have had users renew a streak by watching a video or attempting an exercise, but given the importance of practice and our mastery system, we believe getting one skill to proficient or higher is the ideal indicator that users are on the right track to meaningful progress towards their goals (and we have efficacy research studies to back that up).

We want users to be able to look back on their streak at the end of a school year with a deep sense of pride and accomplishment of their hard work and consistency!

Why Levels?

We can imagine that for some of you, the addition of levels could seem a bit unnecessary. Afterall, some learners are already doing hundreds of hours of learning and hundreds of skills per year on Khan Academy, so why make changes to the user experience to “gamify” learning?

Well, the truth is, although some users are already highly motivated to learn on their own, the reality is that many more users would love a way to view and celebrate their progress in a way that helps get the wheels of motivation learning. We believe levels and streaks are a great way for everyone to celebrate their journey on Khan Academy, and they can be the motivation for many students to make Khan Academy a part of their weekly routine.

How Can I Start?

To get started, simply visit your current favorite Khan Academy exercise and start leveling up skills! Or, visit our support article to find out more about streaks and how leveling up works.

Hope these features are an exciting addition to your Khan Academy experience, and we will continue to refine and improve them in the coming weeks and months. Stay tuned!

Posted on behalf of Daniel De Angulo, Senior Product Manager at Khan Academy

Update: 6th grade math from Khan Academy!

Hi, folks!

I’m Charlie from the US math team. I’ve always loved teaching middle school math because it’s so fundamental to the day-to-day mathematical reasoning that we use in our home lives. Ratios are everywhere, whether we’re looking for a fuel-efficient travel route or tweaking the proportions in a recipe so the garlic flavor is strong enough for one family member and weak enough for another. So I’m excited that we got to renew our 6th grade math materials this year.

Are you visiting the 6th grade math course for the first time? Here’s what you can look forward to.

  • Ratios, rates, and percentages all tell us about how two values relate to each other. They show up everywhere, from deciding which juice includes the least filler per serving to finding what percent of voters support a suggested law. Watch for familiar representations, like fraction models and number lines, to help you relate what you already know about fractions and number patterns to these new concepts.

  • Can you take apart and combine shapes to form new ones? If so, you’re ready to take measurement of 2D and 3D figures to a whole new level. If we measure volume with unit cubes, what do we do when the side lengths are smaller than a unit long? How much fabric does it take to cover a tent?

  • If we start at zero, we can keep counting upwards forever. Did you know that we can count backwards from zero, too? Learn to use negative numbers to represent changes in the opposite direction, like when it’s colder than zero degrees or when you dive below sea level. Are you a teacher who’s used our 6th grade math course before? Here’s what’s changed.

  • We revisited major 6th grade topics, especially developing ratio and percentage reasoning and working with negative numbers, to address the areas that the students found most challenging. We’ve provided new scaffolds and showed connections between different representations. We used common student responses to develop incorrectly worked example items, giving students a safe opportunity to recognize mistakes as a normal part of being a mathematician and to learn from them.

  • To encourage mastery and retention of the content, we’ve arranged the content in shorter, spiraling units. For example, the students work with the relationship between fraction multiplication and division early in the course, and they continue to reinforce it later, such as in one-step equations or in finding missing measurements when given the area of a figure.

  • We want to set up students to successfully show what they’ve learned mathematically, without barriers. So we’ve given special attention to reading levels and to usability on an assortment of devices that classrooms use. We hope that you’ll find joy in the patterns and problem solving that await you in our revised 6th grade math course. Please let us know what you think below.

Happy Learning,

Charlie

Update: Assignment Scores CSV Download Feature Release!

Hello Khan Academy Teachers!

If you are a teacher who uses Khan Academy in your classroom, you may want an easy way to transfer your students’ scores from Khan Academy assignments into your personal grade book, or your school’s grade tracking system. Luckily, this is possible through the newly released “Assignment Scores CSV Download” feature!

This feature is on the “Scores” tab under the Assignments dropdown menu and offers a downloadable spreadsheet containing your students’ scores from Khan Academy assignments.

The feature was designed closely with feedback from teachers who use Khan Academy and therefore includes data that was said to be most helpful when adding scores to their grade books.

The CSV includes:

  • Customizable date range:
    • This means you can download only the assignment scores that you need
  • Name and type of the assignment’s content:
    • Name: the title of the assigned content
    • Type: exercise, quiz, unit test, video, or article
  • Due date:
    • The due date you selected when creating the assignment
  • Score or completion status:
    • Practice activities (exercises, quizzes, or unit tests) will have the student’s best score on their columns if the student fully completed the assignment.
    • Videos and articles will have the current completion status: Completed or Not Started Once the CSV is downloaded, the data can be added into your preferred grading system.

For more information about how to use this feature and the spreadsheet once downloaded, please visit this article: How do I download my students’ assignment scores?

While we cannot build a bridge into all varieties of grade books or Learning Management Systems, we hope this feature streamlines your grading processes and helps you lean into using Khan Academy in your classroom(s)!

As always, your thoughts and questions are welcome to be shared with in the Khan Academy Community Forum!

Update: Practice Test changes in Praxis and LSAT

What’s changing?

In an effort to simplify the learning experience for our LSAT and Praxis students, we’ve made some changes to the LSAT and Praxis practice experiences as of April 2022. Specifically:

  • We’ve added a separate tab for practice tests: the Full tests tab. Now, instead of only being able to complete a practice test at the end of a series of stages, you will be able to select which practice test you want to take and when.
  • We’ve removed practice tests from the practice plan. Before, your practice plan was structured using a combination of practice tests and stages. Now, the practice tests will be done separately, in their own Full tests tab, in the order, and at the time of your choosing. The new practice plan will contain only stages and timed mini sections. Stage numbers used to reset after each practice test, but now they reflect the total number of stages you’ve completed. Your progress and work within each stage will not be modified.
  • Because of these new implementations, you may notice that your practice tests names have changed: now, all of our practice tests will follow a regular name order (Practice Test #1, Practice Test #2, Practice Test #3…) even if you removed and re-added them in your schedule.

Why are we making this change?

This change will enable you to better organize your preparation, giving you more control over what you practice and when. Now, instead of having to complete a practice test to continue with your practice plan, you will be able to take practice tests whenever you want. We understand that this will allow for more effective preparation, especially for adult learners with limited time available for their studies.

What about all of my Practice Test scores and schedules?

All of your previous practice test scores and dates will remain in the experience for your reference.

We want to end with a note shouting out to those of you who stayed committed to preparing for the LSAT or the Praxis. We hope that your dedication was personally rewarding, and we thank you for being such an important part of the Khan Academy community.

Overview: Product Offerings for Schools and Districts

How do I purchase Khan Academy Districts Enterprise + Learning Paths for my district?

Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths is a personalized learning program that empowers educators to create differentiated learning experiences. Learning Paths uses MAP Growth scores and Khan Academy’s personalized learning system to provide each student with a custom learning path, while educators get insights and data to inform instruction.

Each student’s personalized learning path includes recommended practice problems, instant feedback, scaffolded help, personalized spiral review and instructional videos and articles.

Note: Learning Paths is only available via to Enterprise partners. It is not available to Enterprise Starter subscribers, however Mappers is available for Enterprise Starter plans.

If your district is interested in purchasing Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths, please access this link for more information.

What is Khan Academy Districts?

Khan Academy Districts is designed to help schools and districts deepen student learning using Khan Academy’s trusted content, administrator reports, powerful teacher tools, and AI-powered tutoring through Khanmigo.

Districts can choose between two plans based on their size and support needs:

  • Khan Academy Districts – Enterprise
  • Khan Academy Districts – Enterprise Starter

What’s included in both plans?

Whether you choose Enterprise or Enterprise Starter, your teachers and students will receive access to:

  • Khanmigo, our AI-powered guide for both learners and educators
  • Student progress tracking, mastery data, and assignment tools
  • Teacher and administrator dashboards with actionable insights
  • Content in core academic subjects, including math, science, ELA, and more Both plans are designed to support effective classroom instruction with Khan Academy and provide meaningful data for teachers and school leaders.

Sal Khan is the founder and CEO of Khan Academy, a global nonprofit that provides free education to more than 200 million people worldwide. He’s also Vision Steward and a board member of TED, a nonprofit conference and media organization with a mission to discover and spread ideas.

Khan Academy was founded in 2008. It began as a way for Sal to remotely tutor his cousins in math. Since then, the organization has grown into a platform available in more than 50 languages that reaches students and teachers in more than 190 countries. Khan Academy partners with more than 600 school districts in the United States as well as school systems in eight countries to provide instruction, practice, assessment, and AI-supported learning in a single, connected experience that reaches 7 million students.

Sal is the founder of the nonprofits Schoolhouse.world, Khan Lab School, and Khan World School, and the author of The One World Schoolhouse and Brave New Words, and the co-author of Teaching Students to Use AI Ethically & Responsibly. His forthcoming book, expected in 2027, examines how AI will transform the future of work and how societies can build learning systems that help people adapt, learn, and thrive.

Privacy and Permissions

Does my child account automatically update to an adult account when I turn 13 years old?

Child account restrictions will be turned off automatically once you turn 13 years old only if you have set your date of birth when creating the account.

If the date of birth was not added while setting up your account, and the account was set as a child account, you will not be able to change this on your own. In this instance, you will have to contact Khan Academy support.

Please use the Report a problem button in the Help Center to send a request. When sending the request, you will be asked to select the type of problem you are reporting; please choose the I need to adjust a birthday option and provide the following information through the form:

  • Your correct birthday

  • Your profile URL

  • The year that you will graduate from high school

  • The number of energy points that are on your account

  • Your account username or email See also:

  • How are child accounts different from regular accounts?

  • How can I edit my child’s settings?

  • How do I reset my child’s password?

How can I cite material from Khan Academy?

We occasionally get questions about how to cite material found on Khan Academy. Journals, schools, and teachers might require specific formats, or may have their own rules about how they wish citations to be recorded.

If you don’t know which style guide to follow, Khan Academy recommends using the current format found in the Chicago Manual of Style (US).

A particularly good source for determining the correct way to cite material found on Khan Academy for APA, MLA, AMA, or Chicago style is owl.english.purdue.edu (the Purdue University Online Writing Lab [OWL]).

Most style guides require the same basic information: date(s) published and/or accessed, author(s), title, and URL. For some parts of Khan academy, the web page is dynamic: what you will see depends on your personal account (for example, a certain URL may lead to one exercise for me but another for you). If you need to refer to a particular exercise problem, because the URL is not enough to know which one, be sure to describe the exercise in your writing.

Below are examples of some types of citations for Khan Academy material using the Chicago Manual of Style. The examples are placed in boxes for clarity only.

The Entire Website

[Khan Academy, in italics], accessed [date in appropriate format], [URL to homepage, without https://]

Example if the site was accessed on the 24th of January 2017

Khan Academy. Accessed January 24, 2017. khanacademy.org.

Text

[author if specified, by Last name, First name.], [article name as it appears in the menu, in quotations marks], [paragraph if indicated, by par. or pars. and number], [Khan Academy in italics], accessed [appropriate date format], [URL, without https://]

Example of use of an entire article with no mention of the author

“Planning a programming project.” Khan Academy. Accessed January, 24.2017. khanacademy.org.

Example of a paragraph from an Art History article with specified authors

Harris, Beth and Zucker, Steven. “A brief history of western culture, par. 1.” Khan Academy. Accessed January 24, 2017. khanacademy.org.

Videos and video talk-throughs

[producer if specified, by last name, first name.], [video name as it appears in the menu, in quotations marks], [performer if different from producer], [medium, in parentheses], [if appropriate, time in (hours):minutes: seconds at which the issue occurs followed by /][running time in (hours):minutes: seconds], [Producing organization or company in italics], accessed [appropriate date format], [URL, without https://]

Example of an entire video with no author

“Systems of equations number of solutions: fruit prices 1 and 2” (video). Khan Academy. Accessed January 24, 2017. khanacademy.org.

Example of a point in a video with known author and content not produced by Khan Academy

When the content was not produced by Khan Academy, the Khan Academy web page is treated as a container.

Ross, Nancy, “Ancient Near Eastern and ancient Egyptian art,” performed by Ydraw (video) 0:30/6:17. Utah System of Higher Education. Accessed January 24, 2017. khanacademy.org.

CS programs

[coder by Nickname], [program name, in quotations marks], [type of program, in parentheses], [Khan Academy, in italics], accessed [appropriate date format], [URL, without https://]

Example:

Brian French. “sphere” (user generated JS animation). Khan Academy. Accessed January 24, 2017. khanacademy.org.

Images

For photos of artworks see A photo of an artwork, photographer not mentioned.

For simplicity’s sake, all images are treated as if the Khan Academy page they are on is only the container. The particulars of the image come first. Then, a line break and an indentation and particulars as if a text was cited.

[Last name, First name of the artist if known], [Title if known], [medium if known, in parentheses], [year created if known], [where found if known]

[Last name, First name of the author of the article if known], [article name as in the menu, in quotation marks], [where on the page the image is inserted], [Khan Academy in, italics], accessed [appropriate date format], [URL without https://]

If neither artist nor title is known, use

Untitled image, [medium if known, in parentheses], [year created if known], [where found if known]

[Last name, First name of the author of the article if known], [article name as in the menu, in quotation marks], [where on the page the image is inserted], [Khan Academy in, italics], accessed [appropriate date format], [URL without https://]

Images on Khan Academy can be created by Khan Academy staff, modified by Khan Academy staff from another image, or be public domain images. Modified images and images from the public domain are credited. As images on Khan Academy rarely have a title, they must be referred to by description and where they are found.

Example of an image with no artist name and no title

Untitled image. “The scientific method” under “Scientific method: Failure to toast, 4. Make predictions.” Khan Academy. Accessed January 24, 2017. khanacademy.org.

Example of a modified image that is credited

Untitled image modified from Zifan, Ali. “Prokaryote cell.” National Institutes of Health. Accessed January 24, 2017. khanacademy.org.

What can I do to protect my privacy while using Khan Academy?

At Khan Academy, we do our best to provide a safe and secure online environment where everyone can feel welcome and comfortable learning. And you can help with that too!

Here are some of our recommendations on what you can do to protect your privacy while learning online.

Always log off from shared devices

When learning online, you might be using a device that other people have access to. This could include family members, other students from your school, or even people you don’t know if you are using a public device.

If you’re using a shared device, always log off as soon as you’re done using Khan Academy. This is an important way to protect your account while also keeping your progress safe and accurate.

To log out of your account on a browser, click on your name at the upper right-hand corner and choose Log out.

Another option is to visit our direct logout page www.khanacademy.org/logout.

You’ll be logged out instantly!

On the mobile app, tap on the gear icon at the upper right-hand corner and choose Sign out.

Usernames should never include real names

Choosing a username for your account allows you to pick a unique set of characters that can be used to log in to Khan Academy.

However, it’s important to remember that it could be viewed by other users, such as when you post a question or an answer in our Community Forums. Because of this, avoid using real names, nicknames, or any other information that could be used to identify you or someone else when choosing a username for your account.

For more details on choosing a unique username, check out this article.

Make your password uniquely yours

A password is a perfect complement to a username. And just like your username, it should be strong and unique to you!

Creating and maintaining a strong password is one of the first steps to help ensure the security of your account. In general, try to combine uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols to create a password that only you will know.

See this article on the requirements for creating your Khan Academy password.

Be thoughtful about what you post

The community is a great place to ask for help, answer questions, or discuss the content to learn even more!

As members of such a helpful community, we are all expected to be respectful to one another at all times so everyone can feel comfortable learning. This means you should be thoughtful with what you post, never start or reply to off-topic posts (downvote or flag them instead) and, never post or ask for personal information in your profile or comments. In general, don’t share your name, personal details, or any kind of information that isn’t appropriate to share publicly anywhere. And remember: if you wouldn’t be comfortable with a parent or teacher reading what you’re writing, it’s best not to post it.

You can check out our Community Guidelines for more details on what’s okay and not okay to post.

Learn more about how to keep safe

You know the drill: here at Khan Academy, you can learn anything! Why not learn more about how to keep safe when learning online?

Our Online data security course unit is a great place to start learning about data security principles, including recognizing personally identifiable information (PII) and other data that can be tracked online.

We also encourage you to check out our Privacy Policy, where you can read more about how we protect information, including details about Transparency and your choices, and Your account settings.

Finally, you can learn more about the Student Privacy Pledge signed by Khan Academy, an important step in safeguarding student privacy.

Why was I banned?

In general, users who persistently violate Khan Academy’s Community Guidelines may be banned from community activities by a Guardian. If you’d like specific information about why your account was banned, or if you’d like to submit a ban appeal, please fill out and submit a Ban Appeal Form.

A Guardian will review your request and respond to you via a Guardian message on your profile. Please note that we receive lots of ban appeal requests, so it may take several days to receive a response.

Readiness Check

Does the Readiness Check affect my students’ mastery, streaks, or Gems?

The Readiness Check includes two separate experiences:

  • the Readiness Check assessment
  • the personalized Readiness exercises students complete afterward These affect student progress differently.

Does the Readiness Check assessment affect student progress?

No.

Completing the Readiness Check does not affect a student’s:

  • Mastery levels
  • Gems
  • Streak
  • Skills to Proficient progress The Readiness Check is used only to identify prerequisite skills that students may need to practice.

Do Readiness exercises affect student progress?

Yes.

After students complete the Readiness Check, they’ll receive personalized Readiness exercises. These exercises contribute to student progress just like other practice exercises on Khan Academy.

Feature

Do Readiness exercises count?

Mastery

✅ Yes (up to Proficient)

Gems

✅ Yes

Streak

✅ Yes

Skills to Proficient

✅ Yes

Students can also earn a Gems bonus for completing their entire Readiness Mission.

Can students reach Mastered through Readiness exercises?

No.

Readiness exercises can help students reach the Proficient level for a skill.

To reach Mastered, students must continue demonstrating their understanding through other mastery activities on Khan Academy.

Quick reference

Answer

No.

Do students earn Gems for Readiness exercises?

Yes.

Does the Readiness Check count toward a streak?

No.

Do Readiness exercises count toward a streak?

Yes.

Can students reach Mastered through Readiness exercises?

No. They can reach Proficient.

How do I assign a Readiness Check to my class?

Assigning a Readiness Check allows your students to complete a one-time assessment that identifies prerequisite math skills they may need to review before beginning grade-level work.

Once students complete the assessment, Khan Academy automatically creates personalized practice based on each student’s results. You don’t need to configure or assign any follow-up work.

To assign a Readiness Check

  • Open the class where you want to create the assignment.
  • Click + Add assignment.
  • Select Readiness Check.
  • Choose the class or students you want to assign it to.
  • Click Assign. After you assign the Readiness Check, it will appear for your selected students. Students can begin the assessment whenever they’re ready.

Do I need to choose a grade level or version?

No.

There is only one Readiness Check. Each student automatically receives questions based on their rostered grade level, so you don’t need to choose a grade, course, or version before assigning it.

Why don’t I see the Readiness Check option?

Readiness Check is only available to users in a USA Partner District (KAD).

If you believe your class meets these requirements but you still don’t see the option, contact your school or district administrator.

Can I assign the Readiness Check more than once?

Students can complete the Readiness Check once per school year.

If a student has already completed the Readiness Check in another class, they won’t be asked to take it again. Instead, you’ll be able to view that student’s existing results in your class’s Readiness Check report.

When should I assign the Readiness Check?

The Readiness Check is intended to be assigned near the beginning of the school year, before students begin working through grade-level content.

Completing the assessment early gives students time to begin personalized practice on prerequisite skills while continuing with their regular class assignments.

What happens after I assign it?

Students will be prompted to take the Readiness CheckAfter students complete the Readiness Check.

Once the student completes it:

  • Each student receives a personalized Readiness Mission based on the skills they need to practice
  • Related gap practice is automatically added to students’ Daily and Weekly Missions when appropriate
  • You can monitor student completion and review class results from the Readiness Check report You don’t need to assign additional practice or manually manage students’ Readiness Missions.

How do I view my students’ Readiness Check results?

After students begin completing the Readiness Check, you can view their results from your class’s Readiness Check report.

The report helps you monitor student completion and identify the prerequisite skills your class may need to review.

To open the Readiness Check report

  • Go to the class you want to view
  • Go to reports
  • Click the Readiness Check tab.

What information is included in the report?

The Readiness Check report includes two types of information:

Student completion

At the top of the report, you can see how many students have completed the Readiness Check.

This helps you quickly identify which students have started or finished the assessment.

Readiness skills

Once students complete the Readiness Check, the report displays the prerequisite skills identified for your class.

For each skill, you can see:

  • which students need additional practice
  • each student’s current mastery level
  • class-wide trends to help identify common areas for review

Can I view results for individual students?

Yes.

The Readiness Check report lets you see which prerequisite skills each student may need to practice, making it easier to understand individual learning needs as well as class-wide trends.

Where else can I see Readiness Check information?

Readiness Check information is also available in the Assignments tab.

Readiness Check results are not currently included in the Activity Report or Skills Report.

What happens if a student already completed the Readiness Check in another class?

Students only complete the Readiness Check once per school year.

If a student has already completed it in another class, you’ll see that student’s existing results in your Readiness Check report instead of asking them to complete the assessment again.

Readiness Check overview for teachers

The Readiness Check is an adaptive assessment designed to be used at the beginning of the school year. It helps you understand which skills from earlier grades your students may benefit from practicing before beginning grade-level work.

When students complete the Readiness Check, Khan Academy automatically creates personalized practice to help them strengthen those skills alongside their current coursework.

The Readiness Check is designed to guide personalized practice. It isn’t a formal diagnostic or standardized assessment.

How it works

The Readiness Check is designed to be simple for both teachers and students.

Teachers assign the Readiness Check once. Students complete the assessment. After that, Khan Academy automatically creates personalized practice and adds it alongside students’ regular lessons.

How does the Readiness Check work?

The Readiness Check is a single adaptive assessment with approximately 36 questions.

As students answer questions, the assessment adjusts to their responses:

  • Students who answer correctly receive more challenging questions.
  • Students who need additional support receive questions that help identify which skills from earlier grades they would benefit from practicing. The Readiness Check only includes content below a student’s current grade level. Students won’t receive questions from their current course or more advanced courses.

What happens after students finish?

Once a student completes the Readiness Check, Khan Academy automatically:

  • Identifies skills from earlier grades the student may benefit from practicing.
  • Creates a personalized Readiness Mission with practice exercises for those skills.
  • Adds Readiness exercises to the student’s Daily and Weekly Missions when they’re most helpful. No additional setup is required from the teacher.

Learn more

The Readiness Check is just one part of the readiness experience. To learn more, see:

  • How do I view my students’ Readiness Check results?
  • Does the Readiness Check affect my students’ mastery, streaks, or Gems? If you still need assistance, visit the Khan Academy Help Center or contact Khan Academy Support

What are Readiness Missions and Readiness exercises?

After a student completes the Readiness Check, Khan Academy automatically creates personalized practice based on the student’s results.

This personalized practice appears in two places:

  • A Readiness Mission, which includes all of the student’s personalized Readiness exercises.
  • Readiness exercises that appear in the student’s Daily and Weekly Missions to help reinforce prerequisite skills before related grade-level work. You don’t need to assign or manage either of these. They’re created automatically after a student completes the Readiness Check.

What is a Readiness Mission?

A Readiness Mission is a personalized collection of practice exercises based on the prerequisite skills identified in a student’s Readiness Check.

Students can work through their Readiness Mission at their own pace while continuing to complete their assigned coursework.

The Readiness Mission appears on the student’s dashboard after they complete the Readiness Check.

What are Readiness exercises?

Readiness exercises are personalized practice exercises that help students strengthen prerequisite skills.

In addition to appearing in a student’s Readiness Mission, Readiness exercises may also appear in the student’s Daily and Weekly Missions.

When a Readiness exercise is related to an upcoming assignment, it appears before the assigned work so students can review the prerequisite skill first.

If shown in the student’s Daily or Weekly Mission, Readiness exercises are identified with a Readiness badge.

How many Readiness exercises will students receive?

The number of Readiness exercises depends on each student’s Readiness Check results.

Students who demonstrate strong prerequisite skills may not receive a Readiness Mission. Students with more identified prerequisite skills to review will receive additional personalized practice.

What types of content are included?

Readiness Missions include practice exercises only.

They do not include videos or articles.

Can I edit a student’s Readiness Mission?

No.

Readiness Missions are generated automatically from each student’s Readiness Check results. Teachers can’t add, remove, or edit individual Readiness exercises.

How should students use their Readiness Mission?

Students should work through their Readiness Mission alongside their regular assignments throughout the school year.

The personalized Readiness exercises are designed to reinforce prerequisite skills while students continue learning grade-level content.

If you still need assistance, visit the Khan Academy Help Center or contact Khan Academy Support

Rostering Guidelines

Guide to Co-teaching for Khan Academy Districts Teachers

Classes that are part of a Khan Academy Districts partnership are able to have multiple teachers connected to them. This feature gives you more flexibility to coordinate with colleagues and support the academic progress of your shared students.

The primary teacher is the main teacher a class is tied to in the roster. Other teachers added to the class are considered co-teachers. Each class can have up to 9 co-teachers, and Co-teachers can do most actions the primary teacher can in a class.

Co-teachers can:

  • Access all student data for the classes in which they are added as co-teachers.

  • Edit students’ settings if they are under 13 years old.

  • Assign content and create Unit Missions

  • Edit and delete assignments and Unit Missions.

  • Access all teacher reports to monitor student progress. Co-teachers canNOT:

  • Receive weekly class emails from Khan Academy

  • Be included in the Khan Academy Districts Administrator Progress reports, or the downloadable CSVs. Co-teachers are on the activation reports, though.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I add a co-teacher to my Khan Academy classes?

Co-teachers must be designated in your district’s Clever or ClassLink roster to be reflected on Khan Academy. This means that, in order to have a co-teacher for a class, the information must be added by your district in Clever or ClassLink.

How do I know if I have a co-teacher added to my Khan Academy classes?

Go to your class dashboard and click Settings. In the class settings, you can view any additional teachers with access to a particular class and each teacher’s role.

Do the standard Khan Academy rostering limits also apply to classes with co-teachers?

Yes. As explained in this article, some features might load slowly or be disabled when primary or co-teachers have over 100 students in a single class or 1,000 students across all of their classes.

What happens if a co-teacher is removed from my class?

If a co-teacher is removed from the class, the class remains intact as long as the primary teacher is not changed.

Can I have more than one co-teacher for my class(es)?

Yes, you can! There can be up to 9 co-teachers on 1 class. However, this cannot be done by the teacher on their Khan Academy account. The co-teachers must be designated in your district’s class roster before they can be reflected on Khan Academy.

A co-teacher deleted an assignment I created. How do I get it back?

When an assignment is deleted, it cannot be recovered by any of the class’s teachers or by the Support Team at Khan Academy. Deleting an assignment will remove it from both your assignments page and your students’ assignments pages permanently.

How can we see which teacher created an assignment?

At the moment, teachers cannot see which teacher created or deleted an assignment.

My district has Khan Academy Districts. Can I have co-teaching in my non-district-synced classes, too?

Only classes synced with your district as part of the Khan Academy Districts program can be shared among multiple teachers.

This co-teaching feature relies upon the flow of rostering information from your district’s SIS to your Khan Academy Districts classes. Without the district connection, it is not possible to add a co-teacher at this time.

We hope this article gave you helpful information about the co-teaching functionality on Khan Academy. Have more questions? Reach out to our Support team here. We’re happy to help.

How can I add an administrator to my district using Khan Academy’s in-product admin rostering feature?

If you’re unable to add administrators through your rostering system (such as Clever or ClassLink), you can manually control administrator access directly from your Khan Academy administrator dashboard.

Important: Whenever possible, roster administrators through your SIS-connected system (like Clever or ClassLink) to minimize manual work. Admins added manually will not be automatically updated or removed if changes occur in your SIS.

Where to find the in-product admin rostering tools

  • To begin, log in to your Khan Academy administrator account and go to the Manage Administrators section in the “settings” tab from the overview menu on the Administrator Dashboard

  • If you are not seeing this option, you do not have the required permissions to add other administrators. From the Manage Administrators page, you can:

  • See who has administrator access, which school site(s) they have administrator access for, and their roster source (Clever, ClassLink, or Khan Academy in-product)

  • See each administrator’s permissions

    • View = can access the administrator dashboard
    • Manage = can access the dashboard and the Manage Users page for their school site(s)

  • Resend their email invitation

  • Add, edit, or remove administrator access

How to add a new administrator

  • Click the blue “Invite Users” button.
  • Fill in the required fields, including:
    • Administrator’s name, email address, and school(s) they should manage. Select all schools for district-level access
    • If the person is already rostered as a teacher, make sure their email matches the one in Clever or ClassLink.
    • Use the “User can invite and manage administrators for the assigned schools” permission sparingly, as it allows the user to edit admin access for the assigned school(s).
    • If your district is part of a broader state or regional partnership, you may see another step asking you to select a role for the administrator you are inviting.
      • Full partnership role: has access to all the regions and schools in the partnership
      • Region role: will have access to all the schools in the region
      • School role: will have access to the school(s) you select for them in a particular region
  • Click the blue “Send Invite” button. The administrator will receive an email to log in and access the admin dashboard.
  • Note: Admins added through this manual method will need to log in using Google Single Sign-On or a username and password. They won’t be able to access the admin dashboard through Clever or ClassLink.

What happens when I invite a new administrator?

  • Once you click “Send Invite”, users will be sent an email from noreply@khanacademy.org with the title “Action needed: Confirm your Khan Academy Administrator account”
    • Please have folks check their spam and junk folders if they are not seeing the email from us.
  • Users will click the blue “Confirm your account” button
  • Users will select to create a new Khan Academy account with the email address you’ve invited, or log into an Khan Academy existing account.
    • If they log into an existing Khan Academy account, the email address you invited will be added to it, and that account will receive the additional administrator privileges.

How to edit or remove administrator access

  • On the Manage Administrators page, click the three dots next to an administrator
  • Choose one of the following options:
    • Edit their information
    • Resend the invitation email
    • Delete their administrator access If the administrator was rostered as a teacher through Clever and then given admin access manually, you’ll need to remove their access both in the SIS and on the Manage Administrators page if they leave the district.

Tips for effective administrator roster management

  • Keep your administrator list up to date at the start and end of each school year
  • Coordinate with your SIS team to avoid duplicate or outdated administrator records
  • Grant “manage users” permission only to those who need it—this role allows someone to make changes across your school’s user base If you need help with managing administrator access, please contact your Districts Success Manager or submit a ticket to the Support team. We are here and happy to help!

How do I set up rostering with Khan Academy and Learning Paths?

If your district is getting ready to use Khan Academy with Learning Paths, you’ll need to set up rostering through Clever and connect your NWEA MAP Growth data. This process involves a few key steps to make sure teachers and students can access everything smoothly.

Step 1: Set up your district on Clever

Clever is free for districts, and it’s the first step to rostering with Learning Paths. Visit the Clever website to begin your setup.

Important: The first sync between your Student Information System (SIS) and Clever can take a few weeks. Start early to avoid delays in launching Learning Paths.

Step 2: Roster with Clever for MAP Growth

To sync MAP Growth RIT scores into Learning Paths:

  • Make sure your students are rostered with NWEA in Clever.
  • Students must be rostered using their district email addresses. Note: Students need at least one MAP Growth test result in the last three terms to receive a RIT score in Learning Paths.

Step 3: Add NWEA Instructional Connections

In your NWEA account, add Khan Academy / Learning Paths as an Instructional Connections Provider.

  • Be sure to select each school that will be using Learning Paths.
  • You can follow NWEA’s instructions for adding Instructional Connections.

Step 4: Request applications in Clever

Request access to both the Khan Academy and Learning Paths applications in Clever.

Note: If you don’t see them, please contact Khan Academy Rostering support for help.

Step 5: Set up Clever sharing rules for Learning Paths

Be sure to only share:

  • Math classes
  • (Optional) Advisory/Intervention classes for relevant grades Important: Learning Paths supports content through Algebra 1 and Geometry.

All teachers and students must have:

  • A district email address
  • Date of birth entered for students

Step 6: Add co-teachers in SIS (if applicable)

If interventionists, or other staff, need access to Math classes:

  • Add them in your SIS as co-teachers.
  • Each class can have up to 9 co-teachers.

Step 7: Set up Clever sharing rules for Khan Academy

Use the same sharing rules as Learning Paths, and also:

  • Include any additional subjects or grades that may use Khan Academy or Khanmigo. For example, if grades 5–8 will use Khan Academy for all subjects:

  • Include Khanmigo access if your district is using it.

Step 8: Confirm student license coverage

Make sure the students you share in both Clever and Khan Academy are included in your student license agreement.

Step 9: Add sharing rules for staff

Don’t forget to include non-teaching staff—such as administrators or coaches—who need access to reports or data.

Step 10: Configure the Clever portal

Finally, make sure both the Khan Academy and Learning Paths icons appear in your Clever portal.

Teachers and students can use either icon to access both platforms.

✅ Once these steps are complete, your district will be fully rostered and ready to use Khan Academy with Learning Paths.

How do I transition from the free Clever Library app to Khan Academy Districts?

This is a guide for teachers to transition using Khan Academy from Clever Library to Khan Academy Districts.

Khan Academy Districts provides several benefits for teachers:

  • Automatically updated class rosters
  • Multiple professional learning opportunities tailored to needs
  • Dedicated Success Manager for implementation guidance
  • Prioritized Tech Support by submitting a ticket here.

What is different about your teacher account when you are part of Khan Academy Districts?

  • Class rosters are automatically updated nightly. Teachers cannot manually update class rosters.
  • Class sections and rosters will appear automatically, in addition to classes that have been created manually or through your installation of Khan Academy via Clever Library.
  • Teacher accounts will be connected to a district email account.

What is the same or different about student accounts when they are part of Khan Academy Districts?

  • Students still go through their Clever portal to access their Khan Academy accounts.
  • Class rosters will automatically appear alphabetically in “last name, first name” format.
  • Student accounts will all be attached to a district email account.
  • Your roster will be updated nightly as students enter and leave your class.

All student progress will be accurately attributed to all of the student’s teachers and administrators of record.

Instructions

Step 1: Go to Clever and select Khan Academy.
  • Log into Clever as you usually would, with your school district username and password.
  • Go to the “More Apps (District)” section in your Clever Portal (you may have to scroll down to find it), then select the Khan Academy tile.
  • Since you have an existing Khan Academy account associated with your school email, you will be brought directly to your homepage after clicking on the Khan Academy tile. Welcome back to Khan Academy!
Step 2: Clean up the classes on your Teacher Dashboard.

Since you’ve used Khan Academy through Clever Library in the past, you may see duplicated or older classes in your Teacher Dashboard now.

We recommend setting aside 10-15 minutes to clean up your Teacher Dashboard classes.

  • You can delete classes added by Clever Library.
  • You cannot delete classes added by Khan Academy Districts - you’ll need them; they’re current. When you delete a class created by Clever Library, you will lose all assignments and course mastery goals you’ve made for the students in that class. Students will not lose their mastery progress, but their assignment scores will get deleted.

Step 3: Delete any classes added by Clever Library.

Click into the name of the class you want to delete.

On the left-hand side navigation bar, under ADMIN, click on Settings.

Scroll down to the bottom of the Settings page until you see a red button that says “Delete this class.”

When you’re ready, press the “Delete this class” button to delete the class.

How does automated rostering work for Khan Academy Districts accounts?

Khan Academy accounts who are part of a partner district in the Khan Academy Classroom program have access to automated rostering via Clever and ClassLink.

Please note: this article does not apply to Enterprise Starter customers. Please view this article to learn more how rostering works for Enterprise Starter plans.

Here are some fundamental aspects of how Khan Academy Classroom accounts receive roster information from Clever and ClassLink:

  1. The Khan Academy system syncs with Clever and ClassLink every weeknight.
  • Changes made to your district’s Clever or ClassLink roster need to sync overnight in order to show up on Khan Academy.
  • If the changes you make to your Clever or ClassLink roster are more than 50% of the existing totals on Khan Academy, the roster change will not go through and a member of the Khan Academy team will be in contact with you to ensure those changes are intended.
  • For more information on how to set up your roster data on Clever and ClassLink, check out these articles: Khan Academy Districts + Clever set-up guide and Khan Academy Districts + ClassLink set-up guide
  1. Khan Academy occasionally pauses rostering:
  • Rostering is paused to honor the winter holidays and office closures. These include: Thanksgiving and the last two weeks of December through early January.
    • We will attempt to proactively communicate with districts in cases where rosters are paused. Any roster changes made over the holiday breaks will be reflected on Khan Academy when the Khan Academy offices reopen.
  • Note: We may pause rostering over the summer break to ensure that students and teachers maintain access to Khan Academy during this time. However, typically, your rosters will continue to process nightly throughout the summer. Please let your District Success Manager know if your district plans to roster summer school classes.
  1. The rostering process does not automatically create Khan Academy accounts for users
  • If there is an existing Khan Academy account that matches the user’s rostered email address and/or Clever/ClassLink ID:
    • That Khan Academy account likely will be automatically “activated” and receive the roster information from Clever or ClassLink on it.
  • If there is not a matching Khan Academy account:
    • Users will need to go through the activation process.
    • This process prompts users to either create a new Khan Academy account with their district-synced email address, or connect a personal Khan Academy account which they will now also use as their district-synced account.
  1. Once the Clever and ClassLink data syncs with Khan Academy, classes and student rosters are updated automatically
  • On these classes you’ll see:
    • The District name
    • The # of average skills to proficient
    • How many students in those classes have activated their Khan Academy accounts.
  1. Classes enter a 10 day grace period at the end of the school year

After the school year ends, district-synced classes are marked for deletion and enter a grace period before they are permanently removed.

During this grace period, the classes remain visible in Khan Academy, giving your district time to review or update roster information before the classes are deleted.

Below is some additional information about Khan Academy Districts classes and accounts:

  • Teachers cannot add or remove students from district-synced classes.
  • Teachers cannot edit district-synced students’ display names on Khan Academy.
  • The Google Classroom integration cannot be used on a district-synced class.
  • Students cannot remove district teachers or classes from their Khan Academy accounts. We hope this information was helpful as you continue on your Khan Academy Districts journey! If you need additional assistance, please reach out to your Districts Success Manager, or contact the Khan Academy Support Team.

I am rostered for both Learning Paths and Khan Academy Districts. Which app do I access on my district’s Clever Portal?

All teachers and students rostered for Learning Paths will also be rostered for Khan Academy Districts.

These district users will see both the Learning Paths and Khan Academy apps in their district’s Clever Portal.

Note: Learning Paths can only be rostered in Clever at this time.

If you see both apps on your district’s Clever Portal, you can click either app and will be brought to the same Khan Academy account.

If you, or your student, do not see the Learning Paths app but should, please report this issue to your school administrator.

Khan Academy Districts + ClassLink set-up guide

Please note: This guide is a technical resource for districts who are already Khan Academy Districts partners and are preparing to share their data with Khan Academy. In order to become a partner, please visit the Khan Academy Districts website and click the “Request a Demo” button in the top righthand corner to get connected with the team.

Khan Academy + ClassLink set-up guide

Once your District is a Khan Academy Districts partner, syncing your organization’s Student Information System data with ClassLink is quick and easy.

Note: districts rostering with ClassLink cannot use Data Guard in ClassLink to obfuscate PII (first name, last name, email address, class name) for students,teachers, and classes.

Prepare your district’s Student Information System to sync with ClassLink

Once your district is set up on Classlink, please ensure your SIS meets the requirements for the below categories:

  • Enrollment dates:

  • Please ensure your Teachers, students and classes have an active Enrollment Begin or End Date. Those with enrollment dates in the past will not get synced to Khan Academy, and those with Enrollment dates in the future will not be rostered until that date.

  • Enrollments also require the following data: org_id, class sourcedID, student_id, begin_date, and end_date

  • Classes:

  • Ensure that the classes in the SIS reflect the classes your district wants to roster for the current term and include the following data: org_id, class sourcedID, teacher_id, name, grade, and subject. Please only share the current semester’s classes with Khan Academy.

  • Please let your rostering specialist know if you anticipate more than one section per class period for each teacher. - Co-teachers: Classes can contain one primary teacher and up to nine co-teachers. This needs to be set up in your SIS to sync with ClassLink. Ensure that individual classes have a primary teacher = true indicated. Contact your SIS provider with questions about setting up co-teachers.

  • Please note: co-teachers will not show up on all the Khan Academy Administrator reports. - Co-teachers are not shown on the Progress Reports, or downloadable csv reports. - If you use block scheduling with multiple teachers teaching the same group of students, we recommend giving each teacher their own Khan Academy class, rather than the teachers all sharing one class.

  • Teacher email address:Khan Academy uses the teacher’s email address as an identifier to give teachers access to their correct district account. Ensure that each teacher has an accurate district email address in the SIS. The additional data required for teachers is: district, name, org_id, sis_id, email, title, and role.

  • Student email address: Khan Academy uses the student’s email address as an identifier to give students access to their correct district account. Ensure that each student has an accurate district email address in the SIS. Other data requirements for students are: district, name, org_id, sis_id, student sourcedID, date of birth*, email, and grade.

    • Student date of birth: Khan Academy has two levels of permissions for student accounts under FERPA and NY Section 2-d regulations. Students under 13 have limited permissions on discussion posts and computer science projects. Students over 13 do not have these limitations. Ensure all students have a date of birth in the SIS that is shared with ClassLink.
    • Student enrollments:
    • Ensure that students are enrolled in at least one section. Students must be enrolled in at least one section (class) to activate their Khan Academy Districts account.
  1. Organizations

Be sure that the Orgs section in the SIS includes the org_id and the org name.

Authorize and Set Up Khan Academy in ClassLink

  • Add the Khan Academy Application in ClassLink: Ensure that data sharing is enabled and that Demographics are also shared. Khan Academy’s rostering team will receive a notification when you’ve added the application for your district.

  • Additional resource: How to add an application to your ClassLink Launchpad

  • Set sharing rules Share the correct teachers, students, and administrators per your implementation and service agreement. We recommend sharing by grade level and subject. (See considerations below on how to avoid oversharing section data.)

  • Add Administrators: Add administrators in ClassLink to give access to the administrator dashboards in Khan Academy. Ensure that administrators are associated with at least one Org that has students and classes associated with it. Administrators who are associated with district offices won’t see usage data.

  • Add the Khan Academy app in your District’s Management Console Assign the Khan Academy app to only those students that are part of your district’s implementation. If you previously created a link to the free Khan Academy site on your district’s launchpad, make sure that the participating students will not have access to that link.

Considerations

Teachers or students with more than one email address:

District users will activate their accounts using a district email address. If your teachers or students have more than one email address, please inform our rostering operations team as early as possible so we can develop an activation plan.

Avoid oversharing section data in ClassLink:

Please only share data for sections (classes) included in Khan Academy’s implementation for your district. When sharing data in ClassLink, please ensure that elective classes like P.E., Art, Chorus, and Band are not included. Rostering these sections will confuse teachers who likely won’t use Khan Academy as part of their instruction.

Student Grade Levels:

Please note: students who are rostered in grade levels outside the standard K-12 range, such as grades 13, 14, or PostGraduate, their grade level will be shown as “Other” in Khan Academy administrator reports.

If you have any questions, please contact your Districts Success Manager, or submit a ticket to our support team here.
