What happens to a class that is no longer active in the Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths program?

Your school district might add, remove, or replace classes from your roster on Clever during the school year. When these changes cause an existing district-synced class to no longer be included on the roster shared by the district on Clever, the class is also removed from the teacher’s Khan Academy account.

Only unused classes will be removed at first. If you have previously used any classes (by setting Learning Paths Placements or creating Assignments, for example), they will remain in your account for a grace period of 10 days, and you will be able to check any past work during this time. Once the grace period has expired, the classes will be removed from the account for good, and any assignments and scores data will no longer be available.

Important: Because these classes are no longer connected with the district, data relating to them cannot be recovered, so keep that in mind when you prepare for the next term!

All class changes mentioned above follow specific requirements set by the district and the official roster set on Clever.

What happens to a class that is no longer active in the Khan Academy Districts program?

Your school district might add, remove, or replace classes from your roster on Clever during the school year. When these changes cause an existing district-synced class to no longer be included on the roster shared by the district on Clever, the class is also removed from the teacher’s Khan Academy account.

Only unused classes will be removed at first. If you have previously used any classes (by creating Assignments, for example), they will remain in your account for a grace period of 7 days, and you will be able to check any past work during this time. Once the grace period has expired, the classes will be removed from the account for good, and any assignments and scores data will no longer be available.

Important: Because these classes are no longer connected with the district, data relating to them cannot be recovered, so keep that in mind when you prepare for the next term!

All class changes mentioned above follow specific requirements set by the district and the official roster set on Clever. If you think that one of your classes might have been removed in error, please send us a support ticket.

What happens to an account that is converted to grassroots after it is no longer part of the Khan Academy Districts program?

When you are no longer part of the Khan Academy Districts program, you will start seeing changes when your Khan Academy account is converted to a grassroots account, which will vary depending on the account role and specific district requirements.

All account changes mentioned here follow specific requirements set by the district and the official roster set on Clever. If you think that your account might have been converted in error, please send us a support ticket.

All changes are based on information provided by the district and their specific requirements so, if you think this might be an error, please contact your partnership manager for more details.

Admins

Admin accounts that are no longer part of the program will be converted to a regular grassroots teacher account on Khan Academy. This means that all of your district-synced information will be removed, but you will still be able to log in to the account and use Khan Academy as normal.

Given the high volume of district information admins have access to, the district might instead require the administrator account to be removed. In this case, you will receive an error message if you attempt to access any district reports.

That said, if you are also a teacher, you will still be able to sign in to your teacher account and use Khan Academy as normal! Otherwise, you can also create a new account by following the steps in this article.

Teachers

Teacher accounts that are no longer part of the Khan Academy Districts program will be converted to a regular grassroots Khan Academy account. Since they’re no longer connected to the district, all of the district-synced classes will be removed, and students will no longer see those classes or the Goals or Assignments created there, but all student progress is retained on their own accounts.

The coaching relationship between the students in the district-synced class and that teacher account will also be removed, so if you want to continue coaching the students, please refer to this article to see how to create a new class, add students, and keep using Course Mastery goals and/or Assignments to coach them.

Students

Student accounts that are no longer part of the Khan Academy Districts program will be converted to a regular grassroots Khan Academy account. This means that they’re no longer connected to the district, but they’re still able to log in and use the account as normal. Additionally, all of your progress is still visible on the account!

That said, the account will no longer show the district-synced classes and features. This means that if a teacher previously created a Course Mastery Goals or Assignments in a district class you were part of, they will no longer appear on the student account, however, any progress on the skills achieved while working on those Goals and Assignments will still be there.

The coaching relationship between the student and the teacher will also be removed, so if the teacher wants to continue coaching this student, they’ll be able to do so by inviting them to an independent class as shown in this article.

What happens to my account at the end of the Khan Academy Districts school year?

At the end of the school year, you will start seeing changes in your Khan Academy account as we stop the automatic rostering feature and prepare district accounts for the next Khan Academy Districts term.

The timeframe of all account changes mentioned here follows the scheduling agreed with the district. If you think the changes in your account do not align with the end of the district school year, please send us a support ticket.

Admins

Admin accounts retain their reporting features and will continue to see the data relating to the previous term even after the district roster is cleaned up in preparation for the next term. That said, if an Admin clicks on a teacher row of a report filtered By Teacher, it will show no classes since those are cleaned up by the end of the term in the roster preparation phase.

Admin accounts that will not be part of the Khan Academy Districts program for that district in the next term are converted to regular grassroots teacher accounts on Khan Academy. This means that all of your district-synced information will be removed, but you will still be able to log in to the account and use Khan Academy as normal.

Given the high volume of district information admins have access to, the district might instead require that administrator account to be removed.

In this case, you will receive an error message if you attempt to access any district reports.

If you are also a teacher, you will still be able to sign in to your teacher account and use Khan Academy as normal. Otherwise, you can also create a new account by following the steps in this article.

Teachers

At the end of the school term, all district-synced classes are removed from teacher accounts. This means that, once the roster cleanup goes through, you will no longer have access to assignments, scores, and teacher reports from those classes, as they are tied to the class. That said, no progress is lost; all progress achieved is retained on the student’s account.

Please note that this cleanup phase removes district-synced classes only, so any grassroots classes or classes not currently synced with the district (usually indicated with [Archived]) will remain on the account, and you’ll be able to retain or remove them whenever you wish.

Please refer to this article for more details on how to delete a grassroots account.

Another change you might notice is that the coaching relationship between the teacher account and the students enrolled in district-synced classes is also removed, as we prepare the account to receive the new list of students rostered for the next term.

If you want to continue coaching the same students as before and they won’t be part of your roster for the next term, please refer to this article to see how to create a new class, add students, and keep using Course Mastery goals and/or Assignments to coach them.

Teacher accounts that will no longer be part of the Khan Academy Districts program for the next term are converted to regular grassroots Khan Academy accounts after their district-synced classes and coaching relationships are removed.

Students

Once the district roster cleanup is completed, students will no longer see district-classes listed on their Learning Homepage. This means that Course Mastery Goals or Assignments received from a district class will no longer appear on the student account. That said, any progress achieved while working on them will still be registered on the account.

The coaching relationship between the student and their district teachers is also removed, so they will no longer be listed on the Teachers tab.

If the teacher wants to continue coaching a student that will not be part of their roster for the next term, they’ll be able to do so by inviting them to an independent class as shown in this article.

Student accounts that will no longer be part of the Khan Academy Districts program are converted to regular grassroots Khan Academy accounts. This means that they’re no longer connected to the district, but they’re still able to log in and use the account as normal. Additionally, all progress achieved will still be visible on the account.

Scoring and Reporting

How are Khan Academy assessments scored?

For Beta and Live assessments, student performance is reported as both a score and a performance level. Khan Academy Interim Assessments use three performance levels to classify student performance:

  • Beginning (Lowest): Students have some foundational skills but are performing below grade-level expectations. They demonstrate limited understanding of grade-level standards and require considerable instructional support to build toward proficiency.
  • Approaching (Middle): Students have a good grasp on some grade-level standards, but have not yet achieved consistent performance across all expectations. They are approaching grade-level proficiency and need targeted support to address remaining gaps.
  • Demonstrating (Highest): Students demonstrate proficiency across the full range of grade-level standards. They consistently meet, or exceed, expectations and can independently apply their knowledge and skills in various contexts. How scores work

Scores are calculated using Item Response Theory (IRT), a statistical scoring approach that accounts for the difficulty of each question a student answers, rather than just counting correct answers. This is part of why the assessments can adapt to each student, while still producing scores that are comparable across different students and test forms.

Scores for assessments within each subject (Math and ELA) are placed on the same continuous scale (about 300–900), though each individual assessment has its own range of possible scores. Each assessment also has two cut scores — marking where the Approaching and Demonstrating levels begin — set by groups of subject matter experts (teachers, curriculum specialists, and administrators) in each subject through a process called Standard Setting.

A note on Explain Your Thinking and short response questions

We’re currently evaluating the use of AI to help score Explain Your Thinking conversations and short response questions. AI is not currently used for scoring. EYT Conversations and Short Responses are not yet factored into a student’s reported score.

To see how these scores show up in your reports, visit the following articles:

  • How can teachers use interim assessment performance reports? or
  • How can administrators use interim assessment performance reports?

How can administrators use interim assessment performance reports?

Performance reports help administrators understand how students are performing at different levels, including across districts, schools, and individual classes.

Access performance reports

  • Click your name and select Administrator dashboard
  • Click Assessments
  • Select an assessment
  • Click the Performance tab

Understand the different report tabs

Within the assessment view, you can switch between several report tabs:

  • Completion to track assessment completion across schools and classes
  • District overview to see performance across all schools in a district
  • School overview to view performance for a specific school
  • Performance to explore detailed results for a specific class

Start with the performance overview

At the top of each report (District overview, School overview, or Performance), you’ll see a summary of results.

This includes:

  • Average overall score
  • Scores by domain (for example: Expressions, Functions, Statistics)
  • A score distribution chart

Understand performance levels

Student scores are grouped into three performance levels:

  • Beginning
  • Approaching
  • Demonstrating For more information on scoring and performance levels, see How are interim assessments scored?

Review performance across schools and classes

Below the overview, you’ll see a table with results.

The table changes depending on the selected report:

  • In District overview, results are grouped by school

  • In School overview, results are grouped by class

  • In Performance, results are focused on a specific class This includes:

  • School or teacher and class name

  • Students who started and completed

  • Average overall score

  • Scores by domain

View detailed class performance

In the Performance tab, you can select a specific school, teacher, and class to explore more detailed results.

This view includes additional tabs such as:

  • Class overview
  • Student performance
  • Student growth
  • Explain Your Thinking
  • Engagement These views provide more detailed insights into student performance for a specific class.

What administrators can view

  • Engagement data is visible in the Performance tab for a selected class
  • Explain Your Thinking insights are also available within class-level views Engagement data and Explain Your Thinking insights are available in class-level views. For deeper analysis and instructional use, teachers can explore these reports within their own dashboards.

Use this report to identify differences

You can use performance reports to:

  • Identify differences in performance across schools or classes
  • Spot patterns across domains

Troubleshooting missing data

If you’re not seeing expected results:

  • Confirm students have completed the assessment
  • Check back after more students finish

How can teachers use interim assessment performance reports?

Performance reports help you understand how your students are performing on assessments, including overall scores, engagement, and how students explain their thinking.

Access performance reports

  • From the teacher dashboard, click on the assessments tab.
  • Find the desired assessment
  • Select “View Reports”
  • Select the Performance tab.

Start with the class overview

When you open the Performance tab, you’ll first see a summary of your class results.

This includes:

  • Average overall score
  • Performance by domain (for example: Expressions, Functions, Statistics)
  • A score distribution chart Use this section to quickly understand overall performance and where students are clustered.

Understand performance levels

Student scores are grouped into three performance levels:

  • Beginning
  • Approaching
  • Demonstrating For more information on scoring and performance levels, see How are interim assessments scored?

In addition, there are several other tabs that allow you to view other results

This view includes additional tabs such as:

  • Student performance
  • Student growth
  • Explain Your Thinking
  • Engagement Use this alongside scores to better understand performance.

Review student performance

Click the Student performance tab to see detailed results for each student. Click on a specific student for specific details.

You’ll see:

  • Completion status

  • Overall score

  • Scores by domain

  • Total time spent

  • Rushing indicators Use this view to:

  • Compare performance across content areas

  • Identify students who may need support

  • Spot patterns in performance

Review student growth

Click the Student growth tab to see how student performance has changed over time.

Growth is measured by how students’ overall scores and performance levels change across assessments.

What you’ll see

  • Performance levels and scores from different assessment points (for example, middle of year and end of year)
  • Changes in overall score
  • Growth indicators showing increases or decreases in performance Understand growth across your class

Use this view to:

  • Identify students who are improving over time
  • Spot students whose performance may be declining
  • Compare growth across students in your class

View growth for an individual student

Click on a student’s name to see their detailed growth report.

You’ll see:

  • A visual comparison of scores across assessments

  • Changes in performance over time Use this to:

  • Support one-on-one conversations

  • Track progress across assessment periods

View class-level Explain your thinking insights

Click the Explain Your Thinking tab to see patterns in how students explain their reasoning across the class.

Each question includes:

  • The concept being assessed
  • A summary of student responses
  • Common strengths and misunderstandings Use this to identify trends and plan instruction.
When are Explain Your Thinking insights available?

Explain your thinking insights appear once there is enough student data to provide meaningful insights.

  • If there isn’t enough data yet, you’ll see a message indicating that insights are not available
  • As more students complete the assessment, insights will appear automatically

Review student engagement

The “How engaged were students?” section shows how students interacted with the assessment.

This includes:

  • Rushing through questions
  • Ending conversations early You’ll also see a student-level table with engagement indicators.

View detailed results for an individual student

Click on a student’s name to open their detailed report.

What you’ll see

At the top of the page:

  • Overall score

  • Scores by domain

  • Indicators such as rushing activity

  • An option to compare with the class average Below that:

  • The Explain your thinking questions section

Review Explain Your Thinking for an individual student

You can also view Explain Your Thinking responses for a specific student.

  • Go to the Student performance tab

  • Click a student’s name

  • Scroll to the Explain your thinking questions section What you’ll see

  • A summary of the student’s response

  • Key strengths and areas for improvement

  • A Review conversation option to view the full interaction How to use this

  • Identify specific misconceptions

  • Prepare for one-on-one support

  • Better understand how a student is reasoning

Troubleshooting missing data

If you’re not seeing expected results:

  • Confirm students have completed the assessment
  • Check back after more students finish

How do I use interim assessment completion reports?

What are Completion Reports?

Completion Reports provide a real-time view of assessment participation. They show who has started, is in progress, or has completed an assessment during an open testing window.

While Performance Reports focus on scores after completion, Completion Reports focus on tracking participation and progress.

Who can see Completion Reports?

Access depends on your role:

  • District administrators can view completion data across all schools
  • School administrators can view completion data for their school
  • Teachers can view completion data for their assigned classes and students

Where do I find Completion Reports?

Access depends on your role.

District and School Administrators

To view administrator-level Completion Reports:

  • Click your name in the top right corner of Khan Academy.
  • Select Admin Reports.
  • Choose Assessments.
  • Select the relevant assessment.
  • Open the Completion tab. This path gives you access to district-level or school-level completion tracking.

If you instead select the Assessments tab from the left-hand navigation, you will see the teacher-level completion view only.

Teachers

To view class level Completion reports:

  • From teacher dashboard, click on the assessments tab.
  • Find your class and assessment
  • Select “View Reports”
  • Select the Completion tab.

What information is included in Completion Reports?

Completion Reports allow you to:

  • See whether students have started, are in progress, or have completed the assessment
  • View average time spent at the district, school, class, or student level
  • Identify rushing behavior that may need follow-up
Drill-down views

You can drill down by:

  • School: View completion rates and participation across schools
  • Class: View each class’s testing status
  • Student: View individual progress, time spent, and rushing indicators

When is the data updated?

Completion Reports show live data. Refresh the report to see the most up-to-date completion and engagement information.

How can I use Completion Reports?

Completion Reports help you:

  • Monitor participation early in the testing window
  • Identify schools or classes that may need follow-up
  • Track progress in real time
  • Reduce last-minute surprises before the window closes

What interim assessment reports are available?

If your district is using Khan Academy assessments, administrators and teachers have access to reporting tools that help monitor performance and track assessment participation.

Assessment reports provide visibility into how students are progressing and how testing is moving forward during an assessment window.

There are currently two types of assessment reports available:

  • Performance Reports, which show how students scored after completing an assessment
  • Completion Reports, which show who has started, is in progress, or has completed an assessment Both report types are designed to support schools and districts in planning, tracking, and following up during the testing window.

Who can access assessment reports?

Access depends on your role:

  • District administrators can view data across all schools and drill down to school, class, and student-level reports.
  • School administrators can view reports for their school and drill down to class and student-level reports.
  • Teachers can view class and student-level reports for their assigned classes. If you do not see the Assessments tab in your Admin Reports section, your district may not currently be participating in Khan Academy assessments.

Performance Reports

Performance Reports help you understand how students performed after completing an assessment.

These reports include overall scores, Domain Scores, and engagement information such as rushing behavior and Explain Your Thinking insights.

Performance reporting is currently available for select assessments.

To learn more, visit:

How can teachers use interim assessment performance reports?

How can administrators use interim assessment performance reports?

Completion Reports

Completion Reports help you monitor assessment participation in real time.

This report:

  • Shows which students have started, are in progress, or have completed the assessment
  • Provides visibility into time spent and rushing indicators Depending on your role/permissions, you’ll be able to see this information at the school, class, and student level.

Completion reporting is available for both Pilot and Beta assessments.

  • Beta: Grade 6 Math, Grade 8 Math, Grade 8 Math, Algebra 1, Geometry, Grades 9-10 ELA, Grades 11-12 ELA.
  • Pilot: Grade 6 ELA, Grade 7 ELA, Grade 8 ELA, Algebra II To learn more, visit:

How do I use interim assessment completion reports?

Setting up and Managing Child Accounts

How are child / restricted accounts different from regular accounts?

Some features are restricted or modified in child accounts to help protect the privacy of our Under-13 users.

Some of the most notable differences are:

  • Any parent who creates an account for their under 13 child becomes the permanent guardian and teacher of the account.
    • Child accounts created with parental approval will be deleted after 7 days if no parent connection to the account is confirmed.
    • The maintenance of a child account is reserved only for the use of one of the parents or legal guardians. Violation of this policy may result in the deletion of that account in its entirety.
    • Additionally, a Parent can prohibit, approve, or deny teacher access through their Parent Account.
  • Child accounts cannot add personal information to a profile.
    • Child accounts cannot disclose any personal information on their account, except for username and progress data to a teacher added to the account through a class.
    • Parents may add personal information to the account profile through the Parent Account Settings.
  • Under 13 accounts cannot participate in Khan Academy forum discussions,
    • This includes not being able to post questions/answers.
  • Under 13 accounts cannot receive email communication from Khan Academy.
    • All communications from Khan Academy will be sent to the Parent or teacher email associated with the account.
  • In regards to the Computer Science programs on Khan Academy:
    • Programs created by an under 13 user are only viewable to the user’s parent and teacher - not to the general public on the Browse Projects page.
    • No one will be able to upvote Computer Programs made by an under 13 user. See also:
  • If my child is under age 13, what login options are there?
  • How do I add additional coaches for a child account?

How can I edit my child’s settings?

If your child is younger than age 13, you can change their:

  • Username: Your child will use this name to log in to Khan Academy. It’s also the name that will show up on your parent homepage.

  • Gender: This information is optional.

  • Birthdate: If your child is younger than 13, indicating this will restrict your child’s access to Discussion Forums and keep their information private.

  • Primary language: We’ll show your child content in this language.

  • Sound effects: Choose whether you’d like your child to hear celebratory sounds when they achieve something.

  • Video auto-continue: Choose whether you’d like the next video to automatically start playing after watching the last one.

  • Password: Change your child’s password.

  • Coaches: Choose whether your child can add other coaches.

  • Accessibility: Choose “Hide visually dependent content” to hide content that requires mouse interaction with the screen.

  • Delete account: Permanently delete your child’s account. To change your child’s settings, follow these steps:

  • Log in to your own Khan Academy account and click your name at the top right. A menu will open.

  • Click Settings

  • Scroll down to Child accounts and click Settings for the child whose settings you want to change. Note: You can also reach these settings by selecting Your children from the drop-down menu, clicking on the child account you want to adjust, and clicking View settings. **

If your child is over the age of 13

  • If your child is over the age of 13, the settings button will no longer be visible next to their name. This means you cannot make changes to their settings or account information. Instead, your child can manage their own settings by visiting their settings page.
  • Additionally, parents cannot edit the settings of children who were not created directly through their parent account.

How do I add or remove coaches on a child account?

Parents have the ability to choose to allow or deny the addition of additional coaches to their child’s account (coaches can view a child’s Khan Academy progress information).

Additional coaches on child accounts are allowed by default in case your child’s teacher, tutor, or another friend or family member is going to help coach them using Khan Academy.

If you create an account for your child, you will have the option to disable this option upon creation or in your Child’s Settings (see below).

What is a coach?

A coach is someone who uses a Khan Academy teacher account to set Course Mastery goals, assign activities, and track your child’s progress.

How to enable your child’s account to add coaches

  • Log in to your Khan Academy account and make sure that you are viewing your Parent Dashboard by clicking your name in the upper right corner and selecting Parent Dashboard from the drop-down menu.
  • Click the Edit settings link next to the child account where you’d like to enable the ability for your child to add coaches. In your child’s Settings, scroll down to Coaches and check the Can add other coaches box. Your changes should be automatically saved.

How to view and update your child’s coaches

  • From your child’s account, you can track your child’s coaches, remove coaches, and help your child join a teacher’s class. To do this, click your child’s name from your Parent Dashboard and click the Teachers link.

See also:

- [If my child is under age 13, what login options are there?](https://support.khanacademy.org/hc/en-us/articles/202487460-If-my-child-is-under-age-13-what-login-options-are-there-)
- [How are child accounts different than regular accounts?](https://support.khanacademy.org/hc/en-us/articles/202262974-How-are-child-accounts-different-from-regular-accounts-)

How do I create or link child accounts to my parent account?

If you’re a parent and you already have a Khan Academy account, you can visit your Parent Dashboard and click the Add a child button. (If you don’t have an account for yourself yet, go to this link to create one.)

Once you click Add a child, you will be asked if your child already has an existing account. Select yes or no based on your child’s situation and click the Next button.

If your child has an existing account:

Enter your child’s email address into the email field and click the Send Invite button. Your child will receive an email invitation to link their account to yours.

If your child doesn’t have an email address, click My child doesn’t have an email address. You will be prompted to log out of your Khan Academy account and have your child login. From here, your child can add your email address in their account settings.

If your child doesn’t have an account:

If your child does not yet have a Khan Academy account, you will be prompted to create a new account by first entering your child’s date of birth.

Your child’s birthday is needed to determine permissions. Accounts for students younger than 13 are managed by a parent to protect the child’s privacy. You can find more information about accounts for students younger than 13 here.

If Your Child is Younger Than Age 13

You will be prompted to create a username and password for your child (note that the account is a restricted child account):

We strongly encourage that you do not use real names or any other information that could be used to identify someone when creating a username.

Fill in the form and click Create to create the account.

If Your Child is Age 13 or Older

You will be asked if your child has an email address. If your child has an email address you may either send your child an invitation to join Khan Academy, or you could create the account for your child:

If your child does not have an email address (or you choose to create the account yourself) you will get a form similar to the form if your child were younger than 13.

Multiple Children

If you have more children you can continue creating accounts now by clicking Add a child. You can also see the status of any email invitations you may have sent to your child’s email address. If you no longer wish to use a particular email to create an account for your child, you may delete your invitation at any time by clicking the red Delete invitation button.

After Account Creation

After you have created your child’s account(s) you can return to your homepage and log out and your child can log into his/her account.

Note: Always remember to log out of your account when you are done using it and teach your child to do the same! We frequently get reports of progress being made on the wrong account because parents or children forgot to log out.

See also:

  • If my child is under 13, what login options are there?
  • How are child/restricted accounts different from regular accounts?
  • How do I set-up a new user account?
  • How do I enable or disable Khanmigo on my child’s account?

How do I delete my child’s account?

Deleting a child account (under 13) is a little different than deleting an account for an adult or older teenager. Child accounts cannot be deleted without having a parent account attached and linked to it.

If you want to delete a child’s account from your linked parent account, you can do so by following the steps below. However, before doing so, there are two important considerations:

  • Deleting a child’s account is a permanent action that will delete all progress and put a lock on your child’s username. Their account cannot be restored once deleted.
  • If your child’s account was established for school use, you should check with your child’s teachers as they may be using the account for school assignments and to track their progress. To check whether the account is being used for school purposes, check to see if your child has any teachers linked to their account. To do this, go to your Parent Dashboard by clicking on your name in the upper right corner, and then click on Parent Dashboard.

In your Parent Dashboard, click on your child’s name:

Then, click on the Teachers tab in the left navigation bar:

If they have any linked teachers, they will be listed on the right-hand side, like this:

If your child does have one or more teachers linked to their account, you should check with them as to whether they need your child to keep their account active and the teacher linked, or whether they are OK with you removing them (the teacher) from your child’s account, and deleting it.

Once you have verified your child does not have any active teachers linked to their account, and you still want to permanently delete all of their past progress (assignments completed, badges earned, etc) and delete their account, follow these steps:

Back in your Parent Dashboard, click Edit Settings next to the child account you’d like to delete.

Scroll down to the bottom of the child’s Settings page and click on Delete [child account username].

You’ll be asked to re-enter the password for your account just to make sure you’re the parent or adult connected to the child’s account, and then your child’s account will be deleted.

How do I make assignments for my child?

Great news! Parents are now able to make assignments for their children without needing to add the teacher role, or add their children as students in a class!

Parents are able to assign the following content items to their children:

  • Quizzes
  • Articles
  • Videos
  • Unit tests
  • Course challenges At this moment, parents are unable to assign Unit and Course Mastery goals. Please note that the maximum number of children that you can assign content to is 10 and each class created can have only one child at a time.

You can assign content from the following places:

From the Parent dashboard:

  • Through your Parent dashboard, click on the Assignments tab. From there, select Create assignments.

  • This will open up the Class Details modal. Follow the below steps to set up a class for your child in order to make assignments for them.

    • Select the child you want to assign content to from the Children dropdown menu.
    • Name your class
    • Click on the Next button on the lower right hand corner.
    • Select the course you would like your child to work on from the Course Menu
    • Please note: after the above class set up details have been added, you will need to click on the class itself from the “Assignments” tab in order to create assignments for your child.
    • If you see the below error stating “No available children…”, it means you have already set up all the classes for your child or the remaining children connected to your parent account are part of a Khan Academy Districts classroom.
    • Go back to the “Assignments” tab and click on the specific class to create the assignments.

  • Once you have completed the class set up, you are ready to create assignments for your child through the below steps:

    • You’ll see all the units from the course you have added to the class.
    • Scroll through the different units. You can expand the units to see the individual items by clicking the > next to each unit title
    • Click the checkmark on which items you’d like to assign
    • Once you have selected the items, click the blue “Assign” button

  • Note: you will be able to see the number of assignments you are selecting in the Assign button with the parenthesis. Double check this number in case you are assigning more than you intended!

  • Once your assignments are selected and you have clicked on the Assign button, select the start date and due dates for the assignments.

  • After this, click Assign and you will be all set! From the content’s page:

  • Find the content that you would like to assign from Khan Academy’s content library.

    • You can do this by using the search bar at the upper left-hand side of your screen, or by clicking the “Explore” menu

  • Once you are on a content page, click the “Assign” button located at the top right-hand corner.

  • Once you have clicked on the Assign button, choose the child (or children) you’d like to assign the content to, as well as the the Start and Due dates for the assignment(s).

  • Don’t forget to click on the Assign button in the bottom right-hand corner of the pop-up screen to save and complete. Once that is done, your assignment(s) will be all set! If you’d like to know more about how to use your Parent Dashboard to help your child, please visit these helpful articles:

  • Khan Academy for Parents: Quick Start Guide

  • What can I do from the Khan Academy Parent Dashboard?

  • What Khanmigo tools are available to parents?

  • How do I monitor my child’s activity on Khan Academy?

How do I remove my email from my child’s account?

In order to be able to remove your email address from your child’s account, you’ll need to create a new email address, at least temporarily, for your child. Fortunately, free email accounts are easy to create.

If your child is 13 or older:

  • Create a new account for your child using the email server of your choice.
  • After this is done, please allow your child to log in and go to their Account Settings.
  • Under Linked accounts, click on Connect an email. Then from there, you can add the new email you created for them following the instructions after clicking the corresponding button.
  • Once you’ve connected a new email, then you can go to the email tab and enable the new email address.
  • Then go back to the Account tab and disconnect the previous email on the same section (Linked accounts), and log out. After this is done, you should be able to use the email you just disconnected to create another account if you want to, and your child will have a way to retrieve their password if the password is forgotten through their newly created and linked email address.

If your child is under 13:

This means that your child has a child account and as such, they are not meant to have an email address attached. Child accounts are meant to be managed by a parent account and they are usually created with only a username and password. No email.

However, if an email was added to it, for whatever reason, this is not something that can be reversed. This means that until the child turns 13 and the account automatically becomes an adult account, the email will not be able to be changed.

In this case, if the parent would like to be linked to their child’s account then the only solution would be for the parent to create a new email address for themselves and create a parent account. Once this is done, their child will be able to log into their account and link their child account to their parent’s newly created one by going to the Account settings (child’s) and add their parent’s email address.

How do I unlink my child’s account from my parent account?

We recognize that for a variety of reasons, you may want to unlink your child’s account from your parent account. At this time, there is no way to do this on your own.

However, our Support team can easily and quickly get you and your child’s accounts all squared away. If you would like to remove a child’s account from your parent account, please reach out to the Khan Academy Support team through this link. Please be sure to include the below information in your request, as it will help us complete your request even faster:

  • The email address and/or username of your Khan Academy account
  • The email address and/or username of the child account(s) you would like removed from your parent account We appreciate your understanding and are looking forward to hearing from you to assist with this!

How do I view my child’s profile?

Your child’s profile shows their unique username, coaches, learning history, and accomplishments. If your child is under 13, only you, your child, and your child’s other coaches will be able to see your child’s profile. You can learn more about how Khan Academy protects students under the age of 13 here.

If you have selected the Parent role as your Home page in your Settings, the Parent page will be the first you see after logging in. You can always return to this view by clicking the Khan Academy logo at the top of every Khan Academy page.

If you do not see the Parent homepage when you do this, you must first change your Homepage under Roles in your Account Account Settings. Instructions for changing your role can be found here.

To view your child’s profile, please follow these steps:

  • Make sure you’re on the Parent Dashboard
  • Your children should be listed. To view, click the person iconnext to your child’s name to be taken directly to their Learner Home.
  • Your child’s profile page will load and you’ll be able to see their progress.
  • You’ll then be able to switch to a different tab to view different information. In each tab you will find the following information:
    • Progress tab shows information about what your child has learned at Khan Academy.
      • Which math skills are in each level (attempted, familiar, proficient, mastered)
      • Name of the videos watched and the amount of time spent watching videos for each date
      • Activity per day, showing what skills were worked on, what videos were watched, and how many energy points were earned for each day
      • Breakdown per videos and skills. Showing how many problems were done or videos were watched for a specific skill.
    • Profile tab shows the following:
      • Badges that your child has already earned as well as the badges they can earn in the future
      • Streaks which are the number of days your child has consecutively worked on Khan Academy
      • Discussion activity
      • Projects that your child has created with our computer programming curriculum
    • Teachers tab allows you to see a list of your child’s current coaches and choose whether your child can add other coaches. See also:
  • How can I edit my child’s settings?
  • What can I do from the Khan Academy Parent Dashboard?

How does my child remove coaches on the mobile app?

Children under the age of 13 cannot remove coaches unless the parent has enabled the Can add other coaches option in the child’s account settings.

Because the Android and iOS apps don’t currently have the Parent dashboard, parents can only enable or disable the addition of other coaches on their child’s account from their Parent dashboard on the website.

Parents can click here for more information on how to add or remove coaches on their child’s account from their Parent dashboard.

Removing Coaches in the Mobile App

If you’ve enabled the Can add other coaches option for your child, they can remove a coach in their mobile app by going to Settings and then Manage teachers.

Once there, they can tap the red minus icon next to the teacher they’d like to remove.

They’ll be prompted to confirm that they understand removing the teacher will mean that they won’t receive future assignments from them; if so, they can tap Remove and the teacher will be removed.

Note: Your child won’t be able to remove any teachers listed under the District-Assigned Teachers section, since these are teachers and classes managed by your child’s school.

If my child is younger than age 13, what login options are there?

We are committed to protecting children’s privacy and have built security measures to protect children interested in using Khan Academy.

If a child younger than the age of 13 attempts to create an account on Khan Academy, the page following the signup screen will prompt them to submit a parent’s email address. We will notify the parent at that address with additional instructions to create the child account.

If a child younger than the age of 13 wants to create an account on Khan Academy, there are currently three options:

  • A child’s parent or legal guardian can create a child account by visiting khanacademy.org/parent. The parent can then click the Add your child button. The parent account is automatically tied to the child account and will become his or her permanent coach. Some features are restricted on child accounts to help protect the child’s privacy. Parent accounts require email logins, but the child accounts associated with a parent account do NOT require separate email addresses.

  • The child’s teacher can create an account. Many schools use Google Apps for Education, which allows managed accounts that the school controls. These Google accounts can be given to students under the age of 13.

  • The child can create an account by themselves. While creating their accounts, these users will be asked to enter their parent’s email address. Parents will then receive an email asking to approve the child account within 7 days. See also:

  • How are child accounts different from regular accounts?

  • How do I enable additional coaches for a child account?

  • Why is my child’s account being deleted after 7 days?

What reports can I use as a parent to monitor my child’s activity on Khan Academy?

As a parent in Khan Academy, you will be able to assign content such as: quizzes, articles, videos, unit tests, and course challenges. These can be assigned straight from the Parent dashboard, as well as from the content page.This article will give instructions on how you can view your child’s progress after they have worked through the assignments you have sent their way.

You can view your child’s progress on Khan Academy in 3 places:

  1. The Activity Overview Report on the Activity tab

Click on your child’s name to view their activity in the courses across Khan Academy. This includes work your child did at home and at school, broken down by Khan Academy course.

  1. The Individual Student Report from the Activity tab

Click the person iconnext to you child’s name to be taken directly to their Learner Home. Here you’ll see additional progress information, and if applicable, their Khanmigo Chat History and Khanmigo settings page.

  1. The Assignment Scores report from the Assignments tab

If you have made assignments for your child, you can see the scores for them here.

For additional help and support, please be sure to reach out to our support team here! We are happy to help in any way we can.
