Setting up your teacher account

How can I create my teacher account?

Whether you are a teacher, parent, or student, you create your Khan Academy account the same way.

To create your account, follow these steps:

  • Go to khanacademy.org
  • Click Sign up in the top right-hand corner, or select the blue “Teachers” button from the middle of the screen.
  • Choose your login method: Google Single Sign-on, Clever Single Sign-on, Facebook, Apple, Microsoft Single Sign-on, or Email and Password. Once you do, you will be guided through the process of customizing your teacher account by adding classes, students, and classwork for them to work on.

See also:

  • How do I get started on Khan Academy?
  • How do my students get started on Khan Academy?
  • How do I add new students to a class?

How do I add my school to my teacher dashboard?

Once you’ve created your Khan Academy account as a teacher, you can add your school to your account.

The “Add your school” feature allows teachers to select their school out of a list of schools from publicly available databases of educational institutions (e.g., NCES for the United States) and add it to their Khan Academy account.

From the Unknown School button on your Teacher Dashboard, you can filter by region and select your school.

  1. Add the country

  2. Add the school zip code

  3. Select your school

Adding your school allows you to personalize your account, and helps Khan Academy better understand the reach and impact of our product and services. Adding the school you teach at is entirely optional and will in no way affect your experience at Khan Academy.

If you’d like to skip this step, you can click on the X at the top right-hand corner of the pop-up.

If you’re trying to change the school you selected, you can access the “Name of your School” pop-up by clicking on the button at the top right-hand corner.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Why can’t I seem to find my school on the list? What can I do?

If you’re not able to locate your school in the “Add your school” pop-up, it is likely that it is not yet included in the list of schools of the NCES, or our list has not yet been updated.

In these cases, we recommend teachers either dismiss the pop-up or select “OTHER” as their school for any specified ZIP Code in the United States.

For more information on what to do if your school is not listed, please check out this article.

What if I teach in more than one school?

At the moment, teachers are only able to select one school per Khan Academy account. If you use the same Khan Academy account for several schools,

  • Feel free to select the school you prefer to see connected to your Khan Academy, or
  • Create a different account for every school you teach at. If you need more help with using Khan Academy, please visit our Help Center or let us know by submitting a support request. We’re happy to help!

How do I add or edit a course on my Khan Academy class?

Khan Academy has distinct collections of learning materials for various subjects, which we refer to as courses. Once added to your Khan Academy classes, these courses act as the “curriculum” from which you can create assignments for your students.

Why is it important to add courses to a class?

Adding courses to your classes on Khan Academy makes navigating your content as a teacher far easier, and is imperative to making sure all Khanmigo teacher features work properly, and ensures Administrator reports are accurate for Khan Academy District partners.

Editing the courses in your Khan Academy classes

If you’ve already set up classes on Khan Academy, or are part of a Khan Academy Districts partnership and automatically have your classes added to your roster, the next step is to add courses to those classes.

  • Click My Classes, then Class Settings.
  • Make sure the correct one is selected at the top left side of the screen.
  • You’ll be prompted with another screen where you can select, or deselect, a course.
  • After this, click Save. We hope this article was helpful in understanding how to add a course to your Khan Academy class! If you need more help with using Khan Academy, please visit our Help Center or let us know by submitting a support request.

How do I change my existing Khan Academy account into a teacher account?

If you previously were using Khan Academy as a student, adult learner, or parent, but now want to use it as a teacher, you can easily adjust your account’s “role.”

Below are the instructions to do so:

  • Log into your existing Khan Academy account
  • Click your name in the top-right corner
  • Click “Settings” from the dropdown
  • Scroll to the “Roles” section
  • Select the Teacher/Coach role from the options
  • Click “Save changes” We also suggest you fill out the “Add your school” and “Teacher confirmation” sections which are located below the “Roles” section on the settings page.

If you are not seeing these options and would like to switch your Khan Academy account to be a teacher, you can always send a help request to the Khan Academy Support team. We are here for you!

How do I change my homepage?

Khan Academy offers three homepage options for adult users:

  • Student page, Learner home

  • Coach/teacher page, Teacher Dashboard

  • Parent page, Parent Dashboard (Your children) You can change your account role and default homepage to the one of your preference by following these steps:

  • Go to your Account Settings

  • Scroll down until you find Roles

  • Select your role

  • In Homepage select the page you want as your homepage

  • Click Save Changes Here’s an example:

After your preferences have been saved, it could take a couple of minutes before the change is processed.

Note: You’re unable to uncheck Learner in your settings because for us, as a learning platform, everyone is a learner.

See also:

- [How can I edit my account settings?](https://support.khanacademy.org/hc/en-us/articles/204707040-How-can-I-edit-my-account-settings)
- [How do I change my account from a child to an adult or teacher account?](https://support.khanacademy.org/hc/en-us/articles/209891998-How-do-I-change-my-account-from-a-child-to-an-adult-or-teacher-account)

How do I get started using Khan Academy as a teacher?

Welcome to Khan Academy! This guide contains essential information on how to get started using Khan Academy in your teaching practice.

Step 1: Identify your goals in using Khan Academy

There are lots of ways to use Khan Academy as a teacher! Below are 3 tracks for you to choose from to help get you started.

  • Track 1: Do I see myself using Khan Academy material to aid in my instruction?
  • Track 2: Do I want to use Khanmigo to help prepare lesson plans + refresh my knowledge on subjects I am teaching?
  • Track 3: Do I want my students to do work on Khan Academy itself so I can track their progress and scores?
    • Did you know we’ve seen that with just 30+ minutes of usage per week, students were 2.5x more likely to meet their grade-level standards?
    • Ideas on crafting a classroom routine using Khan Academy

Track 1: Using Khan Academy material to aid in my instruction

Khan Academy offers a variety of material in 50+ languages for you to do so! We have articles, videos, exercises, quizzes, unit tests, and more that you can present to the whole class during instructional time.

Find material on khanacademy.org by clicking the “Explore” link in the top, lefthand corner, or searching for a topic in the search bar.

Check out this site for Khan Academy content based on US state standards and this section of our help center for educational standards outside of the US. You then can bookmark Khan Academy material in your web browser or make a list so you can have it handy to use with your students.

Track 2: Using Khanmigo as my teaching assistant to help prepare lesson plans, refresh my knowledge on subjects I am teaching, and more

Did you know we have lots of Khanmigo activities designed just for teachers? Use Khanmigo to help with lesson planning, rubrics, exit tickets, and more! Sign up for Khanmigo here to save time preparing to teach, and learn more about all the features here.

Track 3: Get your students working on Khan Academy

We are so excited you want to get your students started using Khan Academy!

Before even getting your student’s accounts set up, we recommend you develop a classroom routine based on:

  1. When you + your students have access to technology (consider during instructional time, and outside of it)

  2. How much time you have for Khan Academy during instructional time. Some ideas are:

  • “Khan Day”: On a specific day during the week, students work on Khan Academy for a part of the period.
  • Homework, bell-ringer or exit ticket: Daily or a few times a week, students will be assigned a video, article, or exercise, on Khan Academy to review the concepts they learned in class.
  • Khan Academy Station or Center: Incorporating Khan Academy into your existing centers routine or as a warm up
  • Incorporate LearnStorm in your routine as a way to celebrate progress, and maybe have a friendly competition between classes ;)
  1. What goals are your students working towards?
  • Are they studying for the Digital SAT? Filling in skills gaps? Learning how to be excited and motivated to complete classwork? Understanding these goals will help you craft your plan. Next: setting up your account, your classes, and your students’ accounts

You’re almost there! Khan Academy’s Teacher Tools are just around the corner. But first, you and your students need to get logged in. Check out these resources to do so:

  • How can I create my teacher account?

  • How do I add additional classes to my Khan Academy teacher account?

  • How do I add new students to a class in my Teacher Dashboard? - Invite students via email. You will need a list of student emails. - Add students without email accounts. You’ll create Khan Academy accounts for them. - Have students add themselves by class code. Each class has a unique class code. Students can enter the class code at khanacademy.org to join your class. - Link to your Google Classroom account and import the class. You will need your username and password for Google. Next: Create Assignments and Course Mastery Goals

  • Course Mastery Goals are year-long goals for proficiency in a course, promoting steady progress and deep understanding. Unit Mastery Goals are smaller and aimed at the mastery of one unit within a course.

  • Assignments can be used in a variety of ways, with some examples being:

    • Assigning the Course Challenge to gauge students’ understanding of an entire course, reinforcing particular skills, or practicing tricky skills for upcoming state assessments.

  • Check out this help center section to get you started: Making assignments and mastery goals for your students Next: Support student motivation and growth mindset:

  • Learning new things can be hard and vulnerable! We have this Growth mindset course to help you and your students be kind with themselves when being challenged.

  • We also offer the LearnStorm tracker to gamify learning for your students. Learn more about it here! Next: Track student progress through reporting

Khan Academy offers a variety of reporting options for you to track student progress, with options based on assignment scores and Mastery progress. Check them out here!

Finally: Embrace flexibility through adapting your routine to your students’ needs, and turn to the below resources if you need help!
  • Khan for Educators Course
  • Teachers and Coaches Section of the Khan Academy Help Center
  • Reach out to our support team through this link if you need to talk to a human! We are here and happy to help.

Settings and accessibility

How do I change my settings in Khan Academy Reimagined?

Your Settings page is where you can manage your account and customize your Khan Academy experience.

To open Settings, select Settings from the navigation menu.

Account

The Account tab lets you manage your basic account information and connected accounts.

Basics

From the Basics section, you can:

  • Update your display name (available for students ages 13 and older)
  • Select your state from the dropdown menu Note: Students under 13 cannot edit their display name. If your account is managed by your school, some information may also be locked.
Password

Students ages 13 and older can change their password by entering their current password and choosing a new one.

Students under 13 will see a message letting them know that a parent or guardian must log in to change their password.

Parent/Guardian

You can connect one parent or guardian to your account by entering their email address and selecting Send request to connect.

Only one parent or guardian can be connected at a time for privacy reasons.

User ID

Your User ID is displayed for reference and cannot be edited.

Linked Accounts

The Linked Accounts section shows any accounts connected to your Khan Academy account.

Personalization

The Personalization tab lets you customize how Khan Academy looks and behaves.

Video play options

Choose how videos play throughout Khan Academy.

Available options include:

  • Autoplay videos
  • Turn captions on or off by default
Primary language

Choose the language Khan Academy displays in.

This changes the language used for menus, instructions, and other interface text. Some content may not be available in every language.

Accessibility

The Accessibility section includes settings that can help customize how you interact with content.

For a detailed walkthrough of available accessibility features and settings, see What accessibility features are available in Khan Academy Reimagined?

Khanmigo

The Khanmigo tab contains settings for students who have access to Khanmigo.

If Khanmigo is available for your account, you can choose which voice Khanmigo uses when reading responses aloud.

If Khanmigo is not available for your account, you’ll see a message letting you know that Khanmigo is currently disabled for your classes.

Looking to customize Khanmigo?

Visual customizations such as accessories and outfits are not managed in Settings. To customize Khanmigo’s appearance, select your Gem count in the upper-right corner of your dashboard to open Collections.

For more information, see How do I earn Gems in Khan Academy Reimagined?

Notifications

The Notifications tab lets eligible students manage email notifications.

Students ages 13 and older can manage their notification preferences. If your email address hasn’t been verified yet, you’ll be prompted to verify it before changing your notification settings.

Students under 13 do not have access to email notifications and will see a message explaining that notifications become available after they turn 13.

Classes

The Classes tab shows the classes you’re enrolled in.

From this page, you can:

  • View your enrolled classes
  • Select Add a class to join another class

Need help?

If you still need assistance, visit the Khan Academy Help Center or contact Khan Academy Support

What accessibility features are available in Khan Academy Reimagined?

Khan Academy Reimagined includes a variety of accessibility features and supports designed to help learners access content in ways that work best for them.

This article provides an overview of accessibility-related features available in Khan Academy Reimagined, including accessibility settings, screen reader support, keyboard navigation, video accommodations, and text-to-speech options.

For more information about Khan Academy’s broader accessibility efforts, please see our Accessibility Statement.

Accessibility settings

You can customize several accessibility settings from the Personalization page.

To access these settings:

  • Select Settings from the navigation menu.
  • Select the Personalization tab.
  • Scroll to the Accessibility section. The Accessibility section includes options that support how you see, hear, or interact with content.
Hide visually-dependent content

This setting prioritizes content and experiences that are widely accessible, particularly for learners who use assistive technologies such as screen readers.

Content remains available, but Khan Academy Reimagined will prioritize options that rely less on visual information.

Reduce motion and animations

This setting limits motion effects and animations throughout the experience.

If your device is already configured to prefer reduced motion, animations may automatically be reduced regardless of this setting.

Remove color from videos

This setting displays videos in grayscale for learners who find black-and-white content easier to perceive.

Mute sound effects

This setting turns off interface sound effects throughout the experience.

Video settings

Khan Academy Reimagined also includes settings that can make video content easier to access.

From the Video section of the Personalization page, you can:

  • Mute videos by default
  • Turn captions on or off
  • Adjust video playback speed
Captions

You can turn captions on or off from your Personalization settings.

Playback speed

You can adjust video playback speed to learn at a pace that works best for you.

Mute videos

You can choose to have videos play without sound by default.

Screen reader support

Khan Academy Reimagined is designed to work with commonly used screen readers, including:

  • NVDA
  • JAWS
  • VoiceOver For the best experience, we recommend using the latest version of your browser, operating system, and assistive technology.

If you use a screen reader and encounter content that is difficult to access, please contact Khan Academy Support and include details about the page or activity you were using.

Text-to-speech support

Khanmigo includes a built-in text-to-speech feature that can read Khanmigo responses aloud.

[include a screenshot of the Khanmigo text-to-speech button]

In other areas of Khan Academy Reimagined, learners may also use supported screen readers or their device’s built-in text-to-speech tools.

The availability of text-to-speech features may vary depending on your device, browser, and assistive technology.

Keyboard navigation

Many areas of Khan Academy Reimagined can be accessed using a keyboard.

Common keyboard controls include:

  • Tab to move between interactive elements
  • Shift + Tab to move backward
  • Enter or Space to activate buttons, links, and other controls If you encounter an area that is difficult to navigate using only a keyboard, please let us know.

Browser compatibility

For the best experience, we recommend using a supported browser, including:

  • Google Chrome
  • Microsoft Edge
  • Mozilla Firefox
  • Safari Keeping your browser and operating system up to date can help ensure compatibility with accessibility features and assistive technologies.

Need help with accessibility?

If you encounter an accessibility issue or would like to share feedback, please contact Khan Academy Support and include:

  • The page, lesson, or feature you were using
  • Your browser and device
  • Any assistive technology you were using, such as a screen reader
  • Steps to reproduce the issue, if possible Accessibility feedback helps us continue improving the learning experience for all learners.

Sharing Khan with Others

I’d like to share Khan Academy with my colleagues or school, what materials do you have to help?

We have a whole page of materials that you can print out to share with your class or colleagues. Check it out here. In addition, check out our teacher resources. Thank you for helping to spread the word!

Khan Academy has greatly impacted my life - where can I share my story with others?

Your story of how Khan Academy has impacted your life truly inspires us. We love watching and reading your stories and sharing them with others. If you’d like to share yours on our site so that we can share it with others, or if you’d like to see other people’s stories, please visit our Khan Academy stories site.

Streaks & Levels

Can my course levels be reset on my account?

Your levels cannot be reset.

Your total and course level represents the total number of skills at the Proficient level you have achieved. If you would like start from 0, you can create a new account.

Do covered skills count towards streaks and levels?

Yes. Covered skills count towards streaks and course levels.

If those covered skills come from a course you are not participating in however, they won’t appear in your list of courses.

Likewise, if you level down on a previously proficient skill that has a “covered skill”, you would lose that skill point as well.

Does it get harder to get to the next course level?

It does! Getting to the next level requires that you earn one additional skill point than the prior level.

Another way to look at it: The level number you are on is also the amount of skills needed to move to the next level.

For example:

  • Starting at Level 1, it takes 1 skill point to get to Level 2.
  • At Level 2, it takes 2 skill points to get to Level 3.
  • At Level 3, it takes 3 skill points to get to Level 4.
  • At Level 20, it takes 20 skill points to get to Level 21. Keep going!

How do Course Levels work?

What is a course level?

A course level represents how many skills to proficient you have achieved in a course. Each level requires an increasing number of skill points to reach the next one.

In the example above, the learner is at level 4. They have achieved 2 out of the 4 skills needed to reach level 5. This user has a total of 8 skill points/8 skills proficient.

Earning skill points depend on achieving proficient or higher in new skills. With every proficient skill you earn, you get one skill point. Learn more about Mastery and Proficiency here.

Leveling up a skill to proficient moves you one point closer to your next course level. On unit quizzes and tests, you may earn more than one skill point at once since they cover more than one skill. If you level down a previously proficient skill, you will lose a skill point.

Note: Some skills may have a “covered skill.” A “covered skill” is a separate but related skill. If you get proficient on a skill that also has a covered skill, you earned an additional skill point!

How many levels does a course have?

The number of levels in a course depends on how many skills are in a course. You might see courses with 6 levels (17 skills),13 levels (88 skills), or more!

How many skill points does a level contain?

Every course starts at level 1, where you haven’t earned a skill in that course yet. Each level requires an increasing number of skill points to reach the next level. The higher you go, the more skill points are needed.

The level you are currently on represents the number of skill points needed to reach the next level. Each level up adds one additional skill point requirement.

For example:

  • You start at Level 1 with 0 skill points. To get to Level 2, you need 1 skill point.

  • At Level 2, you need 2 skill points to reach Level 3.

  • At Level 10, you need 10 skill points to reach Level 11.

What happens when you achieve proficiency in all the skills in a course?

Congratulations! Getting to proficient in all the skills in a course takes hard work and persistence. The course will be marked complete.

What happens when courses are updated with new skills?

The Khan Academy content team periodically reviews and updates course content in order to keep it fresh and standards-aligned. In these updates, skills can be added to or removed from a course. If new skills are added, more potential skill points will be added to a course. If you had completed every skill in a course, you will see that you now have additional skills to achieve proficiency in.

If skills are removed, we will subtract them from the total skills. Your level may go up, down, or stay the same depending on whether or not you had completed the skills that were removed.

How do I get to the next course level?

To get to the next level you need to earn the needed amount of skill points to get to the next course level. The amount of skill points needed depends on what level you are on.

The fraction next to your current course level tells you how many skill points you’ve earned while in this level and how many skill points are needed to get to the next one.

In the example above, the user is at Level 16 and they have 6 skill points. To get to the next level (17th), they need to earn 10 additional skill points for a total of 16.

How do I keep a streak going?

To keep a streak going, you must achieve at least one proficient skill a week.

  • The streak window runs from Monday at 12:00am to Sunday at 11:59pm (Pacific Time) If you do this, your streak will increase and continue!

Hover over your streak number for more information.

My child/student worked on my/another account instead of theirs. Can they transfer their skill points to their actual account?

They cannot.

Streaks and course level are tied to the account. We can’t transfer those skill points/levels/streaks.

What are Streaks and Course Levels?

Streaks and course levels celebrate your achievements by visually tracking your learning progress across Khan Academy.

Leveling up a skill to proficient or better will contribute to your streaks and course levels.

Streaks

To begin a streak, earn proficient in at least one skill.

To maintain your streak, achieve proficient in at least one new skill every week. The streak window runs from Monday at 12:00am to Sunday at 11:59pm (Pacific Time). If you level up before Sunday ends, your streak continues! If not, the streak ends and you’ll need to start over. How long of a streak can you build?

Course levels

Think of course levels like your favorite video game. The more skills you achieve proficient in, the higher your level. Every time you earn proficient or better on a skill, you earn a skill point. As you earn more skill points, you go up in levels. Learn more about Mastery and proficiency levels here.

If you haven’t started a course yet, you’ll be at level 1. With each proficient skill you earn, you move closer to the next level. If you level down a Proficient skill, it will affect your standing.

Your current level and the number of skills needed to reach the next level are displayed.

Want to know more about how course levels work? Click here

How do I read the streaks and levels bar?

To see your overall progress, visit your learner homepage. At the top you will find an overview of your achievements.

  • Total level and progress indicator: Your current level and the number of skills needed to reach the next level are displayed. This is the total cumulative level for all the skills you’ve earned.
  • Information icon: Hover over it to get more details.
  • “Up next”: Click to go to the next suggested skill.
  • Week streak number: Hover over it to get more information.
  • Triangle icon: Click to see the 4 most recent courses you’ve worked on. Like your total level, your current level and skills needed to move up are displayed.
  • “Level up”: Click to go directly to that course. When on a specific course page, that respective course level is displayed. Clicking on “Up Next”* will take you to the next suggested skill for that course.

*The wording may change depending on context, but it will take you to the next suggested skill.

May your streaks be long and your levels high!

If you run into any issues or have further questions, don’t hesitate to submit a support request. We’re here to help and ensure you get started smoothly.

What is a course level?

A course level is a measure of your achievement. More specifically, a course level represents how many skills to proficient you have achieved in a course.

On your learner homepage, your total level is displayed. This is the total cumulative count of all skills you’ve earned in every course you have taken.

Each level requires an increasing number of skill points to reach the next one.

When you’re on an individual course or lesson, the level for that course will be displayed.

What is a streak?

A streak measures the amount of consecutive weeks you’ve achieved at least one proficient skill.

To start a streak you must earn at least 1 proficient skill.

To maintain a streak, you must achieve at least 1 proficient skill every week. The streak window runs from Monday at 12:00am to Sunday at 11:59pm (Pacific Time). Doing so will continue your streak.

If you do not maintain the streak, the count goes back down to 0.

Where can I find my streaks and course level information?

There are two places you can see your streaks and course levels:

    1. Your learner homepage:
    • On this page, you will see:
      • Your current streak
      • Your total level (all skill points from all courses)
    1. On a Course/Unit/Lesson/Exercise page
    • On these pages, you will see:
      • Your current streak
      • Your level for the specific course you are on.

Where can I see my course levels?

You can see the 4 most recent courses you have worked on by clicking on the triangle next to your current level.

If you want to see your course level for courses not displayed here, go to your learner homepage, click on courses, then click on the individual course.

Heads up, if you earned skill points from covered skills in a course you aren’t actively participating in, they won’t appear here.

Why did I go down a level?

There are a couple of possible reasons you went down a level/or lost skill points.

  • You leveled down a proficient skill. (This is probably the most likely reason): This happened when you got a question (that you were previously proficient in) wrong on a unit quiz or test. When this happens, you lost that skill point you earned earlier. Losing that skill point could cause you to go down a course level.
  • The course was changed: We periodically update our courses and sometimes skills are added or removed. If a skill was removed that you had previously earned, you will lose that skill point. This could cause you to go down a course level. If you feel something else may have happened, feel free to contact us. We will be happy to help!

Why did my streak end?

Your streak ended because you didn’t get at least one skill to proficient in the prior week.

To start a new streak, achieve at least one Proficient skill.

To maintain your streak, you must achieve at least one Proficient skill every week. The streak window runs from Monday at 12:00am to Sunday at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)

Hover over your streak number for more information.

Why is my total skill level higher than all my individual course levels combined?

Great attention to detail!

Yes, there are situations where your total skill level might be higher than all of your individual course skill levels added up.

In the image below, the Total Level (all skill points earned), is at Level 4. This person has a total of 6 skill points.

However, if you look at the individual course levels and add them up, this person should only have 3 skill points.

Where did the additional 3 points come from?

The additional three points are from a “covered skill”.

  • A covered skill is a skill that is related to the one you were working on.
    • For example, let’s take the skill “adding 2 digit numbers”. This skill also has a “covered” skill called “adding 1 digit numbers”
    • This covered skill likely lives in a totally different course that you may not have taken.
  • In this (simplified) example. when you earned proficient on the skill of “adding 2 digit numbers”, you also earned proficient on the covered skill.
    • This also meant you earned an additional skill point. Instead of the usual 1 skill point earned, you earned 2 skill points.
  • While all skill points earned contribute to your total level score, it doesn’t appear in your list of course levels because you aren’t actively participating in the course the covered skill lives in.
  • Not all skills have “covered skills” Note: if you level down a skill that had a “covered skill”, you would lose both skill points.

Will my course level reset to zero if my streak ends?

Nope!

A streak ending has no impact on your total skill points earned/your Total or Course Level.

Those skills points were earned and cannot be taken away by a streak ending.

However, you can lose a skill point if you level down a previously Proficient skill.

Student account management and troubleshooting

How can I access Khan Academy in languages other than English?

Khan Academy provides as many resources as possible to support learners whose primary language is not English. The tools below are helpful for English Language Learners (ELL) and students in English as a Second Language (ESL) programs, and for students who are learning in a language other than English

Translated sites

In addition to English, Khan Academy has been translated into many other languages. You can see the full list of languages and how much has been translated here.

You can find those sites in the language drop-down at the bottom of the main Khan Academy page before you log in, or by setting a preferred language for your account.

Setting a primary language

On your account settings page, you can set English, (Latin American) Spanish, (Brazilian) Portuguese, or other languages as your primary language. You will then see all available Khan Academy content— including articles, videos, and skills— in that language. Learn more about editing your account settings.

Mobile app language settings

Android

If you’re using the Khan Academy app through an Android device, you can select the language you want the content to appear in using the Language Settings.

iOS

For iOS devices, the operating system will automatically set the app’s language based on your device’s language settings.

In practice, this means the app will try to match your main Language first, then a language in your Preferred Language Order, and finally, the app will default to English if no other supported language has been found.

Since the release of the Khan Academy App v6.4.0, users are able to change the language of their device settings to set a different language on the app.

How can I change my students’ birthdays?

Teachers who have confirmed that they are associated with a school can access and change some of their students’ settings, including their account passwords from their Teacher Dashboards.

Teachers can only edit the settings of students who are under 13 years old.

In order to access these features, be sure to confirm that you are associated with a school by checking the “I am a Teacher” box in the school selector in your account settings. Please carefully read the requirements before making this selection.

In addition to being able to adjust students’ date of birth, teachers can also modify their primary language, video settings, accessibility settings, and password.

You can access these features by going to your Roster tab and selecting the class where the student is enrolled.

Once you are in the class, go to the student’s page by clicking on the student you wish to modify settings for.

When you click a student’s name, you will be able to see the option for Settings right next to Assignments.

Once you have accessed these settings, you will be able to change the student’s birthday and other settings. Please be sure to click Save changes once you are done.

How can I coach a student from a restricted email domain?

Schools that use different e-mail address domains (the part after the @) for students and teachers may result in an error when some students try to add coaches.

Many school-supplied e-mail domains are restricted domains which limit the coaches that students can add in order to protect the privacy of students’ data.

If you are trying to coach a student account registered to a different email domain than yours, the student’s parent needs to adjust their settings in order to enable this. Parents can take the following steps on their children’s accounts if they want them to be able to add coaches outside of their domain:

  1. Access your Parent dashboard to view the children linked to your account.

  2. Click on Edit settings for the child in question.

  3. Scroll down to Coaches and enable your child to add coaches to their account.

Once this is enabled, your child will be able to approve coach requests themselves via their notifications. They will then be able to be coached by accounts outside of their exact email domain.

How can students under 13 create a Khan Academy account using Google Classroom?

Students who are over 13 and use Google Classroom can create a Khan Academy account using their Google account.

To get started:

  • Go to khanacademy.org/signup.
  • Click Student
  • Enter their date of birth
  • Select Sign in with Google and choose your school Google account.
  • Follow the prompts to finish creating your Khan Academy account and sign in.

Important information for students under 13

⚠️Students under 13 who do not already have a Khan Academy account should create their account using one of these methods:

  • Accept the email invitation sent after you sync to your Google Classroom.
  • Enter your class code at khanacademy.org. 🛑 Do not create an account through khanacademy.org. If students under 13 use the standard sign-up page, they will be asked to provide a parent’s email address as part of the account creation process.

Students who are 13, or older, can use any of the signup methods listed above.

Logging in after creating an account

After their account has been created, students can sign in at any time by following these steps:

  • Go to www.khanacademy.org.
  • Click Log in in the upper-right corner.
  • Select Google.
  • Follow the prompts to sign in with your school Google account.

What can I do if my student forgot their password?

Teachers who have accepted the Teacher Terms of Service in their account settings can access and change some of their students’ settings, including their account passwords, from their Teacher Dashboards.

To access these features, be sure to confirm that you are associated with a school by checking the “I am a Teacher” box in the school selector in your account settings. Please carefully read the requirements before making this selection.

In addition to being able to adjust students’ passwords, teachers can also modify their students’ nicknames, usernames, primary language, date of birth, and accessibility settings.

To view or make changes to a student’s settings, go to your Teacher Dashboard and then select the class the student is in.

Once in the class, click on Roster in the left navigation menu (found under Assignments).

Once you are in the class, go to the Student Roster page shown below. From there, click on the student for whom you wish to modify settings.

When you click a student’s name, you will be able to see the option for Settings right next to Assignments. If the student is younger than 13 years old, you’ll be able to update their information (such as changing their username, password, or birthdate).

You can make the necessary changes to the student’s settings from this page directly. Please be sure to click Save changes once you are done.

⚠️Note: If a student who is younger than 13 has a parent attached to their account and their parent has selected OFF for the “can add coaches” setting, that student will not be able to add teachers until this setting is adjusted, and their parent will have to adjust their settings for them.

Can I get a copy of my students’ usernames and passwords?

When you create student accounts in bulk without attaching email addresses, the system automatically sets them up as child accounts. During this process, you will receive a prompt to download a CSV file containing the username and password for each student account.

🛑STOP! As highlighted in the pop-up window below, this is a one-time opportunity to ensure privacy for our users. We highly encourage you to stop for a second and not skip it, as it is essential for managing your student accounts effectively.

If you skipped this step or if you no longer have the CSV file, your best option is to reset the students’ passwords directly from your class page if they’re under 13 years old. You can also submit a help request to our Support team if you need more help.

If you’d prefer to create new accounts and passwords for the students instead, you can do that using the instructions here.

Here are some tips when getting started:
  • When creating accounts for students, add their parents’ email addresses (double-check to make sure they’re correct— a lot of times these are entered incorrectly), so parents will receive an email from Khan Academy inviting them to create an account as well.
  • ⚠️Note: The email attached to the account that creates the student accounts will be shared with parents. Write down or print the usernames and passwords for the student accounts. You can pass these along to the next teacher, although you should keep in mind that a parent can change the username and/or password at any time.

Student roster management

Can a user have multiple coaches? Is there a way to add a co-teacher?

Co-teaching functionality was introduced for classrooms in the Khan Academy Districts and Learning Paths programs. You can go here to learn more about these programs.

If you do have a Khan Academy Districts and Learning Paths classroom, you can learn more about how to use this feature here: Learning Paths, Khan Academy Districts.

A user can have any number of coaches. However, teachers who are not using Learning Paths or Khan Academy Districts cannot co-teach a class in the sense of sharing assignments. Each teacher manages their own assignments, and only the teacher who created an assignment can view its reports and results.

However, multiple teachers can still work with the same students and view their progress. There are two ways to do this:

  • Share a single teacher account.
  • One teacher creates the class, and both teachers sign in using the same teacher account. This is the only way for both teachers to access the same assignments, reports, and assignment results.
  • Have each teacher create their own account.
  • One teacher creates the class, and the second teacher creates their own teacher account. Students then join the second teacher’s class using the class code or by accepting the teacher’s email invitation.
  • In this setup:
    • Both teachers can view the students’ overall progress and learning activity.
    • Assignments, assignment reports, and other class-specific data are not shared between teacher accounts. Each teacher can only see the assignments they created. Note: Students only need one Khan Academy account. They do not need separate student accounts for each teacher. Once students have joined both classes, each teacher can view their progress, but assignment information remains tied to the teacher account that created it.

Now, if you’re a teacher who’d like to transfer your class and/or assignments to the next year’s teacher, we do have a workaround!

While Assignments data (such as reports and scores, for example) is only visible to the teacher who created the class and cannot be transferred, Unit missions can be used by future teachers to leverage the work the students have already done on their accounts.

Unit Missions look at the mastery of an entire course, so any mastery already achieved by your students in that course is accounted for and should be retroactively updated! Please refer to our article: How do I create Unit Missions for my students? for more details.

This means that while the next year’s teacher won’t be able to access Assignments data (since they’re tied to the old class), any Unit Mission the teacher sets on the new class should still consider the existing progress on the students’ accounts. They would need to create a new class, enroll their students, and create the Unit Missions for them.

How do I add new students to a class in my Teacher Dashboard?

Once you’ve created a class in your Teacher Dashboard, you’ll need to add students to it.

To add a new student to a class:

  • Go to your Roster tab and make sure you’ve selected the correct class.
  • To add a student to the class, click on Add students.
  • This pop-up screen will appear once you click on the Add students button. Follow the prompts to add the student to the class, or create new accounts for your students. You can also adjust your students’ settings if they are under 13 years old. Please take a look at this article for more instructions on how to do that: What can I do if my student forgot their password?

How do I import my Google Classroom roster to Khan Academy?

Teachers who are using Google Classroom can import their student roster to Khan Academy to quickly set up their classes and student accounts.

This article will go over:

  • How to import a Google Classroom roster onto a Khan Academy account

  • What your students will see after you do so

  • Some troubleshooting tips for helping get your students set up on Khan Academy using their Google Single-Sign-On (SSO) as their login method Here is a quick summary of this article in case you are in a hurry!

  • We’re only importing your student roster from Google Classroom, not any assignment data. We also cannot send assignments from Khan Academy to your Google Classroom.

  • You need to create the class on Khan Academy before you can connect a Google Classroom to it. You can do this from the class creation flow, or from the class settings page.

  • If your students are under 13 years old and do not have Khan Academy accounts, they will need to sign up for one through the following options:

    • The emailed invitation that is sent out once you sync your Google Classroom
    • Entering your class code on khanacademy.org
    • If they try and sign up on the main khanacademy.org site, they will be required to also enter their parent’s email address.
    • Students above 13 years old can use any of the above options Here are the steps to import your Google Classroom roster to Khan Academy:

  • On your Dashboard, click on Add class.

  • Select “Import from Google Classroom” and click on “Create a classroom”.

  • Select which class you’d like to import from Google Classroom

  • Once the class is created and the roster imported, you will be able to view a final message stating the following:

  • The first time you access the class, you’ll be prompted to assign content to the class:

  1. Optional final step: visit the “Class Settings” page of your new class and check the “Sync with Google Classroom” option.

This is in case a new student joins your Google Classroom, they will automatically be synced to your Khan Academy roster.

All set! You’ll notice that your newly created class in Khan Academy has adopted the classroom name from the rostered classroom. You can always later change its name from your class’s settings.

How do I get my students logged in once my Google Classroom is set up?

Students who already have a Khan Academy account:

  • Will automatically be enrolled in your Khan Academy class if the email on their account matches what is on your Google Classroom Roster Students who do not have a Khan Academy account:

  • Are marked as “Pending” on your Khan Academy roster

  • Receive email invitations to join Khan Academy. NOTE: If your students are under 13 years old and do not have Khan Academy accounts, they will need to sign up for one through the following options:

  • The emailed invitation that is sent out once you sync your Google Classroom

  • Entering your class code on khanacademy.org

  • If they try and sign up on the main khanacademy.org site, they will be required to also enter their parent’s email address.

  • Students above 13 years old can use any of the above options We hope this article was helpful in learning the ins and outs of syncing your Google Classroom roster with Khan Academy! If you need additional assistance, please reach out to the Khan Academy Support Team!

How do I manage my student roster?

Class changed? Need some help organizing your students? You’ve come to the right place.

Add students without Khan Academy accounts to an existing class

  • Make sure you’re in your Teacher Dashboard. You can get there by clicking on your name in the top right corner of the screen and selecting Teacher Dashboard from the drop-down menu.
  • To add a new student, click on the name of a class. Don’t have a Khan Academy class set up yet? Learn how to create one here.
  • Click on Students under Admin in the left sidebar.
  • On the Student Roster page, click on Add new students.
  • Follow the prompts.

How to remove students from a class

Do you need to remove a student from a class? We know you are sorry to see them go!

  • Make sure you’re on your Teacher dashboard. You can get there by clicking on your name in the top right corner of the screen and selecting Coach Dashboard from the drop down menu.
  • Click on a specific class and then click on Students under Admin in the left sidebar.
  • Check the box on the right side of your screen across from the student name. Then click on the Action menu above and select Remove from class.

How to stop coaching a student

  • Make sure you’re on your Teacher Dashboard. You can get there by clicking on your name in the top right corner of the screen and selecting Teacher Dashboard from the drop down menu.
  • Click on Students under Admin in the left sidebar.
  • Select one or multiple students by clicking the boxes on the right-hand side of the list of students. Click on the down arrow to the right of the word Actions on the right hand side at the top of the student list and select Stop coaching. This will remove selected students from ALL classes.

How to rename students

  • Make sure you’re on your Teacher Dashboard. You can get there by clicking on your name in the top right corner of the screen and selecting Teacher Dashboard from the drop down menu.
  • Click on the Students tab. You will see that students are listed by their usernames.
  • To change that, hover your cursor over the student name. A link will appear to the right. Click on Edit display name. This will open a field where you can change the name to whatever will make it easiest for you to identify and organize your students. Like things in alphabetical order? Click on the little arrow next to the words Student name at the top of the list of students to put the list in alphabetical order. Click it again for reverse alphabetical order!

How do I manually create an account for a student?

You can create Khan Academy accounts for your students without an email address by selecting the option Create your students’ accounts when adding your students in the class creation process.

This option will allow you to create both the username and the password for each of your students.

First, you will be prompted to enter each student’s name. If you have a list with their names, you can simply copy and paste them into Khan Academy. Just make sure each student is added in a separate line.

Once you have added the student names, our system will provide generic usernames and passwords for each new account. You can edit these usernames and passwords if you’d like to. After setting up the username and passwords, click on Create account.

Right after, you’ll be given the option to download a copy of student names, usernames, and passwords.

Note: For privacy reasons, you will only be able to download this list in this step.

How do I remove students from a class?

While a teacher can stop coaching a student altogether and, as a result, remove the student from the class (assignments included), there is a way to remove a student from a particular class without severing the coaching relationship entirely.

With the Remove from this class feature, a teacher essentially removes the student from the class while retaining the coach/student link. This way, a teacher is able to still see the student on their Students list, and if they wish to add them to another one of their classes, they can do so easily.

To remove a student from a class:

  • Log in to your account and go to your Dashboard
  • Select the class from which you want to remove students.
  • Click on Roster in the left sidebar.
  • Select one or multiple students by clicking the boxes on the left-hand side of the list of students.
  • Click on the Bulk actions button
  • Select Remove from this class.

How do I remove students from my Khan Academy class roster?

There are 2 options for teachers who would like to remove students from their classes on Khan Academy:

  • Removing them from a class, but still have them connected to your account.

    • This is good for students you might teach again next semester, or in a different class.

  • Remove from your account entirely.

    • This option is good for students who have graduated, switched schools, or who will not be your students again. Below are instructions on how to do both of these:

  • Click “Roster” from the lefthand menu

  • Select which class, or click “View students across all classes” button

  • Select one or multiple check boxes next to the student name

  • For one student only = click the 3 dots. For multiple students, click “Bulk actions”

  • Click “Remove from this class” or “Remove from my account” If you are doing complex roster management, or have lots of students, but want to see them all on one single list, we recommend using the “View students across all classes” option:

  • Adjust the filter at the top to see if there are any students without active classes

  • Select all students by clicking on the Checkbox beside “Student” in the table header, or select the students you want to remove one by one.

  • Click on the Bulk actions drop-down menu.

  • Click on Remove from my account. We also recommend checking out the article “Is there a limit to the number of students or classes I can have on Khan Academy?”.

We hope this article was helpful in understanding how to remove students from your Khan Academy classes! If you need additional help, please reach out to the Khan Academy Support team. We are here and happy to help!

How do I rename students on my class roster?

Teachers and coaches can edit how their students’ names are displayed in the Students tab of their Teacher Dashboard.

Changing a student’s display name in your Students tab won’t affect the student’s selected username or nickname (or anything else in their account), and any changes will only be visible to you.

To adjust a student’s name in your Teacher dashboard:

  • Make sure you’re in your Teacher Dashboard. You can get there by clicking on your name in the top right corner of the screen and selecting Teacher Dashboard from the drop-down menu.
  • Click on the Students tab. By default, students are listed by their usernames. To change that, hover your cursor over the student’s entry in the roster. Click on the Edit display name link that appears on the right side of the student entry (next to the checkbox).
  • This will open a field where you can change the name to whatever will make it easiest for you to identify and organize your students. To save the change, hit the Enter key on your keyboard. Like things in alphabetical order? Click on the little arrow next to the words Student Name at the top of the list of students to put the list in alphabetical order. Click it again for reverse alphabetical order!

How do I input math expressions when working with Khanmigo?

Entering math expressions when chatting with Khanmigo is easy, thanks to our math input tools! Khanmigo also understands LaTeX, a text-based way to write math. The steps vary slightly depending on whether you’re a student or a teacher.

Note: The math input features described in this article require Khanmigo. If your account does not include Khanmigo, you will not see the chat option at all, and these instructions will not apply to you. Learn more about getting Khanmigo.

  • Below the chat input, you’ll see a grid icon (⁞⁞) next to the “+” button.
  • Click the grid icon — the tooltip will confirm it’s “Math keys”.
    • The keypad will appear. Toggle it on or off as needed.
  • Use the keypad or type in LaTeX to write your equation. Add regular text for context.
  • Hit the send button (arrow icon) and let Khanmigo assist you! Important: If you want to enter specific math language, the entire equation must be written using the math palette.

LaTeX: Your Math Typing Tool

Some exercises have a special keypad for math symbols. But sometimes, you’ll need to type them. That’s where LaTeX comes in handy. Here are some common LaTeX commands:

Multiplication: Use an asterisk (). E.g., “34”

Division: Use a slash (/). E.g., “3/4”. For operations in the numerator or denominator, use parentheses. E.g., “12/(5n)” or “(n+3)/6”

Square root: Type “sqrt(x)”. E.g., “sqrt(3)”

Pi: Type “pi”

Theta (θ): Type “theta”

Powers or exponents: Use a caret (^). E.g., “4^5”

Fractional exponents: Use a caret (^) and type the fraction in parentheses. E.g., “x^(1/3)”

Greater than or equal to: Type “>=”

Less than or equal to: Type “<=”

Logarithms: For base 10, enter “log(x)”. For natural logarithms, enter “ln(x)”

Logarithms with other bases: Enter as “log_b(n)”, where b is the base and n is the number

If you still need assistance, visit the Khan Academy Help Center or contact Khan Academy Support

How do I upload images to Khanmigo in the reimagined Khan Academy?

If you’re working through a challenging math or science problem, you can attach an image in your Khanmigo conversation in the Tutor Me activity. Whether it’s a diagram, graph, handwritten work, or another relevant visual, adding an image helps Khanmigo better understand your question and provide more specific and personalized support.

Note: This feature is only available to users with Khanmigo access, either through a personal purchase, parent-granted access, or a Khan Academy Districts partnership that has enabled the feature.

Which types of images work best?

To get the most out of this feature, make sure your image clearly supports your question or learning goal in math or science. Here are a few good examples:

  • A photo of your handwritten math problem to check your steps
  • A geometry diagram you’re trying to solve
  • A science diagram (like a circuit or a cell structure) that needs an explanation
  • A graph or data set that you want help interpreting

How to attach an image

  1. Navigate to the Tutor Me activity on Khanmigo.

  2. Click the + (plus) icon in the chat.

  3. Choose how you’d like to upload your image: Files, Camera, or From URL.

Note: If using the Camera option, you’ll need to grant your browser permission to access your camera.

  1. Add your question or prompt in the text box — this helps Khanmigo know how to help you. It is required to include a message or question with your image. The system doesn’t allow image-only submissions.

  2. Click Send.

Supported image types

You can attach the following types of images:

  • PNG
  • JPEG Screenshots, mobile phone photos, and scanned documents all work great. Once submitted, thumbnails are clickable to reveal a full-screen rendering of the image.

⚠️ Note: The Khan Academy app does not currently support image input. If you need this feature on mobile, we recommend using the mobile web version instead.

What not to attach

Please avoid attaching the following types of images, as they may be flagged or ignored by the moderation system:

  • Images that contain personal or sensitive information
  • Images that are not related to schoolwork or learning
  • Inappropriate, offensive, or disruptive content
  • Blurry, blank, or unreadable images Sticking to clear, relevant, and educational images helps keep Khanmigo safe and focused on learning.

Important: If a child’s chat is flagged by the moderation system, their connected adult will automatically receive an email notification. This notification includes an AI-generated description of the flagged image. Parents can also review past flagged Khanmigo conversations through their child’s chat history page.

What happens to the images?

Images you attach are only visible during your live chat session. Once you close the chat, the image is removed to protect your privacy and ensure security. Images uploaded to Khanmigo are never stored on Khan Academy servers.

In your chat history, you’ll see a placeholder along with a brief, AI-generated description of the image, so you can still reference what was shared.

Who has access to this feature?

The following users can add images to their Khanmigo conversations:

  • Those who have purchased Khanmigo for themselves
  • Those who gained access to Khanmigo through their parent
  • Those who are part of a Khan Academy Districts partnership that has enabled the feature on their district’s Settings page
    • District administrators can manage this setting for their entire district If you still need assistance, visit the Khan Academy Help Center or contact Khan Academy Support

How do I use Writing Coach?

Writing Coach, powered by Khanmigo, guides you through each stage of the writing process, from understanding your assignment to revising your final draft.

This guide explains what to expect at each step so you can confidently complete your Writing Coach assignment.

Do I have access to Writing Coach?

You have access to Writing Coach if:

  • You have an active Khanmigo subscription.
  • Your teacher assigned you a Writing Coach assignment. Note: Teachers in the United States who have access to Khanmigo teacher tools also have access to Writing Coach.

Access Writing Coach

How you access Writing Coach depends on how it’s available to you.

If you’re using Khan Academy Classroom (KAC)

Writing Coach assignments appear in your learning queue.

Select the assignment to open it directly within Khan Academy Classroom.

If you’re using standalone Writing Coach

You can access assignments from the Writing Coach website.

Complete your assignment

Writing Coach guides you through five stages.

1. Understand the assignment

Begin by reading your assignment instructions carefully.

During this stage, you can:

  • Review the essay prompt.
  • Ask Khanmigo questions about the assignment.
  • Get help understanding what your assignment is asking.
  • Ask for suggestions on how to get started. When you’re ready, select Next: Start outlining.
2. Create an outline

Before writing your essay, use the graphic organizer to organize your ideas.

You can:

  • Write your thesis.

  • Add body paragraphs.

  • Include supporting evidence.

  • Add reasoning and explanations.

  • Include external sources when appropriate. You can also:

  • Add additional body paragraphs.

  • Rearrange sections.

  • Remove sections you no longer need. If you need help, you can ask Khanmigo questions or request feedback on your outline.

You can also open the Assignment tab at any time to review your essay instructions.

If part of your outline is incomplete, you’ll see a reminder before continuing. You can choose to complete the missing sections or continue anyway.

When you’re ready, select Next: Start drafting.

3. Write your first draft

Use your outline to write the first draft of your essay.

While drafting, you can:

  • View your outline alongside your essay.
  • Copy sections from your outline into your draft.
  • Ask Khanmigo questions or request guidance.
  • Review your assignment instructions at any time. When you’ve finished your first draft, select Next: Start revising.

Important: Make sure your first draft is complete before continuing. You can only submit your first draft for feedback once.

4. Complete the completeness check

Before feedback begins, Writing Coach reviews your draft to make sure it’s ready for revision.

If your draft needs additional work—for example, it’s too short or missing important sections—you’ll be prompted to continue writing before moving on.

5. Revise your essay

Instead of receiving all of your feedback at once, you’ll work through one feedback category at a time.

You’ll revise your essay in this order:

  • Thesis & Focus: Is your main argument clear and well-defined?

  • Evidence & Reasoning: Do your ideas include strong evidence and explanation?

  • Structure & Organization: Is your essay organized logically?

  • Language: Is your writing clear, precise, and appropriate? For each category, you’ll:

  • Review the feedback.

  • Revise your essay.

  • Ask Khanmigo follow-up questions if you need help.

  • Continue to the next category after completing your revisions. Working through one category at a time helps you focus on improving one part of your essay before moving on to the next.

Tip: If you’re unsure how to revise your essay, ask Khanmigo follow-up questions. The more you engage with the feedback, the more you’ll get out of the revision process.

Finish your essay

The final step depends on how you’re using Writing Coach.

If you’re using Khan Academy Classroom (KAC)

After you’ve completed all four revision categories, you’ll see an End-of-Task card confirming you’ve finished the assignment.

You’ll also earn 10 gems before returning to your learning queue.

You can then export your essay as:

  • Microsoft Word (.docx)
  • Google Drive (requires a Google account) Your completed essay will remain available if you return later.

Need help?

If you have questions about using Writing Coach, please contact our support team.

Related articles

  • What will my students see when completing a Writing Coach assignment?
  • How do I sign up for Writing Coach?

What is a streak and how do I keep it going in the reimagined Khan Academy experience?

A streak tracks your consistent learning progress on Khan Academy. You earn a streak by gaining at least 1 proficient skill in a week.

You can find your streak under Achievements. This is where you can see your current streak count and track your weekly progress.

How do I keep a streak going?

To keep a streak going, you must achieve at least one proficient skill every week.

  • The streak window runs from Monday at 12:00 AM to Sunday at 11:59 PM (Pacific Time).
  • If you earn at least one proficient skill before Sunday ends, your streak continues!
  • Your streak count will update the following Monday. You can earn proficient on a skill through exercises, unit quizzes, or unit tests.

Why did my streak end?

Your streak ended because you didn’t earn at least one skill to proficient during the prior week.

To start a new streak: Achieve at least one proficient skill.

If you still need assistance, visit the Khan Academy Help Center or contact Khan Academy Support

What is the Readiness Check?

If your teacher assigned you a Readiness Check, you’re in the right place! Here’s what it is, how it works, and what you can expect after you finish.

The Readiness Check is a short math assessment that helps Khan Academy choose practice that’s just right for you.

It asks questions about skills from earlier grades to see what you already know and where you can keep growing. Then, it creates personalized practice to support you as you learn new topics.

Don’t worry about getting every question right. The goal isn’t to earn a score. It’s to help Khan Academy understand what practice will be most helpful for you.

Take the Readiness Check

When your teacher assigns the Readiness Check, you’ll see it in your assignments.

You can complete it at your own pace and come back later if you need to.

The Readiness Check:

  • has about 36 questions
  • has no time limit
  • can be paused and finished later
  • doesn’t affect your mastery, Gems, or streak

Get personalized practice

After you finish the Readiness Check, Khan Academy uses your answers to create practice that’s personalized for you.

If there are skills that could help you with upcoming lessons, Khan Academy will automatically create extra practice just for you.

There’s nothing else you need to do. Your personalized practice is created automatically.

Keep learning

Your personalized practice may appear in two places.

Readiness exercises

As you work through your Daily and Weekly Missions, you may see Readiness exercises before some of your regular assignments.

These exercises give you a chance to practice important skills before you learn something new.

Just like other practice exercises on Khan Academy, Readiness exercises:

  • earn Gems
  • count toward your streak
  • help build your mastery
Readiness Mission

You’ll also see a Readiness Mission on your dashboard.

Your Readiness Mission brings all of your Readiness exercises together in one place, so you can work through them whenever you’d like.

When you reach Proficient on every skill in your Readiness Mission, you’ll earn a 10-Gem bonus.

Keep making progress

Once you’ve completed the Readiness Check, just keep learning as you normally would.

If you have Readiness exercises, they’ll appear automatically as you work through your missions. They’ll help you build the skills you’ll need for upcoming lessons.

That’s it! Just keep learning. We’ll make sure your personalized practice is there when you need it.

If you still need assistance, visit the Khan Academy Help Center or contact Khan Academy Support

Where can I find my Khanmigo chat history in Khan Academy Reimagined?

You can view past Khanmigo chats from your History tab while logged into your account. Here’s how to find and review your chat history:

1. Open the History tab

While logged in, select History from the left-hand menu.

2. Go to the Chat history section

Once you’re on the History page, click Chat history at the top.

You can filter your chat list using the dropdown menu to show chats from:

  • Today

  • Last 7 days

  • Last 30 days

  • All time

  • A custom date range Chats are shown in reverse chronological order and include:

  • The chat title
