Transitioning from using grassroots Khan Academy to Khan Academy Districts

This article is for teachers who used Khan Academy with their students before the district chose to purchase Khan Academy Districts

Welcome! Now that your district has chosen to purchase Khan Academy Districts, we’d like to make the transition as smooth as possible for you and your students. There are 3 key things you need to know about when making the transition from Khan Academy prior to Khan Academy Districts (we refer to this as “grassroots” KA) to Khan Academy Districts:

  • Account linking
  • What data is preserved?
  • Class dashboard cleanup

1. Account Linking

If you or your students have been using Khan Academy prior to Khan Academy Districts, there may be one step - which we call account linking - that you need to take in order to ensure your previous activity on our platform is ported into your new Khan Academy Districtsaccount.

The below video goes over everything you need to know about if you were using Khan Academy with your students before your district purchased Khan Academy Districts:

If you already have a Khan Academy account associated with your official school email address or have been using Clever Library, good news! Your accounts will automatically be linked when you log in, no action needed.

Account Linking Instructions for Teachers:

If you have been using a different email address than your official school email for your Khan Academy account, follow the below instructions to link that account to your new Khan Academy Districts account:

  • You’ll receive an activation email (subject line “Confirm your official Khan Academy account”)

  • Open that email and click on the blue button that says “Confirm your account”

  • On the next screen, click the button “Log into my existing account” (pictured below)

  • Log into your existing account using your username and password, or through clicking the Continue with Google button.

  • Your accounts are now linked! You will see your previous classes and your district rostered classes in one place. Account Linking Instructions for Students:

  • This process is the same for students, except they do not receive an activation email.

  • If a student has been using Khan Academy previously with their official school email address or Clever Library, their previous account will be automatically linked to their new Khan Academy Districts account.

2. What Data is Preserved?

You’re probably wondering what data from your old Khan Academy accounts is preserved in your new Khan Academy Districts accounts, and what is lost.

  • The good news:
    • Your grassroots classes are preserved to refer back to.
      • BUT your district will want you to use the new Khan Academy Districts classes for any work students do in the future, so that the data shows appropriately on the administrator dashboards.
    • All student mastery progress data is preserved.
      • So, for example, if you create the same mastery goal for students in your new classes as one they were working on in their old classes, they will get credit for all of the mastery points they’ve already earned, and be at the same % progress as they were in your previous class.
  • The bad news:
    • Any assignments or mastery goals set in your previous grassroots classes, cannot be moved over to your new Khan Academy Districts classes. You’ll have to recreate them.
    • Even if you do recreate the same assignments for students in your new classes, if they had previously completed that assignment, the score will not transfer over.
      • Students will have to re-do the assignment in order for that score to be captured in the new class.
      • As mentioned previously though, mastery data will transfer over to the new mastery goals you create.

3. Class Dashboard Cleanup

As mentioned previously, any grassroots classes that you created before activating your Khan Academy Districts account will still remain active and on your teacher dashboard. Your district will want you and your students to transition to using the district-rostered Khan Academy Districts classes for data and reporting purposes.

To minimize student confusion, we recommend that you clean up your class dashboard after gathering the data you need from them, so that obsolete classes don’t show up in the product for students. You can easily delete classes from your teacher dashboard under the Settings tab.

Additional guidance on how to do this can be found in steps 2 and 3 of this Khan Academy Support Article

Need further guidance? Please reach out to our support team through this link!

What happens if I have more than one school district account?

While working on your student account on Khan Academy, you may end up with more than one school district account.

This can happen if, for example, one teacher added you to their class via the Clever portal, and another teacher (perhaps from a previous year) might have added you to their class by using your school email.

While it’s possible for our users to have multiple accounts, only one of them can have your school email, and this is the one that will be used if your teacher has their classes rostered for them by the school district (if they are using Khan Academy Districts or Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths).

If you have more than one school account, it could happen that you might be doing school work for your teacher in one account, but the other school district account containing your school email is the one that will be used when you are added to a new Khan Academy Districts or Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths class. At the moment, it’s not possible to merge accounts or transfer progress between them.

If you believe you might have more than one school district account and the one you’re accessing might not be the correct, feel free to contact us by reporting a problem if you’re unable to access the second school account, and our support team will be happy to help you regain access to that account directly.

Using Khan Academy Districts: Administrator Reports and Data

CSV Data Dictionary for Administrator Reports

Khan Academy offers administrators the option to export student data into downloadable CSV files they then can use for additional analysis and reporting outside of the Khan Academy platform. This document will go over the data included in those files, and how it is formatted.

To start off though, let’s answer the question: “What is a CSV?”

  • A CSV, or Comma Separated Values is a type of file that stores data.

  • In a CSV file, each line is a data record and each record consists of one or more fields, separated by commas.

  • It’s like a simple spreadsheet, but without the formulas and formatting.

  • You can then open CSV files in programs like Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or Numbers Khan Academy offers 4 types of CSV files for administrators to download. Click on the CSV title to jump to information about the data on it:

  • Overall Khan Academy Student Data CSV Report: File Name: District-name_daterange

  • Mastery Progress:

    • By Student CSV: File name: District-name_MasteryProgressStudent_daterange
    • By Classroom CSV: File name: District-name_MasteryProgressClassroom_daterange
    • Once exported, individual columns will show weekly progress data, from Monday-Sunday, with the last column on the document being the current week.
    • Please note: this report updates nightly starting on Mondays. That means if you export this report on a Monday before midnight, you wont see any progress yet for the current week.

  • Skills Progress:

    • All Skills CSV: File name: District-name_skills_progress_Course-name_daterange
    • Course Challenges Skills CSV: File name: District-name_CourseChallengeSkills_Course-name_daterange

  • Khanmigo CSV: (Available if your school district has purchased Khanmigo licenses for your teachers and/or students) File name: District-name_khanmigo

  • If your district also is a Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths customer, you will also see the below 2 additional CSV export options. You can learn more about those reports here

  • Learning Paths

  • Learning Paths Skills Progress Note: The numbers at the end of the file names are the date in this format: YYYYMMDD. Example: 20230710_20230717 means: July 10, 2023 through July 17, 2023

Now, let’s dive into the data that is included in these 5 files:

1. Overall Khan Academy Student Data CSV Report Data:

  • Column A: Student Name
  • Column B: Student Email
  • Column C: Student SIS ID
  • Column D: Roster Status (Rostered, No Longer Rostered, or Activated) If the student is no longer shared from Clever or Classlink to Khan Academy on the day the report is exported, the status will be “No Longer Rostered.” Rosters are updated every 24 hours
  • Column E: Rostered Grade (Please note: students who are rostered on Clever or ClassLink in grade levels outside the standard K-12 range, such as grades 13, 14, or PostGraduate, their grade level will be shown as “Other” in Khan Academy reports)
  • Column F: School (The name of the school(s) you selected)
  • Column G: Course (The Khan Academy course name(s) you selected. This column will appear if you only selected 1 course, or selected multiple courses, but chose not to have their data combined. The combined version skips the “Course” column, so Total learning minutes is in Column G instead)
  • Column H: Total learning minutes (Total active learning time completed, excluding non-learning activities like navigating the site)
  • Column I: Skills Worked on (Total number of skills that students practiced on)
  • Column J: Skills Leveled Up (Total number of skills worked on that moved up a mastery level by the end of date range)
  • Column K: Skills Leveled Up to Proficient or Higher (Total number of skills that moved up a mastery level and ended at the Proficient or Mastered level by the end of the date range)
  • Column L: Khanmigo chats (The number of chats with Khanmigo a student had associated with the course(s) selected)
  • Column M: Khanmigo Interactions (The number of interactions with Khanmigo a student had associated with the course(s) selected)

2. Mastery Progress Report CSV Data:

  • Student Mastery CSV
    • Column A: Student Name
    • Column B: Student Email
    • Column C: Student SIS ID
    • Column D: No longer rostered: (If the student is no longer shared from Clever or Classlink to Khan Academy on the day the report is exported, this column will say “True.” Rosters are updated every 24 hours)
    • Column E: Rostered Grade (please note: students who are rostered on Clever or ClassLink in grade levels outside the standard K-12 range, such as grades 13, 14, or PostGraduate, their grade level will be shown as “Other” in Khan Academy reports)
    • Column F: School Name
    • Column G: Domain (Subject area of the class)
      • Domain options: Math, Science, Arts and Humanities, Reading and Language Arts, Economics, Test Prep, Computing, Districts (for custom curated courses) or Life Skills
    • Column H: Course (The Khan Academy course added to the classroom. Example: The Algebra 1 Course)
      • Note: If the teacher did not add a course onto their classroom, the student data will not show up on the downloaded CSV
    • Column I: Shared Classrooms (Total number of classrooms a student is in that have the selected course added to it)
      • Note: If a student is in multiple classrooms working on the same course, they will have multiple rows on the CSV. Therefore, if you would like to see unique (non-duplicated) data, you should filter by “Shared Classrooms”=1
    • Column J: Section (class) Name
    • Column K: Section ID
    • Column L: Teacher Name (Primary teacher, not co-teacher)
    • Column M: Teacher Email (Primary teacher, not co-teacher)
    • Column N: Teacher SIS ID (Primary teacher, not co-teacher)
    • Column O: SIS Course Name
    • Column P: SIS Course ID
    • Column Q: Course Goals (Number of Course Mastery Goals added)
    • Column R: Unit Goals (Number of Unit Mastery Goals added)
    • Column S: YY.MM.DD CM % (Course Mastery % by that student for that given week)
    • Column T: YY.MM.DD CM pts (Course Mastery points earned (up to 100 points per skill) by the student in that given week) Some notes about Columns S, T and beyond:
  • A CM% and CM pts column are added for every week of the school year. Once the new school year starts, the previous school year’s data (including summer) will not be available anymore on the CSV.
  • Each column tracks data for a particular week: from Monday-Sunday. The date is shown in the YY.MM.DD format: 23.06.18 equals June 18, 2023
  • The last CM % and CM pts columns of the spreadsheet show the current week. Below is a gif showing an example of how the Student Mastery Progress CSV is formatted:

Below is a screenshot of columns S through V:

  • Columns U and V are the data from the following week: Sunday, August 27, 2023 through Saturday, September 2, 2023 .
  • Classroom Mastery CSV:
    • Column A: School Name
    • Column B: Section (class) Name
    • Column C: Section ID
    • Column D: KA Domain
    • Column E: KA Course
    • Column F: Teacher Name (Primary teacher, not co-teacher)
    • Column G: Teacher Email (Primary teacher, not co-teacher)
    • Column H: Teacher SIS ID (Primary teacher, not co-teacher)
    • Column I: SIS Course Name
    • Column J: SIS Course ID
    • Column K: Activated Students in class
    • Column L: Course Goals (Number of Course Mastery Goals added)
    • Column M: Unit Goals (Number of Unit Mastery Goals added)
    • Column N: YY.MM.DD Median CM % (Median Course Mastery % of activated students for that given week)
    • Column O: YY.MM.DD students with progress (Number of students who made progress towards Course Mastery in the designated week) Some notes about Columns N, O and beyond:
  • A Median CM% and Students with Progress column are added for every week of the school year. Please note that Khan Academy does not track Mastery data throughout the summer.
  • Each column tracks data for a particular week: from Monday-Sunday. The date is shown in the YY.MM.DD format: 23.06.18 equals June 18, 2023
  • The last CM % and CM pts columns of the spreadsheet show the current week. Below is a gif showing an example of how the Classroom Mastery Progress CSV is formatted:

Below is a screenshot of columns N through Q:

  • Columns P and Q are the data from the following week: Sunday, August 27, 2023 through Saturday, September 2, 2023 .

How do I export a CSV file for Khan Academy Districts administrator reports?

Khan Academy offers administrators the option to export student data into downloadable CSV files that they can use for additional analysis and reporting outside of the Khan Academy platform. This document will go over how to export data and download the report as a CSV.

To start off though, let’s answer the question: “What is a CSV?”

  • A CSV, or Comma Separated Values is a type of file that stores data.

  • In a CSV file, each line is a data record and each record consists of one or more fields, separated by commas.

  • It’s like a simple spreadsheet, but without the formulas and formatting.

  • You can then open CSV files in programs like Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or Numbers The Export Student Data tab on your Administrator dashboard offers 4 categories of data available for download as CSV files:

  • Overall:

    • This option includes data from all the tabs if applicable, as well as data from Khanmigo for each course selected
    • Customization options:
      • Date range: today, last 7 days, last 30 days, or custom date range
      • Schools: select any or all schools
      • Khan course: select which Khan Academy course(s)

  • Skills Progress:

    • This option allows administrators to zoom in on students’ Mastery progress as broken down by a particular Khan Course or Course Challenge
    • Customization options:
      • Date range: today, last 7 days, last 30 days, or custom date range
      • Khan course
      • Schools
      • Grades
      • District course (as shown on the SIS)
      • Teachers

  • Khanmigo Use Data:

    • Available if your district has purchased Khanmigo licenses for your students and/or teachers
    • This csv shows helpful data about how those in your district are interacting with Khanmigo, including number of flagged chats, and tokens used.
    • You can learn more about the Khanmigo Administrator reports here

  • Learning Paths:

    • Available if your district also has purchased Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths powered by MAP Growth
    • You can learn more about the Learning Paths Administrator reports here

  • Learning Paths Skills Progress:

    • If your district also has purchased Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths powered by MAP Growth
    • You can learn more about the Learning Paths Administrator reports here To export student data via a CSV, please follow the below steps:

For more information about the data found on the downloaded CSVs and its format, please check out this article from the Khan Academy Help Center: CSV Data Dictionary for Administrator Reports

How do I use the Activation administrator reports?

Khan Academy provides many reports for administrators to monitor and track student learning progress with. This article will give you an overview of the different Activation Reports Khan Academy offers to administrators and how to use them.

To start off though, let’s answer “What is Activation?”

Activation occurs once a Khan Academy account is successfully linked with a school’s SIS roster. Activation reports allow administrators to monitor how many of the users in their district have their accounts ready to utilize the Khan Academy product, while also helping identify where additional support is needed to do so.

There are 3 report options to zoom into activation data:

  • Activation by school

  • Activation by grades

  • Activation by teachers To navigate to these reports, please follow the below steps:

  • Click your name in the top right corner

  • Click “Administrator Dashboard” from the dropdown menu

  • Click the “Activation” category on the left-hand menu

  • Click which activation report you would like to view Please note:

  • You can filter out which schools you’d like to see the data for at the top of each activation report

  • Clicking on a column category adjusts the sorting order of the report (largest to smallest, or smallest to largest)

  • Hovering over the column title shows additional information about what is included in the metric

  • The activation reports are updated each night, not in real time For more information about each of the administrator reports and export options Khan Academy offers, please check out this section of the help center: Using Khan Academy Districts: Administrator Reports and Data

How do I use the different Progress reports for administrators?

Khan Academy provides many reports for administrators to monitor and track student learning progress with. This article will give you an overview of the different Progress Reports offered to administrators, the data analysis options for the reports, and some specific technical aspects to keep in mind when using them.

Since each school and district may have different data needs, Administrators have 5 different options to monitor student progress:

  • Progress by Courses
  • Progress by Site
  • Progress by Grades
  • Progress by Teachers
  • Skills Progress Each of these reports are accessible on the Administrator Dashboard by clicking the “Progress” tab on the “Reports” page, and then selecting the report you would like to view.

The below features are available on the Progress by Course, Schools, Grades and Teachers reports:

  • Targeted subject areas. Click “More” to see all the options
  • Minimum active students customization option. Use this to filter out schools, teachers or classes
  • Only show courses added by teacher customization option. Select this box for more targeted data
  • Customizable filters for selecting specific subject date ranges, schools and grades. Click “Apply” after selecting your filters to see the results.
  • When you hover over the column titles, a tooltip appears and explains more about the metrics.
  • Reverse the sorting order from high-low, to low-high by clicking on the “Total” “Average” or “Proficiency” column titles Below is an image outlining these features:

Some additional data analysis options for the Progress by Course, Site, Grades, and Teachers reports:

  • Whenever you see a > symbol, that means the data can be expanded and drilled into further.
  • When you click on a student’s name, you are taken to their Individual Student Skill report which shows information on all their skills progress while working on Khan Academy. Below is a GIF showing this functionality:

A few reminders to keep in mind when using the Progress by Course, Site, Grades and Teachers reports:

  • The Khan Academy course has to be added by the teacher to their classroom in order to be tracked on the Progress by Course report.
  • The columns with “average” values use “Activated students” as the denominator.
  • Co-teachers will not show up on the “Progress by Teacher” report Now, let’s dive into how to use the Skills Progress report, as this has slightly different functionality than the Progress by Courses, Schools, Grades, and Teachers reports.

The Skills Progress report allows administrators deeper insight into which skills students have demonstrated understanding, and which ones might still need more focus.

The Skills Progress report offers the below customizable filters:

  • Date Range: (Today, last 7 days, last 30 days, or custom range)
    • Please note: Progress data available for this report goes back to October 2021. Skills worked on before this date will not show up on the report.
  • Khan course: (The Khan Academy course added to the classroom. Example: Algebra 1)
    • Please note: that the teacher must have added the course to their classroom in order for the student work to appear on this report)
  • Schools
    • Please note: if you’re not seeing a school you expected to see listed here, you might not have Admin access to that school’s data on Clever or Classlink.
  • Grades
  • District Course (Optional field, as not all districts use course IDs on Clever or Classlink to roster with Khan Academy)
  • Teachers (Optional field. Only Primary Teachers will show as options here. If unselected, all teachers from the selected schools and grades will be displayed) After selecting your filters, the report will show the data available according to the chosen criteria.

Below are some additional data analysis options for the Skills Progress report:

  • Combined and Unit view
    • Use this drop-down menu to choose whether to display all the skills in a Combined view or by skills listed in each unit in the Unit view.
  • Sorting options
    • Use this drop-down menu to choose one of the several sorting options. To quickly identify which skills students need more support on, sort by Attempted (high to low)
    • For more information on how the Khan Academy’s Mastery levels work, check out this article.
  • Mastery levels
    • On the top right corner of the results window, you can find the interactive Mastery levels matching the progress bar colors. Click on a proficiency level to hide it from the progress bars below.
    • In the Unit view, the Mastery levels can be enabled or disabled by unit.
  • Progress bars
    • The progress bars show the number of students that worked on each skill in different colors for each Mastery level achieved.
    • Hovering over each bar shows the total of students that worked on that skill and a breakdown of students by Mastery level. Clicking on each Mastery level brings up the list of students included.
    • Clicking on a student’s name in the list takes you to their Individual Progress Report, giving you an overview of that student’s progress across skills. If you would like to explore the data from the Skills Progress Report, there are two options:
  • Save as image icon
    • After making the desired selections and choosing the viewing and sorting options that best fit your needs, click on the Save as Image icon in the upper right corner to save the current view as a .jpeg image.
    • In the Unit view, each unit view can be saved separately.
  • CSV Export link
    • If you’d like to explore the Skills Report data further on your own device, click on the CSV Export link in the upper right corner to go to the Export Student Data page and then click on the Skills Progress tab.
    • To learn more about how to export a CSV file of student data, check out this article: How do I export a CSV file for Khan Academy Districts administrator reports? We hope these Progress reports give you access to the data you need to understand and support your students throughout their learning journeys!

If you have feedback about how you use these features or ideas for improvements, please share your thoughts with your District Success Manager or contact our support team. We’d love to hear from you!

How do I use the Khanmigo Activity Administrator Report?

Khan Academy offers 2 reports for districts who have Khanmigo to understand how it is being used in their school(s): the Khanmigo Usage and Khanmigo Activity reports. You can also download Khanmigo usage data to a CSV file.

This article will cover the Khanmigo Activity Report, which was designed for you to see the top Khanmigo activities and places around Khan Academy where your students are using Khanmigo.

Below is some helpful info and pointers to keep in mind as you navigate the Khanmigo Activity Report:

These are outlined in the screenshot and corresponding numbered list below:

  • Where is this report located? The Khanmigo Usage Report is found on your Administrator Dashboard under the Khanmigo section
  • Toggle between the Students Usage Report and Teachers Usage report
    • Please note: if a student or teacher has not activated their Khan Academy account, they will not be included in this data
    • If a student or teacher is removed from your Clever or Classlink roster, their data will not show up on this report
  • Select which school(s) in your district you’d like to see the data for
  • Date range you’d like to see the data for on the Bar Graph showing the number of active students or teachers
    • Hover over the bar graphs to see the % of active users
    • The percentage of Unique Users is the number of students in each category divided by the total number of students on the top row
  • Sortable filters: click to sort the columns, or hover over the column title for more information on what is included in the data
    • Number of students or teachers
    • % of unique users
  • Expandable categorical data
    • Click the < to see more information broken down by course and unit
    • Note: the numbers when you expand the with an article, video or exercise categories may not always add up as the user may have worked on more than one article, video or exercise.
    • Once the info is expanded, the lists can be sorted alphabetically or numerically by clicking on the column title
    • If you see the “Other” category, it means the student was chatting with Khanmigo on their Learner Home, or in the Give me feedback on my academic essay activity
    • The “Challenge” category means the user was working on a Computer Science challenge in any of the Computing Programming Courses We hope this article was helpful in understanding the Khanmigo Activity Report! If you have questions or need further assistance, please contact your District Success Manager, or reach out to our Support team here.

What data is included on the Administrator Homepage?

Khan Academy provides many reports for administrators to monitor and track learning progress with. This article will give you an overview of the Administrator Homepage, which is designed for administrators to quickly receive a high-level overview of a variety of data and connect you to helpful resources.

The key features of the Administrator Homepage are outlined below:

  • Activation Summary: shows the number of students who have been rostered, activated and started a Khan Academy activity
  • Resources: Links to helpful resources applicable to administrators
  • Skills to Proficient and Above Summary: Average that is calculated by taking the total number of skills which reached the Proficient or Mastered level by activated students in the district and dividing it by the total number of activated students
  • Khanmigo Usage Summary: only if the district has Khanmigo licenses added to their rostered users. Shows how often and for what students are using Khanmigo for
  • Learning Time Summary: Learning time by active students including Khanmigo usage
  • Skills Leveled up Summary: Average that is calculated by taking the total number of skills which reached the Attempted, Familiar, Proficient or Mastered levels by activated students in the district and dividing it by the total number of activated students Learning Paths tab:

If your district has purchased Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths linked to MAP Growth licenses, you will see an additional tab with similar data to the Overall tab:

  • Activation Summary, Skills to Prof+ Summary for Learning Paths skills, Learning Time Summary for Learning Paths skills, Skills Leveled up Summary for Learning Paths skills To navigate to the Administrator Homepage please follow the below steps:

  • Log into your Khan Academy administrator account

  • Click your name in the top right corner

  • Click “Administrator Dashboard” from the dropdown menu

  • You can also get to the Homepage from anywhere on your Administrator Dashboard by clicking the “Home” option on the lefthand sidebar Frequently Asked Questions:

Question: Can I filter the homepage to see data from particular schools in my district?

  • Answer: Yes! There is a school filter in the top right corner of the Administrator Homepage. You can select one or multiple schools Question: How does the homepage handle students who are no longer rostered?

  • Answer: The only place you will be able to see data for students who are no longer rostered, will be on the downloadable CSVs only, which are available on the “Export Student Data” tab. Question: Can I adjust the date ranges shown on the Administrator Homepage?

  • Answer: Not on the Homepage, which is programmed to show data from throughout the school year. If you would like more customizable date ranges, we recommend using the Administrator reports, which are highly customizable. Question: Do I see the information from all the work the rostered students in my district have done on the Administrator Homepage?

  • Answer: The Skills to Proficient+, Learning Minutes, and Skills leveled-up metrics show the work students have done in class context, meaning only on Khan Academy courses that have been added by the teacher to the district synced class. We hope this article helps you understand the Administrator Homepage! If you have questions or need additional support, please reach out to your Districts Success Manager, or contact the Khan Academy Support team. We are here to help and thank you for choosing Khan Academy Districts!

What reports does Khan Academy offer to administrators?

Khan Academy Districts provide a variety of reports for administrators to monitor the implementation of Khan Academy in their schools. In addition to the in-product reports, data can be exported into downloadable CSV files that administrators can use for further analysis. This article will give you an overview of each administrator report and the data download options Khan Academy offers to administrators.

  • Administrator Homepage: This page gives administrators a high-level overview of a variety of data. The key features of the homepage are outlined below:

  • Activation Summary: shows the number of students who have been rostered, activated and started a Khan Academy activity

  • Resources: Links to helpful resources applicable to administrators

  • Skills to Proficient and Above Summary: Average that is calculated by taking the total number of skills that reached the Proficient or Mastered level by activated students in the district and dividing it by the total number of activated students

  • Khanmigo Usage Summary: only if the district has Khanmigo licenses added to their rostered users. Shows how often and for what students are using Khanmigo for

  • Learning Time Summary: Learning time by active students including Khanmigo usage

  • Skills Leveled up Summary: Average that is calculated by taking the total number of skills that reached the Attempted, Familiar, Proficient, or Mastered levels by activated students in the district and dividing it by the total number of activated students

  • Activation Reports: These reports show the amount of users who are rostered with Khan Academy Districts, and whose accounts are successfully activated. Monitoring activation rates can be helpful for admins to see how many of the users in their district have their accounts ready to utilize the Khan Academy product, while also helping identify where additional support is needed to do so. There are 3 report options to zoom into activation data:

  • Activation by Site

  • Activation by Grades

  • Activation by Teachers

  • Progress Reports: These reports show Administrators how activated students in their district are progressing on the content they’ve been working on. These reports are highly customizable and give administrators the options to drill down into progress data broken down by:

  • Courses, Site, Grades, Teachers or Skills

  • Course Progression: this report offers administrators a high-level view of mastery for a given Khan Academy course across schools and grades in their district. It is customizable and gives administrators the opportunity to quickly identify areas of success and struggle as students are on the path toward mastery.

  • Khanmigo Reports:

  • - Khanmigo Usage Report: Shows how many students + teachers are using Khanmigo, how much are they using it, and has the ability to drill down to isolate areas of interest or unusual activity.

    • Khanmigo Activity Report: Shows the top activities and where students + teachers are using Khanmigo across Khan Academy.

  • SAT Reports:

  • If students are preparing for the Digital SAT through Khan Academy’s Official Digital SAT Prep, administrators can monitor data through:

    • The Progress by Course report
    • Selecting the Digital SAT course on the Skills Progress report.

  • If your district is also a Khan Academy Districts + Learning Paths customer, we offer specific reports tailored to you. You can learn more about these in the Learning Paths section of the help center

In addition to these in-product reports, the Export Student Data section offers many customizable report options for administrators to download as CSV files.

These include:

  • Overall student data
  • Course progression data
  • Skills progress data
  • Khanmigo CSV: available if your district has purchased Khanmigo licenses for your students
  • Learning Paths: available if your district has purchased Learning Paths licenses for your students
  • Learning Paths Skills Progress: available if your district has purchased Learning Paths licenses for your students For more information about each of the administrator reports and export options Khan Academy offers, please check out this section of the Khan Academy Help Center: Using KAD: Administrator Reports and Data.

If you have further questions, please contact your Districts Success Manager, or reach out to our support team. We are here and happy to help!

What SAT data is available to administrators?

Khan Academy offers administrators insights into students that are preparing for the digital SAT on Khan Academy.

Below is an image showing a high level overview of where you can access the data on the Digital SAT from your Administrator Dashboard:

Now let’s dive in a bit deeper to learn more about the options highlighted above:

Digital SAT Prep Data: If students are preparing for the Digital SAT test through Khan Academy’s Official Digital SAT Prep courses, administrators can monitor data through the below options:

  • Selecting the SAT tab on the Progress by Course, Site, Grades, or Teachers reports.
    • Please note: If the SAT tab isn’t visible, click the “Subject” option, then select SAT. Below is a GIF showing this navigation:

Using Khan Academy Districts: Implementation Resources

FAQ for [Non-US] Khan Academy Partnerships

For Administrators

What is the District’s International Partnership?

It allows teachers to create and manage their own classes on Khan Academy and connect them to a school or district partnership, without using tools like Clever or ClassLink.

Who should use the District’s International Partnership?

Is a good fit if:

  • Your school or district is part of a Khan Academy partnership
  • You are not using Clever or ClassLink for rostering
  • You’ve been asked to create and link your own classes.

For Teachers

Can I change Schools if I selected the wrong one?

Yes. If you selected the wrong school and are seeing incorrect information, you can update your school in your account settings to make sure your classes and students are linked correctly.

What changes after I mark my class as a district class?

  • Your class appears in district reports (if available)
  • Your class may gain access to partnership features, like Khanmigo, in some programs
  • Your class is officially recognized as part of your school,or district, partnership Will I lose student progress if I connect a class later?

No, all student work and progress stay in your class.

Please note that district reports typically only include activity from the day you connect the class. Earlier work remains visible in your class, but may not appear in reports.

Can I still manage my class and students normally after connecting it?

You can continue to:

  • Add or remove students
  • Assign content
  • Track progress
  • Edit their settings. For detailed steps, refer to this helpful article: How can I adjust a student’s settings, such as their username or password? Everything works the same, with the added benefit of district reporting!

Do students log in differently?

No, students continue using Khan Academy the same way. The District partnership only affects how classes connect to your school, or district, and how data is shared in reports.

Why am I unable to see the option to mark my class as a district class?

This may happen if:

  • Your school isn’t set up or selected correctly
  • Your account isn’t recognized as a teacher at that school
  • Your region uses a different rostering method Try confirming your school in your account settings. If the option still doesn’t appear, contact your school or district, or reach out to Khan Academy support.

What happens to classes at the end of the school year?

This varies by partnership and country, but often:

  • You will be asked to confirm active classes
  • Unconfirmed classes will be archived or removed Please be sure to check with your school or district for specific guidance.

Do you need to clean up your classes manually?

To avoid waiting until the end of the school year to confirm inactive classes, you can also:

  • Delete an unwanted class:
    • You can do so by navigating to the “Settings” tab of the specific class you want to remove.
      • For detailed steps, refer to this helpful article How do I delete a class on Khan Academy.
  • Remove a class from the district:
  • This is the best course of action if you initially linked to the wrong partnership.
    • To do so, navigate to the specific class from your Teacher Dashboard and select the “Remove” option.
    • A confirmation prompt will appear, verifying that the class will no longer be associated with the school. What options do administrators and teachers have to make roster changes?

Administrators:

  • Are currently unable to remove teachers who have been incorrectly linked to a district. Teachers should be very careful when selecting their school or partnership.

  • Can remove students from any synced classes

    • After a student is removed, the Manage Roster page takes approximately one hour to reflect the update. The activation and progress reports will then be updated within the following two hours. Teachers:

  • Can take away a student’s spot on the roster.

  • Has the ability to opt out of a partnership. If you would like a step-by-step guide on how to connect your classes, please check out the article below:

  • Linking your class to a [Non-US] Khan Academy Partnership.

How can administrators recommend and assign Unit Mastery Goals to teachers?

Khan Academy Districts administrators can recommend and assign Unit Mastery Goals (UMGs) to teachers in their district. Unit Mastery Goals are targets set for students to achieve Mastery in specific units of a Khan Academy course. Having an administrator assign these helps save teachers time and guide classroom instruction by setting clear, trackable targets.

Who can assign Unit Mastery Goals?

Only administrators with certain high-level permissions have access to assign Unit Mastery Goals on behalf of teachers. We call these users “Super Administrators.”

You’ll know who is a Super Administrator by:

  • Visiting the “Manage Administrators” section of your Administrator Dashboard.
  • Those who have “District” under the “Admin Role” column and “Manage” under the “Permission” column have access to this feature. Please contact your Khan Academy District Success Manager or another Super Admin if you need, but do not have, the permissions needed for this feature.

How do the Unit Mastery Goals administrators assign show up to teachers?

There are 2 ways the Unit Mastery Goal assignments from administrators can appear to teachers:

  1. If the teacher does not have Unit Mastery Goals already assigned to their students:
  • The admin’s assignments will be automatically assigned once the nightly roster sync occurs.
  • The teacher will see the below popup on their class that reads “Classroom assignments are ready!”
  • The teacher can then click the “Review assignments” button on the popup to learn more about what the administrator assigned. They also can always go back in and edit or adjust the assignments on their teacher dashboard as well.
  1. If a teacher already has similar or identical unit mastery goals for their classes:
  • After the nightly roster sync, an administrator’s Unit Mastery Goal assignments will appear on the teacher’s dashboard as recommendations.
  • Teachers will see blue banners on their class’ “Activity Overview” page telling them they have Mastery recommendations.
  • Then the teacher will click “View recommendations” and accept, or dismiss the administrator’s recommendations.

How to assign Unit Mastery Goals as an administrator

Follow the below 8 steps to assign Unit Mastery Goals to teachers in your district:

  • Visit the “Settings” section of your Administrator Dashboard
  • Click the blue “Manage Courses” button
  • Select which subject areas and Clever roster subjects you would like to assign the Unit Mastery Goals on.
  • Click “Review courses”
  • Create Clever course groupings based on those working on similar subject matter.
  • You’ll do this by:
    • Clicking “add course group”
    • Select which Clever courses you would like to be in a group.
      • For math courses, the Clever section must have the subject labeled as math.
      • For Digital SAT, sections don’t require subject tags, but only high school grade levels will appear on this feature.
    • Clicking “Save changes”
  1. Add the applicable Khan Academy course(s) to this group of Clever course(s).

We will suggest some courses for you, but feel free to adjust them and select what is most applicable.

  • Click “Edit units” to customize the selected unit mastery goals in the course and their due dates
  • Final step! Click “Publish Changes” at the bottom of the page and complete the confirmation modal We hope this article was helpful in understanding how administrators can assign Unit Mastery Goals to their teachers’ classrooms! If you have any questions or need additional information, please feel free to contact your District Success Manager, or reach out to the Khan Academy Support Team through this link.

How can Administrators use the Classroom Access feature to act as a Khan Academy Districts teacher?

Classroom Access is a feature which lets administrators temporarily enter their teachers’ classrooms and act as a co-teacher. When an admin uses Classroom Access, they can take all the same actions as the classroom teacher for the duration of their access. This makes it possible for administrators to:

  • Support classrooms that don’t yet have an activated teacher
  • Assist teachers who need additional support
  • Step in as a substitute teacher

Who can use Classroom access?

  • The Classroom Access feature is available for those with the Administrator Dashboard on their Khan Academy account.
  • From the Administrator Dashboard, you will see Classroom Access on the left sidebar

How do administrators enter a class using the Classroom Access feature?

  • Click “Classroom Access” from the “Classes” tab in the Administrator Dashboard overview menu.
  • If you haven’t added any classes yet, click Add classes.
    • You can add any class in the schools you already have access to on your Khan Academy account.
    • If a teacher on the list is greyed out, it means they do not have any classes available for the admin to enter.
  • Click Enter next to the class name you’d like to join
    • Note: When you click Enter, the class will open in a new tab. To get back to your Admin Dashboard, just switch back to your original tab.
    1. That’s it! Now you are a co-teacher in the class and can take actions like:
  • Making Mastery Goals and content assignments (resources on how to do this)
  • View and export teacher reports showing student assignment scores (resources on this)
How long will I have access to the classes?

By default, admins will have access for 7 days when you first add a class—but you can change this anytime:

  • When adding a class you can select a custom end date.
  • After adding a class, click the calendar icon next to the current expiration date and adjust it. Note: Access ends at the close of the selected day after rostering runs. Example: If your access is set to end on Jan 1, you’ll still have access through that day. On Jan 2, access will expire unless you extend it.
Will teachers and students know I’m in their class?

Yes. While your access is active:

  • Teachers will see you listed as a co-teacher on their settings page.
  • Students will also see your name if they check the list of their teachers. We hope this article was helpful in understanding Khan Academy’s Classroom Access tool! Please reach out to your Districts Success Manager, or submit a support request if you need additional assistance.

How can Khan Academy Districts teachers create a class that is district-synced?

When a Khan Academy Districts teacher creates a class in which all the students are also district-synced, the class becomes district-synced itself.

This is designed to:

  • Unlock assignable Khanmigo activities for classes teachers manually create.
  • Give teachers flexibility in creating their own classes, while still ensuring student progress counts toward district reports. This article will go over some details for teachers and administrators about the feature.

How class upgrade works:

  • Khan Academy Districts teachers can automatically receive classes from Clever or ClassLink. These classes have the “District-synced” label on their Teacher Dashboard.
  • However, they also can create their own classes from their Teacher Dashboard.
  • Once a teacher creates a new class which is comprised entirely of district-synced students, behind the scenes, the class is “upgraded” to be district-synced as well.
  • Please note: Upgraded classes do not look different from other classes a teacher creates. They do not display a “District Synced” badge, and teachers will not receive any notifications when a class has been upgraded.
  • Google Classroom and Clever Library: Class upgrade applies to Google Classroom and Clever Library synced-classes as long as all the students in the classes are also rostered in a district-synced class.

Who can use the class upgrade feature?

  • Any teacher or administrator who is rostered onto Khan Academy from their district’s Clever or ClassLink roster can use this feature. This includes co-teachers.
  • Administrators may need to add the teacher role onto their Khan Academy account if they are not seeing it. Here is an article on how to do this

How do I add students already connected to my account into a new class I created?

  • Glad you asked! It’s super easy.
  • Here is an article on how to do it and below are the steps
    • From your Teacher Dashboard, click the “Students” tab
    • Select the desired students
    • Tip! You will know if a student is district-synced if they are already in one of your classes with the “District-synced” label. You’ll also see their district-synced email in the middle column.
    • Click “Actions” and “Add to class”

A few notes for Khan Academy District Administrators:

  • District reports: Upgraded classes appear immediately in district progress reports. Please note that activation reports may take up to an hour to update.
  • District SIS: Upgraded classes do not sync with the district SIS and are not affected by overnight roster syncs. These classes exist only within Khan Academy.
  • If a district-synced teacher creates a class with no students—this class will upgrade automatically, and remain upgraded as long as only district students are added.
  • If any student in the class does not belong to the district, the class will not upgrade. If non-district students are added later, the class will lose its district designation. We hope this article was helpful in understanding the class upgrade feature! If you have additional questions, please contact your District Success Manager, or submit a ticket to the Khan Academy Support Team.

How can Khan Academy Districts Teachers use the Quick Assign feature?

Teachers in Khan Academy District partnerships can quickly generate links for Khan Academy assignments. Sharing these links on your preferred platform or LMS can make accessing the assignment easier and quicker for your students!

How to use this feature?

  1. Upon creating a new assignment for your district-synced class(es), the Quick Assign pop-up will show the share link automatically
  • A perk of this feature is that even if the student wasn’t given the assignment on Khan Academy, as long as they are in the class the assignment was made in, they will be able to access the assignment through the share link! NOTE: the share link is not available for Course or Unit Mastery goals. It is available for every other type of assignment on Khan Academy though, including Khanmigo assignments.
  1. The share link is also located on the “Manage” tab
  • Then click on the three dots on the right side of the page, followed by “Share” from the dropdown.
  1. Copy and share the link with your students!
  • Once they complete the assignment from the link, they will receive a credit for the assignment in your class. NOTE: If a student is not a part of your class, then they will receive the below error message, notifying them that they do not have access to that assignment. Please be sure to double-check that the students are all added to your class before sending them the link.

Have questions or having trouble with this feature? Feel free to reach out to our support team through this link. We are here to help!

How do district administrators set Khan Academy implementation goals?

Khan Academy District administrators can set target goals to more effectively track, monitor, and communicate their district’s goals for student learning on Khan Academy. Setting a target goal can help lead to a successful Khan Academy implementation.

This article will cover the below topics:

  1. How to set a target goal, along with how to edit an existing target goal

  2. The target goals available and what they each mean

  • In this section we will also cover which target goals Khan Academy recommends setting for efficacious use and improved student learning outcomes

  1. Who can set target goals on Khan Academy Districts

  2. How to track progress towards reaching a target goal

How to set a target goal:

Target goals can be made via these 3 methods:

  1. The goal setting pop-up which shows upon login for eligible users.

NOTE: Selecting a goal from the pop-up results in 3 goals automatically being set for your district. We recommend then customizing these target goals from your administrator dashboard.

  1. The blue “Set a goal” button on the Administrator Dashboard for eligible users. Clicking on this will open the same pop-up modal from option #1 above

  2. Clicking the “Add target” link located on the Administrator Dashboard next to each of the available target goal categories

How to edit a target goal:

To edit a target goal, click the “Edit” link from the link located on the Administrator Dashboard next to each of the existing target goal

Which target goals are available and what do they mean?

The target goals available to be set on the pop-up are:

  1. Students reaching grade level proficiency in math.

Selecting this results in 3 goal targets being set:

- Activation - 80% for all users

- Course Mastery - 80% completion for the chosen Khan Academy courses by the end of the school year

- Skills to Proficient - students will aim to reach proficiency on two Khan Academy skills per week

  1. Students achieving college readiness with Digital SAT prep

Selecting this option will set 3 district target goals:

- Activation - 80% for all users

- Course Mastery for DSAT Reading & DSAT Math courses - 80% course completion by the end of the school year

- Skills to Proficient - students will reach proficiency on two Khan Academy skills per week.

  1. Students filling in gaps in prerequisite learning

Selecting this option will set 3 district target goals:

  • Activation - 80% for all users

- Skills to Proficient - students will reach proficiency on two skills per week.

  • Learning Time - students will spend 30 minutes per week practicing on Khan Academy.
  1. Enabling students to explore AI for learning

Selecting this option will set 3 district target goals:

- Activation - 80% for all users

  • Khanmigo usage - 50% of students are active on Khanmigo each week.

- Skills to Proficient - students will reach proficiency on two skills per week.

  1. Other

Typing in a goal and clicking “Save” on the Goal Setting Pop up will still set three district targets:

  • Activation - 80% for all users

- Skills to Proficient - students will reach proficiency on two skills per week.

  • Learning Time - students will spend 30 minutes per week practicing on Khan Academy.

However, once you complete the pop-up screen, the goals are highly customizable from the administrator dashboard. We recommend then customizing these automatically set target goals from your administrator dashboard.

After completing the Goal Setting set up modal, you will have the ability to edit or set targets for the following categories:

  • Account activation
  • Course Mastery targets for your selected course(s)
  • Skills to Proficient
  • Learning Minutes
  • Khanmigo Usage
    • (If your district has not purchased Khanmigo, you will not be prompted to set Khanmigo usage targets.)
Who can access the Goal Setting feature?

Only district Super Admins have access to the Goal Setting feature. To be a Super Admin, you must be a district-wide administrator and have access to the In-Product Admin Rostering feature.

How to verify if you have Super Admin access:

  • Log in to your Khan Academy account.
  • Ensure that you are on your Administrator Dashboard.
  • In the left-hand navigation bar, go to Admin Tools. Verify that you have access to the Manage Administrators tool.
What targets does Khan Academy recommend for efficacious use and student learning outcomes?
  • Account activation - Khan Academy recommends that 80% of students have activated their accounts.
  • Course Mastery targets - Khan Academy recommends that students achieve 80% course mastery for the courses that support the district’s learning objectives.
  • Skills to Proficient - Khan Academy recommends that students reach Proficiency on 2 skills per week and 60 skills in one school year.
Monitoring progress toward district goals

District staff members with access to Khan Academy administrator reports can view and monitor district targets set by Super Admins through the below options:

Administrator Home Page

On the Administrator Home Page, admins can view district targets and if the district met its target for a specific date range. Admins can view this data for any school with which their account is associated.

Administrator Progress Reports

To monitor progress for specific schools, classes, or users, click View Report. From here, admins can view progress toward district targets for more granular data sets within a selected timeframe.

Schools or user groups meeting district targets will have a green check mark noted.

We hope this was helpful, and please don’t hesitate to reach out to your District Success Manager, or the Khan Academy Support Team if you have questions! We are here to help.

Using reports to track student work on Khan Academy

How can I see the Unit Mastery Goals and learning targets set by my administrator?

Administrators in Khan Academy partner districts can set Unit Mastery Goals or district-wide learning targets for their teachers. These are designed to alleviate some of the manual work on teachers’ shoulders and ensure alignment with school-wide priorities. This article will cover where you can view them on your Teacher Dashboard and if they are editable.

Where can I see the Unit Mastery Goals and targets my administrator has set for me?

These can appear in two ways on your dashboard, depending on whether you’ve already assigned your own Unit Mastery Goals:

  1. If you haven’t assigned Unit Mastery Goals in the same course as your admin:
  • UMGs from your admin will be automatically assigned to your students
  • You’ll see a popup on your class page that says “Classroom assignments are ready!” Click “Review assignments” to view the Unit Mastery Goals that have been assigned.
  • You can edit or remove these Unit Mastery Goals at any time from your Teacher Dashboard.
    • To do this: click the “Progress” section on your teacher dashboard, followed by the 3 dots next to the Unit Mastery Goal you would like to make changes to. Then, select the “Edit goal” or “Delete goal” option.
  1. If you have already assigned Unit Mastery Goals in the same course as your admin:
  • Your admin’s goals will appear as recommendations, not auto-assignments.
  • You’ll see a blue banner on your class’ Activity Overview page. Click “View recommendations” to review them. You can choose to accept or dismiss each recommendation.
  • If you accept the recommendations from your Admin and then change your mind later, you can edit or remove these goals at any time from your Teacher Dashboard.

Where can I see my district targets?

In addition to Unit Mastery Goals, administrators may set district learning targets. These are view-only for teachers and cannot be edited.

You can view your district targets on two places in your Teacher Dashboard:

  • On the Mastery tab of the Activity Overview section
  • On the Activity tab of the Activity Overview section

Types of targets your administrator might set:

  • Course Mastery targets (e.g., “Achieve 90% progress in Algebra 1”)
  • Skills leveled up (e.g., “60% of students leveled up in at least 2 Math skills last week”)
  • Skills leveled up to Proficient
  • Learning minutes (e.g., “60% of students spent at least 30 minutes in the last week”)
  • Khanmigo usage (e.g., “60% of students used Khanmigo in the last week”) These goals are tracked to support progress and alignment, but only administrators can edit them.

We hope this article was helpful for you in understanding how to see the Unit Mastery Goals and targets your administrator has made for you. If you have further questions, feel free to reach out to your Khan Academy Districts Success Manager or submit a ticket to our support team.

How can I view my students’ progress towards their Unit Missions?

These can be assigned by the teacher to their students and monitored on the Teacher Dashboard. This article will give instructions on how you can view student progress towards assigned Unit Missions

Once you have assigned a Unit Mission to any of your students, please follow the steps outlined below to see your student’s progress toward meeting the goal.

  • Log in to your Khan Academy account, navigate to your Teacher Dashboard, and select the class for which you want to view Mastery progress.
  • Once there, click “Reports” on the left-hand side window
  • Click “Assignments”
  • Click on the title of the Unit Mission assignment
  • This will open up a chart which lists your students’ Mastery percentage for that unit
  • You can also view Mastery progress data at the unit level on the “Assignments” tab.
  • To do so:
    • Click “Assignments” from the lefthand menu
    • Click on a Unit Mission assignment
    • Click “Student summary”
  • This will show when students completed the Unit Mission, how many content items in the Unit Mission they have completed, and the number of Skills to proficient (or Mastered) each student has. We hope this article provides helpful guidance on monitoring students’ progress throughout Unit Missions!

For additional help and support, please reach out to our support team here! We are happy to help.

How do activities that my students start over appear in my teacher reports?

The “Start Over” link allows learners to restart practice exercises, quizzes, or unit tests after answering two questions incorrectly.

This guide for teachers explains how this link will be visible to students and details what happens when it’s used, including the process for the bonus question.

📘Reporting implications for teachers:

  • The Individual Student Report (ISR) will indicate when a student used the “Start over” link, by showing “Used ‘Start over’” in the Date column:
    • Here is an article from our Help Center with more information about how to access and use the Individual Student Report.
    • Below is a screenshot of how the “Start over” link will show on the ISR. Some additional notes for teachers:
  • The Best Score will not reflect partial scores from activities where the “Start over” link was used
  • The Responses Report will include responses from activities where the “Start over” link was used
  • The count of attempts will include activities that were restarted
    • Please note that the count of attempts is expected to increase as a result of introducing the “Start over” link

✅ List of all activities that have the “Start over” link available:

  • Assigned and unassigned quizzes
  • Assigned and unassigned Unit Tests
  • Unassigned exercises
  • Assigned exercises that have the “Different question set for each student” setting (please see the below screenshot for an example of this)

🚫 Activities that do not have the “Start over” link available :

  • Mastery Challenges
  • Course Challenges
  • Assigned exercises, which have the “Same question set for all students” setting (please see the screenshot below for an example of this)

🔁 Bonus Questions as a Free Retry

If a learner gets one question wrong, a bonus question will appear at the end of the practice exercise set. If they answer it correctly, their previous mistake is erased, and they can still earn a “Proficient” score. Please note that bonus questions will not be available if a learner has incorrectly answered two or more questions.

For details on bonus questions, refer to the article: How do I earn “Proficient” on a practice exercise?

When clicked, the “Start over” link:

  • Returns the learner to the start of the activity they were working on.
  • Discards any potential mastery changes from that activity.
  • Retains the learning time acquired on the activity before clicking the “Start over” link. We truly appreciate the many students, parents, and teachers who wrote in over the years describing how a feature like this would benefit learners.

Below are some additional resources that may help:

  • Words from Khan Academy’s Learning Science team
  • How do I create assignments?
  • How do I use the Assignment Scores report?
  • Guide to Assignment teaching reports Questions? Reach out to our support team. Feedback? Share your thoughts in the Community Forum!

How do I download my students’ assignment scores and skills data into a CSV file?

If you are a teacher who uses Khan Academy in your classroom, you may want an easy way to download your students’ assignment scores and skills data. Luckily, Khan Academy offers three ways to download this data into a CSV that you can then use for further analysis and documentation.

In this article, we will cover the following topics:

  • What is a CSV?
  • How to download scores from multiple assignments into one CSV
To start off, though, let’s answer the question: “What is a CSV?”
  • A CSV, or Comma-Separated Values, is a type of file that stores data. It’s like a simple spreadsheet, but without the formulas and formatting.
  • You can then open CSV files in programs like Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or Numbers.
How to download the Assignment Scores Data into CSVs:

There are 3 ways on Khan Academy for you to download your students’ assignment data into a CSV.

  • Option 1 is in the “Reports” tab under “My Classes”. To download this CSV, follow the steps below:

  • Click “Download CSV” on the right-hand side of the screen

  • Select a date range. You’ll also have the option to include the average score for any practice activities (exercises, quizzes, and unit tests) in the selected date range.

  • Click Download CSV.

  1. You will see the pop-up window below on your screen, meaning our system is preparing the document for you. Please don’t exit the page until the download is completed and you receive the confirmation below:
  • Option 2 is how to download the CSV for an individual assignment from the Assignments tab.
  • On the Assignments tab, select the assignment you would like to view
  • Click download CSV
  • Or if you’re looking for a Unit Mission, click “Student Summary” and then “Download CSV”
  • Option 3 is to download the general class CSV from the Class settings page. Click “My Classes” and then “Class Settings”. Locate and click “Download CSV”.

Additional Resources:

  • Help Center Article: How do I create Assignments?
  • Help Center Article: How do I manage assignments?

How do I use Reports to view Activity, Skills, and Assignment score reports?

Khan Academy offers teachers insight to track their students’ work on both assigned and unassigned content through a variety of reports. This article will give you an in-depth guide to viewing and understanding the data some of them offer.

  1. Activity tab:

The Activity tab shows the students in a particular class, the total minutes they’ve spent learning, and how many skills they have worked on, leveled up on, and reached the Proficient Mastered level.

This interactive and customizable report allows teachers to drill into student work by many different metrics, including learning time, skill comprehension, and Mastery levels.

  1. Skills tab:

The Skills tab shows the different skills that are included in a Course, and what Mastery levels the students in your class are at for those particular skills.

Notable features of the Skills tab:

  • Customizable filters: select which Course, Unit, or Mastery Level you would like displayed.
  • “Only show assigned skills” check box: Select this if you want to only see the data about the content you have assigned to your students through a Unit Mission, or Assignment. Unselect this if you would like to see the student’s work from all of Khan Academy, whether you assigned it to them or not.
  • Click the skill name or the colored Mastery chart next to the skill name to see where your students fall in the Mastery level for that skill.
  • The “Expand all” and “Collapse all” links open and close all the skills in the unit, and can help save time navigating through the report.
  • The “View Exercise” link shows you a preview of what the exercise would be if you clicked the “Assign skill” button.
  • Click on a student’s name to be taken to their Individual Student Report with more information about how they have spent their time at Khan Academy.
  1. Assignments:

This report shows your students’ scores and completion information for the individual assignments they have been tasked with.

Teachers can filter by date, course, activity, and students.

You can click the Legend button to view what they mean.

You can also download the Assignment scores report as a CSV file; click Download CSV. We recommend also checking the article How do I download my students’ assignment scores and skills data into a CSV file for more details.

In the reimagined Khan Academy, Mastery-based practice is organized through Unit Missions rather than Course Mastery Goals. Unit Missions show student progress to teachers in smaller chunks, making it easier to spot specific gaps and see exactly where students need support. We recommend checking the article How do I replace Course Mastery Goals in the Khan Academy reimagined experience? to learn more about this update.

We hope this article was helpful for you to learn what student data exists on the Reports tab and to decide which resources work best for your teaching practice. For additional guidance or to share feedback, please reach out to our support team here! We are happy to help.

How do I use the Assignments report?

When you’ve assigned content to your students on the Khan Academy platform, you will be able to review their performance and completion information for those assignments on the Assignments Report. This article will cover how to find the report, how to navigate it, and what data is included.

Where is the Assignments Report located?

To access the Assignments Report, select a class from your teacher dashboard, then click the Reports option on the left-hand column menu.

What do the symbols at the top of the columns mean?

Above each assignment, you will notice different icons that represent different types of assigned work.

  • A triangle indicates a video was assigned
  • A piece of paper indicates that an article was assigned
  • A pencil represents either a practice exercise
  • A flag is a Unit Mission, whose completion is represented in a percentage(%)
  • A lightning bolt represents a Quiz
  • A book icon stands for a Course Challenge
  • A star is used to represent Unit Tests
  • A wand is a Khanmigo assignment (including Writing Coach) How is student data shown on the report?

Inside the assignment boxes, you will notice other symbols and colors to help you better understand your students’ performance and/or completion of assignments.

  • A dash without a box around it: The task has not yet been assigned to these students, and they cannot see it on their accounts.
  • A grey box with a dotted square inside it: The task has been assigned, but the student has not yet started the work.
  • A blue box with a half-full square inside it: The task has been assigned, and the student has started but not yet completed the work.
    • NOTE: Articles, videos, and Khanmigo assignments other than Writing Coach will only ever show as the dash (unassigned to the student), grey box (assigned but not completed), or a green check mark (completed). They will never show the blue “In Progress” box
  • A green checkmark indicates that your student completed a video or article assignment in its entirety.
    • If your student claims to have completed a video assignment, but the report does not show a green check, read this article for more information about why this might be happening. The colors that highlight students’ scores help you assess their performance at a glance. The percent listed in the box is your student’s best score on the assignment.
  • Green score box: Video or article was read to completion, or assignment score was 100
  • Yellow score box: Assignment score was between 60-99
  • Red score box: Assignment score was between 0-59

Some additional features of the Assignment report to highlight:

  • Date Range filter: customizable to see assignments from a particular time period.
  • Assignment Type filter: to see results by the type of assignment (e.g., quiz, unit test, exercise, etc.), making it easier to focus on specific activities.
  • Older (←) and Newer (→) arrows: Click these to navigate the list of assignments
  • Download CSV button: Click this if you would like to export your students’ assignment scores. Additional resource: How do I download my students’ assignment scores?
  • Hyperlinked Assignment title names: Click the hyperlink to be taken to the assignment’s Responses Report to see how your students answered the questions in this assignment.
  • Click a student’s name to be taken to their Individual Student Report. Here you can see all the work this student has done on Khan Academy. We hope this article was helpful for you to learn more about the Assignment report and how to find the student data you need on it. For additional guidance or to share feedback, please reach out to our support team here! We are happy to help.
